lines.gr: Μάνθανε δὴ, Μουσαῖε, θυηπολίην περισέμνην,
lines.en: Learn, Musaeus, the very august rite of burnt-offering,
lines.note: θυηπολίη denotes the conducting of sacrifice, often of burnt‑offerings; Musaeus is the traditional pupil of Orpheus.

lines.gr: εὐχήν, ἣ δή τοι προφερεστέρη ἐστὶν ἁπασέων.
lines.en: a prayer which indeed for you is the foremost of all.
lines.note: προφερεστέρη = “most preeminent, foremost.”

lines.gr: Ζεῦ βασιλεῦ, καὶ Γαῖα, καὶ οὐράνιαι φλόγες ἁγναὶ
lines.en: Zeus the king, and Gaia, and the holy heavenly flames
lines.note: “ouranian” = heavenly; the “flames of Hēlios” are his rays.

lines.gr: Ἠελίου, Μήνης θ’ ἱερὸν σέλας, Ἄστρα τε πάντα·
lines.en: of Hēlios, and the sacred radiance of Mēnē, and all the Stars;
lines.note: Mēnē is the Moon personified; “sacred radiance” (ἱερὸν σέλας) suits lunar light.

lines.gr: καὶ σύ, Ποσείδαον γαιήοχε κυανοχαῖτα,
lines.en: and you too, Poseidaon, earth-supporting, dark-maned,
lines.note: Poseidaon is an epic form of Poseidon; gaiēochos = “earth‑holding/supporting,” kyanochaitēs = “dark‑maned.”

lines.gr: Φερσεφόνη θ' ἁγνή, Δημήτηρ τ' ἀγλαόκαρπε,
lines.en: and holy Phersephonē, and Dēmētēr rich in fruit,
lines.note: Phersephonē is an epic form of Persephonē; Dēmētēr’s epithet ἀγλαόκαρπος = “rich in fruit.”

lines.gr: Ἄρτεμί τ' ἰοχέαιρα, κόρη, καὶ ἤιε Φοῖβε,
lines.en: and Artemis the arrow-showering, maiden, and gentle Phoibos,
lines.note: ἰοχέαιρα = “arrow‑pouring”; ἤιε = “gentle/kindly”; Phoibos here is Apollō.

lines.gr: ὃς Δελφῶν ναίεις ἱερὸν πέδον· ὅς τε μεγίστας
lines.en: who dwell in the holy plain of Delphoi; and you who have the greatest
lines.note: Delphoi’s “holy plain” (ἱερὸν πέδον) marks Apollō’s precinct.

lines.gr: τιμὰς ἐν μακάρεσσιν ἔχεις, Διόνυσε χορευτά·
lines.en: honors among the Blessed, Dionysos, lord of the dance;
lines.note: χορευτάς of Dionysos = “leader/lord of the dance,” suited to choral revelry.

lines.gr: Ἆρές τ' ὀμβριμόθυμε, καὶ Ἡφαίστου μένος ἁγνὸν,
lines.en: and Ares of stormy heart, and the holy might of Hēphaistos,
lines.note: ὀμβριμόθυμος = “storm‑hearted, impetuous”; “holy might” (Ἡφαίστου μένος ἁγνόν) evokes sacred fire.

lines.gr: ἀφρογενής τε θεά, μεγαλώνυμα δῶρα λαχοῦσα·
lines.en: and the foam-born goddess, possessor of high-renowned gifts;
lines.note: “foam‑born goddess” transparently indicates Aphroditē; μεγαλώνυμα δῶρα = “gifts of great renown.”

lines.gr: καὶ σύ, καταχθονίων βασιλεῦ, μέγ’ ὑπείροχε δαῖμον ·
lines.en: and you, king of those below, surpassing great daimon;
lines.note: “king of those below” = lord of the underworld (Aidēs/Ploutōn); δαῖμον here = a divine power, not “demon.”

lines.gr: Ἥβη τ’, Εἰλείθυια, καὶ Ἡρακλέος μένος ἠΰ·
lines.en: and Hēbē, Eileithyia, and the goodly might of Hēraklēs;
lines.note: Eileithyia is goddess of childbirth; “goodly might” (ἠϋ‑) of Hēraklēs is honorific.

lines.gr: καὶ τὸ Δικαιοσύνης τε καὶ Εὐσεβίης μέγ' ὄνειαρ
lines.en: and the great boon of Dikaiosynē and Eusebeia
lines.note: Dikaiosynē (Justice) and Eusebeia (Piety) are personified abstractions.

lines.gr: κικλήσκω, Νύμφας τε κλυτὰς, καὶ Πᾶνα μέγιστον,
lines.en: I invoke, and the famed Nymphs, and great Pan,

lines.gr: Ἥρην τ’, αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς θαλερὴν παράκοιτιν·
lines.en: and Hērā, the flourishing bedfellow of aegis-bearing Zeus;
lines.note: aigiokhoios is Zeus’ set epithet “aegis‑bearing”; παράκοιτις = “bedfellow, consort.”

lines.gr: Μνημοσύνην τ' ἐρατὴν, Μούσας τ' ἐπικέκλομαι ἁγνὰς
lines.en: and lovely Mnēmosynē, and I call upon the holy

lines.gr: ἐννέα καὶ Χάριτάς τε, καὶ Ὥρας, ἠδ' Ἐνιαυτὸν,
lines.en: nine Mousai, and the Kharites, and the Hōrai, and Eniautos,
lines.note: Hōrai (Seasons) and Eniautos (the Year) are temporal personifications.

lines.gr: Λητώ τ’ εὐπλόκαμον θείην σεμνήν τε Διώνην,
lines.en: and Lētō of the fair tresses, divine, and august Diōnē,
lines.note: Diōnē is a venerable goddess, sometimes a mother of Aphroditē.

lines.gr: Κουρ ῆτάς τ' ἐνόπλους Κορύβαντάς τ’, ἠδὲ Καβείρους,
lines.en: and the armed Kourētēs, and the Korybantes, and the Kabeiroi,
lines.note: Kourētēs, Korybantes, Kabeiroi: armed/dancing attendants of the Mother and mystery‑deities.

lines.gr: καὶ μεγάλους Σωτῆρας ὁμοῦ, Δι ὸς ἄφθιτα τέκνα·
lines.en: and together the great Sōtēres, the imperishable children of Zeus;
lines.note: Sōtēres likely the Dioskouroi (“Saviors”), called imperishable children of Zeus.

lines.gr: Ἰδαίους τε θεοὺς, ἠδ’ ἄ γγελον Οὐρανιώνων,
lines.en: and the Idaian gods, and the messenger of the Ouranians,
lines.note: The “Idaian gods” are Cretan (linked to Mount Ida); “messenger of the Ouranians” anticipates Hermēs.

lines.gr: Ἑρμείαν κήρυκα, Θέμιν θ’, ἱεροσκόπον ἀνδρ ῶν,
lines.en: Hermēs the herald, and Themis, overseer of sacred rites among men,
lines.note: ἱεροσκόπος of Themis = “overseer/interpreter of sacred matters” among humans.

lines.gr: Νύκτα τε πρεσβίστην καλέω, καὶ φωσφόρον Ἦμαρ,
lines.en: and Night the eldest I call, and light-bringing Day,
lines.note: Nyx is called “eldest”; Day (Ἦμαρ) is “light‑bringing.”

lines.gr: Πίστιν τ’, ἠδὲ Δίκην, καὶ ἀμύμονα Θεσμοδότειραν·
lines.en: and Pistis, and Dikē, and the blameless Law‑giving Lady;
lines.note: Pistis = Trust/Good Faith; “blameless Law‑giving Lady” (Θεσμοδότειρα) may allude to Themis or Demeter as lawgiver.

lines.gr: Ῥείαν τ’, ἠδὲ Κρόνον, καὶ Τηθ ὺν κυανόπεπλον,
lines.en: and Rheia, and Kronos, and Tēthys of the dark veil,
lines.note: κυανόπεπλος = “dark‑veiled,” a marine epithet of Tēthys; Rheia = Rhea.

lines.gr: Ὠκεανόν τε μέγαν, σύν τ
lines.en: and great Ōkeanos, together
lines.note: Lines 27–28 form one syntactic unit: Ōkeanos with his daughters (the Oceanids).

lines.gr: ’ Ὠκεανοῖο θύγατρας
lines.en: with the daughters of Ōkeanos,

lines.gr: Ἄτλαντός τε καὶ Αἰῶνος μέγ’ ὑπείροχον ἰσχύν·
lines.en: and the far‑superior strength of Atlas and Aiōn,
lines.note: Aiōn (Eternity, cyclical time) differs from Chronos (line 30), often linear/temporal succession.

lines.gr: καὶ Χρόνον ἀέναον, καὶ τὸ Στυγὸς ἀγλαὸν ὕδωρ,
lines.en: and Chronos ever‑flowing, and the splendid water of Styx,
lines.note: Chronos “ever‑flowing” contrasts with Aiōn; Styx’s waters are the most solemn oath for gods.

lines.gr: Μειλιχίους τε θεούς· ἀγαθήν τ’ ἐπὶ τοῖσι Πρόνοιαν·
lines.en: and the Meilichioi gods, and, over these, Good Pronoia,
lines.note: Meilichioi (“Gracious/Placatory”) are often euphemistic cthonic powers; Pronoia = Providence.

lines.gr: Δαίμονά τ’ ἠγάθεον, καὶ Δαίμονα πήμονα θνητῶν·
lines.en: and the kindly Daimōn and the baneful Daimōn of mortals,
lines.note: Daimōn = neutral “divine agency”; here benevolent vs. baneful toward mortals.

lines.gr: Δαίμονας οὐρανίους τε καὶ εἰναλίους καὶ ἐνύδρους,
lines.en: the heavenly and sea‑dwelling and water‑haunting daimones,

lines.gr: καὶ χθονίους καὶ ὑποχθονίους, ἠδ’ ἠεριφοίτους·,
lines.en: and the chthonian and under‑chthonian, and those who roam the air,
lines.note: ἠεριφοίτους = “air‑roaming,” of aerial spirits.

lines.gr: καὶ Σεμέλην, Βάκχου τε συνευαστῆρας ἅπαντας,
lines.en: and Semelē, and all the fellow‑banqueters of Bakchos,
lines.note: “fellow‑banqueters of Bakchos” = Bacchic companions/initiates (thiasoi).

lines.gr: Ἰνὼ Λευκοθέην τε, Παλαίμονά τ’ ὀλβιοδώτην.
lines.en: and Inō Leukothēa, and Palaimōn, giver of bliss.
lines.note: Inō deified as Leukothea; Palaimōn (Melikertes) a sea‑helper god.

lines.gr: [Νίκην θ’ ἡ δυέπειαν, ἰδ’ Ἀδρήστειαν ἄνασσαν·
lines.en: [and Nikē, the sweet‑speaking one, and Queen Adrēsteia,
lines.note: Bracketed lines are textually uncertain; ἡ δυέπειαν is likely corrupt, often emended to ἡδυεπῆ (“sweet‑speaking”); some witnesses omit these lines.

lines.gr: καὶ βασιλῆα μέγαν Ἀσκληπιὸν ἠπιοδώτην.]
lines.en: and great king Asklēpios, gentle in giving aid.]
lines.note: Asklēpios’ epithet ἠπιοδώτης = “gentle in giving aid.”

lines.gr: Παλλάδα τ’ ἐγρεμάχην κούρην, Ἀνέμους τε πρόπαντας,
lines.en: and Pallas, the battle‑awakening maiden, and all the Winds,
lines.note: ἐγρεμάχη = “battle‑awakening,” a martial epithet of Pallas (Athena).

lines.gr: καὶ Βροντὰς, Κόσμου τε μέρη τετρακίονος αὐδῶ·
lines.en: and the Thunders, and I proclaim the fourfold parts of the Cosmos,
lines.note: “fourfold parts of the Cosmos” may denote the quarters of the world or elemental tetrad.

lines.gr: Μητέρα τ’ ἀθανάτων, Ἄττιν καὶ Μῆνα κικλήσκω,
lines.en: and I call the Mother of the immortals, and Attis and Mēn,
lines.note: “Mother of the immortals” is the Mother of the Gods (Meter Theōn, Cybele/Rhea); Attis and Mēn are her Phrygian associates.

lines.gr: Οὐρανίην τε θεάν, σύν δ’ ἄμβροτον ἁγνὸν Ἄδωνιν,
lines.en: and the Ouranian goddess, together with immortal, holy Adōnis,
lines.note: “Ouranian goddess” likely Aphroditē Ourania; Adōnis is the beloved youth of her cult.

lines.gr: Ἀρχήν τ’ ἠδὲ Πέρας · (τὸ γὰρ ἔπλετο πᾶσι μέγιστον)
lines.en: and both Archē and Peras (for this is greatest for all),
lines.note: Archē and Peras (Beginning and End) are Orphic metaphysical principles, invoked as deities.

lines.gr: ἐλθεῖν εὐμενέας, κεχαρημένον ἦτορ ἔχοντας,
lines.en: to come gracious, possessing a gladdened heart,

lines.gr: τήνδε θυηπολίην ἱερὴν, σπονδήν τ' ἐπὶ σεμνήν.
lines.en: to this holy rite of burnt‑offering, and to the august libation.

lines.gr: Εἰνοδίην Ἑκάτην κλῄιζω, τριοδῖτιν, ἐραννήν,
lines.en: I invoke Hekate Einodia, of the three-way crossroads, lovely,
lines.note: Einodia (“of/along the roads”) and Trioditis (“of the three-way [crossroads]”) are traditional epithets of Hekate as a liminal road-goddess; I retain Einodia to preserve the cult title.

lines.gr: οὐρανίην, χθονίαν τε, καὶ εἰναλίην κροκόπεπλον,
lines.en: heavenly, chthonian, and seaborne, saffron-robed,
lines.note: Einalia = “of the sea”; krokopeplos (“saffron-robed”) evokes the saffron-dyed garments associated with goddesses in ritual contexts.

lines.gr: τυμβιδίην, ψυχαῖς νεκύων μέτα βακχεύουσαν,
lines.en: of the tombs, reveling Bacchically among the souls of the dead,
lines.note: Tymbidia = “of the tombs”; baccheuousan (“reveling in Bacchic frenzy”) aligns Hekate with Dionysiac rites in the underworld, reveling “among the souls of the dead” (psychais nekyōn).

lines.gr: Πέρσειαν, φιλέρημον, ἀγαλλομένην ἐλάφοισιν,
lines.en: Perseia, fond of solitude, exulting in deer,
lines.note: Perseia is a patronymic (“daughter of Perses”) known from Hesiod; “exulting in deer” (agallomenēn elaphoisin) recalls Artemis’ venatic sphere, here applied to Hekate.

lines.gr: νυκτερίην, σκυλακῖτιν, ἀμαιμάκετον βασίλειαν,
lines.en: nocturnal, of the whelps, the unconquerable queen,
lines.note: Skylakitin literally “associated with whelps/puppies,” marking her canine retinue; I render it idiomatically while noting the etymology. Amaimaketos = “unconquerable/irresistible.”

lines.gr: ταυροπόλον, παντὸς κόσμου κληιδοῦχον ἄνασσαν,
lines.en: Bull-driving, key-bearing queen of the whole cosmos,
lines.note: Tauropolos/Tauropolon is debated (“bull-driving,” “bull-slayer,” or “bull-worshipped”); I choose “bull-driving.” Kleidouchos (“key-bearer”) is a cult title, here magnified as “of the whole cosmos.”

lines.gr: ἡγεμόνην, νύμφην, κουροτρόφον, οὐρεσιφοῖτιν,
lines.en: guide, nymph, nurse of youths, mountain-roving,
lines.note: Nymphē can mean “nymph/maiden” rather than “bride” here; kourotrophos is a technical epithet for a deity who nurtures the young; ouresiphōitin = “mountain-roving.”

lines.gr: λισσομένοις κούρην τελεταῖς ὁσίαισι παρεῖναι
lines.en: being implored, Maiden, be present at holy rites for the suppliants,
lines.note: Lissomenois is a dative of advantage (“for the suppliants”); teletai hosiai are “holy rites/initiations,” and pareinai (inf.) is the standard hymnic request “to be present/attend.”

lines.gr: βουκόλῳ εὐμενέουσαν ἀεὶ κεχαρηότι θυμῷ.
lines.en: ever gracious to the herdsman, with a gladdened heart.
lines.note: Boukolos (“herdsman/cowherd”) likely voices the singer’s persona (Orphic/poetic shepherd); kecharēōti thymō(i) is a formulaic “with a gladdened heart,” here marking favorable divine disposition.

lines.gr: Κλῦθί μοι, ὦ πολύσεμνε θεά, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον,
lines.en: Hear me, O most-august goddess, much-named daimon,
lines.note: daimon here means a divine power or numen, not a malevolent “demon”; πολύσεμνος = “most-august,” πολυώνυμος = “much-named, of many epithets.”

lines.gr: ὠδίνων ἐπαρωγέ, λεχῶν ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι·
lines.en: helper in birth-pangs, sweet in aspect to women in childbed;
lines.note: λεχώς (gen. λεχῶν) denotes a woman in childbed; ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι = “sweet to the sight,” i.e., pleasing in appearance/presence to those in labor.

lines.gr: θηλειῶν σώτειρα, μόνη φιλόπαις, ἀγανόφρον,
lines.en: savior of women, sole child-loving one, gentle of mind,
lines.note: θῆλυ = “female, woman”; μόνη φιλόπαις = “sole child-loving,” highlighting exclusive concern for infants/children; ἀγανόφρων = “gentle-minded.”

lines.gr: ὠκυλόχεια, ἐπαρώγ’ ἀνίαις θνητῶν, Προθυραία.
lines.en: swift-delivering, a helper amid mortals’ pains, Prothyraia.
lines.note: ὠκυλόχεια = “swift in delivery/bringing quick birth”; Προθυραία (“Before-the-door”) is a childbirth epithet linked to the threshold of the birthing-room.

lines.gr: κλειδοῦχ’, εὐάντητε, φιλότροφε, πᾶσι προσηνής,
lines.en: key-bearing, propitious to meet, fond of nurture, gracious to all,
lines.note: κλειδοῦχος = “key-bearing,” a marker of custodial/threshold authority; εὐάντητος = “of auspicious meeting, propitious to encounter”; φιλότροφος = “fond of nurture/rearing.”

lines.gr: ἣ κατέχεις οἴκους πάντων, θαλίαις τε γέγηθας,
lines.en: you who hold the households of all, and you rejoice in banquets,
lines.note: θαλίαι can denote feasts generally and often wedding- or household-celebrations, fitting the domestic/ritual context.

lines.gr: λυσίζων’, ἀφανής, ἔργοισι δὲ φαίνῃ ἅπασιν,
lines.en: girdle-loosener, unseen, yet in your works you appear to all,
lines.note: λυσιζών’ = “loosener of the girdle (zōnē),” a conventional epithet in contexts of marriage and childbirth; ἀφανής/φαίνῃ contrasts the goddess’s invisibility with her manifest effects.

lines.gr: συμπάσχεις ὠδῖσι καὶ εὐτοκί ῃσι γέγηθας,
lines.en: you share in the birth-pangs and you rejoice in easy deliveries,
lines.note: συμπάσχειν = “to suffer with,” implying sympathetic presence; εὐτοκία = “easy/successful delivery.”

lines.gr: Εἰλείθυια, λύουσα πόνους δειναῖς ἐν ἀνάγκαις.
lines.en: Eileithyia, loosening pains amid dreadful constraints.
lines.note: δειναὶ ἀνάγκαι = “dread constraints/necessities,” a formula for the extremity of labor; λύειν πόνους = “to loosen/relieve pains.”

lines.gr: μούνην γάρ σ ὲ καλοῦσι λεχοί, ψυχ ῆς ἀνάπαυμα.
lines.en: for women in childbed call upon you alone, the soul’s repose.
lines.note: ψυχῆς ἀνάπαυμα = “repose/relief of the soul,” i.e., mental solace for those in childbed.

lines.gr: ἐν γάρ σοὶ τοκετῶν λαθιπήμονές εἰσιν ἀνίαι.
lines.en: for in you the sorrows of childbirth are made to be forgotten.
lines.note: λαθιπήμονες (“forgetful-of-suffering”) is a rare compound: the pains become such as to be forgotten—i.e., are made forgettable through the goddess’s aid.

lines.gr: Ἄρτεμις Εἰλείθυια, καὶ
lines.en: Artemis Eileithyia, and
lines.note: The hymn identifies Artemis with Eileithyia, reflecting overlapping roles in childbirth cult.

lines.gr: εὐσέμνη Προθυραία.
lines.en: revered Prothyraia,
lines.note: εὐσέμνη = “revered, august”; Προθυραία reiterates the threshold epithet associated with childbirth rites.

lines.gr: κλῦθι, μάκαιρα· δίδου δὲ γονάς, ἐπαρωγὸς ἐοῦσα
lines.en: hear, blessed one; grant births, being present as a helper,
lines.note: γόνας can mean “births” or “offspring”; in prayer context, “grant births” = grant successful delivery; ἐπαρωγός = “helper, aid.”

lines.gr: καὶ σῶζε, ὥσπερ ἔφυς αἰεὶ σώτειρα προπάντων.
lines.en: and save, as you are by nature ever the savior before all.
lines.note: προπάντων can mean “before all others” (preeminent) or “on behalf of all”; “savior before all” preserves the elevated, preeminent sense.

lines.gr: Νύκτα θεῶν γενέτειραν ἀείσομαι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρ ῶν.
lines.en: I shall sing of Nyx, begetress of gods and of men.

lines.gr: [Νὺξ γένεσις πάντων, ἣν καὶ Κύπριν καλέσωμεν]
lines.en: Nyx, genesis of all things, whom we will also call Kypris.
lines.note: Bracketed line: many editors mark it as interpolated. “Kypris” is Aphrodite; the identification of Nyx with the universal generative principle is Orphic in tone but textually suspect.

lines.gr: κλῦθι, μάκαιρα θεά, κυαναυγής, ἀστεροφεγγής·
lines.en: Hear, blessed goddess, dark-blue-gleaming, star-bright;

lines.gr: ἡσυχί ῃ χαίρουσα καὶ ἠ ρεμί ῃ πολυύπνῳ·
lines.en: rejoicing in quiet and in stillness rich in sleep;
lines.note: “πολυύπνῳ” = “rich in sleep.” The line emphasizes Nyx’s quiet and soporific stillness.

lines.gr: εὐφροσύνη, τερπνή, φιλοπάννυχε, μῆτερ ὀνείρων·
lines.en: mirthful, delightful, lover of all-night vigils, mother of dreams;
lines.note: “φιλοπάννυχε” literally “fond of all-night (vigils/festivals),” alluding to the ritual παννυχίς; hence “lover of all-night vigils.”

lines.gr: ληθομέριμν’, ἀγαθήν τε πόνων ἀνάπαυσιν ἔχουσα ·
lines.en: care-forgetting, possessing a good respite from toils;
lines.note: “ληθομέριμν’” can mean “forgetting cares” or “causing forgetfulness of cares”; the translation reflects the latter nuance. “ἀνάπαυσις” = “respite/repose.”

lines.gr: ὑπνοδότειρα, φίλη πάντων, ἐλάσιππε, νυχαυγής·
lines.en: giver of sleep, beloved of all, chariot-driving, night-luminous;
lines.note: “ἐλάσιππε” = “driver of horses,” i.e., of a night-chariot. “νυχαυγής” = “shining by night.”

lines.gr: ἡμιτελής, χθονίη, ἠδ’ οὐρανίη πάλιν α ὐτή·
lines.en: half-complete, chthonian, and again the same, heavenly;
lines.note: “ἡμιτελής” (“half-complete”) is commonly taken of Night as half the cycle of time. “πάλιν αὐτή” is textually awkward; here understood as “and again the same, heavenly,” i.e., both chthonian and celestial.

lines.gr: ἐγκυκλίη, παίκτειρα διώγμασιν ἠεροφοίτοις·
lines.en: all-encircling, sporting in the chases of those who wander in mist;
lines.note: “ἐγκυκλίη” = “all-encircling” (of the cosmic circuit). “παίκτειρα διώγμασιν ἠεροφοίτοις” is obscure: “sporting in the chases of those who wander in mist,” i.e., amid nocturnal, mist-roaming pursuits (perhaps of spirits or creatures).

lines.gr: ἣ φάος ἐκπέμπεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα, καὶ πάλι φεύγεις
lines.en: who send forth light beneath to the nether regions, and again you flee
lines.note: “ὑπὸ νέρτερα” with ὑπό + acc is difficult: likely “beneath, to the nether regions.” Some take it “from beneath the lower world.” The sending of “light” may refer to moon/starlight seen from below or to a cosmological cycle.

lines.gr: εἰς Ἀΐδην. δειν ὴ γὰρ ἀνάγκη πάντα κρατύνει.
lines.en: into Hades; for dread Anankê prevails over all.
lines.note: “Anankê” (Necessity) personified; “κρατύνει” = “prevails over/rules.”

lines.gr: νῦν δὲ, μάκαιρ’ ὦ Ν ὺξ πολυόλβιε, πᾶσι ποθεινή,
lines.en: But now, O blessed Nyx, much-wealthy, longed-for by all,

lines.gr: εὐάντητε, κλύουσα λόγων ἱκετηρίδα φωνὴν,
lines.en: gracious in meeting, hearing the suppliant voice of my words,
lines.note: “εὐάντητε” is a rare vocative/adjectival form, “gracious in meeting/approach.” “λόγων ἱκετηρίδα φωνήν” = “the suppliant voice of my words.”

lines.gr: ἔλθοις εὐμενέουσα, φόβους δ’ ἀπόπεμπε νυχαυγεῖς.
lines.en: come benevolent, and send away the night-gleaming fears.
lines.note: “νυχαυγεῖς φόβους” = “night-gleaming fears,” i.e., terrors/phantoms that arise or seem to gleam in the night.

lines.gr: Οὐρανὲ παγγενέτωρ, κόσμου μέρος αἰὲν ἀτειρές,
lines.en: Ouranos, all-begetter, the ever-unwearied portion of the cosmos,
lines.note: κόσμου μέρος αἰὲν ἀτειρές: μέρος presents Ouranos as the upper “portion” of the ordered world; ἀτειρές = “unwearied, unworn.”

lines.gr: πρεσβυγένεθλ’, ἀρχ ὴ πάντων, πάντων τε τελευτή,
lines.en: ancient-born, the beginning of all things and the end of all,
lines.note: πρεσβυγένεθλ’ is a contracted vocative, “ancient-born,” i.e., born before all. ἀρχὴ … τελευτή balances “beginning/end” as cosmological first principle and telos.

lines.gr: κοσμοκράτωρ, σφαιρηδὸν ἑλισσόμενος περὶ γαῖαν,
lines.en: world-ruler, rolling like a sphere around the earth,
lines.note: σφαιρηδόν is an adverb, “in spherical fashion,” evoking the rotation of the celestial sphere about the earth.

lines.gr: οἶκε θεῶν μακάρων, ῥόμβου δίνῃσιν ὁδεύων,
lines.en: house of the blessed gods, moving along in the vortices of the whirling rhombos,
lines.note: ῥόμβος is the whirring “rhombos” (bull‑roarer/spinning disc) and here symbolizes cosmic rotation; δίναι are its eddies/vortices.

lines.gr: οὐράνιος χθόνιός τε φύλαξ πάντων περιβληθείς·
lines.en: both heavenly and chthonian, guardian of all, enfolding them round about,
lines.note: οὐράνιος χθόνιός τε pairs seemingly opposed realms; Ouranos is imagined as encompassing above and below. περιβληθείς literally “clothed about, enfolding.”

lines.gr: ἐν στέρνοισιν ἔχων φύσεως ἄπλητον ἀνάγκην,
lines.en: holding within your breast the boundless Necessity of Nature,
lines.note: φύσεως ἄπλητον ἀνάγκην: ἀνάγκη (“necessity”) may hint at the Orphic cosmic Necessity; ἄπλητος = “boundless, unsated.”

lines.gr: κυανόχρως, ἀδάμαστε, παναίολος, αἰολόμορφε,
lines.en: dark-blue in hue, indomitable, all-variegated, changeful of form,
lines.note: κυανόχρως = “dark‑blue/azure‑hued”; παναίολος = “all‑variegated, dappled”; αἰολόμορφος = “changeful in form.”

lines.gr: πανδερκές, Κρονότεκνε, μάκαρ, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον,
lines.en: all-seeing, child of Kronos, blessed, most-exalted daimon,
lines.note: Κρονότεκνε literally “child of Kronos”; in Orphic contexts Kronos can also stand for Chronos (Time). δαῖμον denotes a divine power, not a malign “demon.”

lines.gr: κλῦθ’ ἐπάγων ζωὴν ὁσίην μύστῃ νεοφάντῃ.
lines.en: hear, and bring holy life to the newly revealed mystes.
lines.note: νεοφάντῃ (“newly‑manifest”) modifies μύστῃ (“initiate”); the closing prayer asks the god to grant a holy/pious life to the neophyte.

lines.gr: Ὦ Διὸς ὑψιμέλαθρον ἔχων κράτος αἰὲν ἀτειρές,
lines.en: O you who hold the ever-unwearied might of Zeus of the lofty halls,
lines.note: ὑψιμέλαθρον (“of lofty halls”): an epithet associated with Zeus; the syntax allows a transferred epithet to κράτος; αἰὲν ἀτειρές = “ever indomitable/unyielding.”

lines.gr: ἄστρων ἠελίου τε σεληναίης τε μέρισμα,
lines.en: the portion allotted to the stars, to Helios, and to Selene,
lines.note: μέρισμα = “allotment/portion,” here the cosmic region assigned to heavenly bodies; Helios and Selene are preserved as theonyms.

lines.gr: πανδαμάτωρ, πυρίπνους, πᾶσιν ζῳοῖσιν ἔναυσμα,
lines.en: all-subduer, fire-breathing, the spark for all living beings,
lines.note: πανδαμάτωρ = “all-subduer/all-tamer” (epic); πυρίπνους = “fire-breathing/fiery-breathing”; ἔναυσμα = “kindling/spark,” source of vital ignition for life.

lines.gr: ὑψιφανὴς Αἰθήρ, κόσμου στοιχεῖον ἄριστον
lines.en: high-shining Aither, the best element of the cosmos,
lines.note: ὑψιφανής = “high-shining”; στοιχεῖον = “element” in later/technical sense; ἄριστον = “best/noblest,” asserting Aither’s primacy among elements.
The mid-dot (·) marks a major pause/colon in the Greek; no lexical content to translate.

lines.gr: ἀγλαὸν ὦ βλάστημα, σελασφόρον, ἀστεροφεγγές,
lines.en: O splendid offspring, bearer of brilliance, star-gleaming,
lines.note: βλάστημα literally “shoot/sprout,” here “offspring” in a cosmic-genealogical sense; σελασφόρον = “brightness-bearing”; ἀστεροφεγγές = “star-shining.”

lines.gr: κικλήσκων λίτομαί σε, κεκραμένον εὔδιον εἶναι.
lines.en: calling upon you I beseech that you be well-tempered and serene.
lines.note: κικλήσκων = “calling upon”; κεκραμένον (from κεράννυμι) = “well-mixed/tempered,” often of air; εὔδιον = “fair-weather/serene.” The prayer asks for benevolent, calm conditions.

lines.gr: Πρωτογόνον καλέω διφυῆ, μέγαν, αἰθερόπλαγκτον,
lines.en: Protogonos I call, two‑natured, great, aether‑wandering,
lines.note: “two‑natured” (διφυής) in Orphic context suggests androgyny; “aether‑wandering” renders αἰθερόπλαγκτος.

lines.gr: ὠογενῆ, χρυσέησιν ἀγαλλόμενον πτερύγεσσιν,
lines.en: egg‑born, exulting in golden pinions,
lines.note: “egg‑born” (ὠογενής) alludes to the cosmic egg; “golden pinions” are traditional attributes of Phanês.

lines.gr: ταυρωπόν, γένεσιν μακάρων θνητῶν τ’ ἀνθρώπων ·
lines.en: bull‑eyed, the origin of the blessed and of mortal men;
lines.note: “bull‑eyed” (ταυρωπός) is a traditional divine epithet; γένεσις here = “origin/source.”

lines.gr: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον, πολυόργιον, Ἠρικεπαῖον,
lines.en: the seed much‑remembered, rich in orgia, Erikepaios,
lines.note: πολύμνηστον = “much‑remembered/famed”; πολυόργιον = “rich in orgia (secret rites)”; Ἠρικεπαῖος (Erikepaios) is an obscure Orphic epithet/name retained by transliteration.

lines.gr: ἄρρητον, κρύφιον. ῥοιζήτορα, παμφαὲς ἔρνος ·
lines.en: unspeakable, hidden, whirring‑sounding, all‑shining shoot,
lines.note: ῥοιζήτορα conveys a rushing/whirring sound; ἔρνος = “shoot, scion,” of cosmic generation.

lines.gr: ὄσσων ὃς σκοτόεσσαν ἀπημαύρωσας ὁμίχλην,
lines.en: who by your eyes dispelled the murky mist of darkness,
lines.note: ὄσσων (genitive plural “of eyes”) functions instrumentally: “by your eyes”; ἀπημαύρωσας = “you dispelled/banished.”

lines.gr: πάντῃ δινηθεὶς πτερύγων ῥιπαῖς κατὰ κόσμον ·
lines.en: whirled everywhere by the gusts of your wings through the ordered world,
lines.note: δινηθείς = “eddying/whirled”; κατὰ κόσμον can mean “through the cosmos” or “in due order.”

lines.gr: λαμπρὸ ν ἄγων φάος ἁγνόν, ἀφ’ οὗ σε Φάνητα κικλήσκω,
lines.en: bringing bright, holy light, whence I invoke you as Phanês,
lines.note: Φάνητα (Phanês) from φαίνω, “to bring to light”; the name emphasizes his role as revealer of light.

lines.gr: ἠδὲ Πρίηπον ἄνακτα, καὶ Ἀνταύγην ἑλίκωπον.
lines.en: and as lord Priêpos, and as Antaugê of the circling gaze.
lines.note: Πρίηπος (Priêpos) is the Orphic form of Priapos; Ἀνταύγη (Antaugê, “Reflected‑Gleam”) is a by‑name of Phanês; ἑλίκωπος = “with circling/rolling gaze.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πολύμητι, πολύσπορε, βαῖνε γεγηθὼς
lines.en: But come, blessed one, of much counsel, rich in seed, step rejoicing
lines.note: πολύμητις = “of much counsel, resourceful”; πολύσπορος = “rich in seed, much‑sowing”; βαῖνε is the hymnic “come/step.”

lines.gr: ἐς τελετ ὴν ἁγίην πολυποίκιλον ὀργιοφάνταις.
lines.en: into the holy, many‑patterned rite for the revealers of the orgia.
lines.note: τελετή = initiation‑rite; πολυποίκιλος = “many‑patterned/variegated”; ὀργιοφάνταις = “to the revealers of the orgia (mysteries).”

lines.gr: Ἄστρων οὐρανίων ἱερὸν σέλας ἐκπροκαλο ῦμαι,
lines.en: I summon forth the sacred radiance of the heavenly stars,
lines.note: ἐκπροκαλοῦμαι intensifies the invocation (“call forth”); σέλας = “radiance” of the stars. The spacing in ἐκπροκαλοῦμαι in the source is typographical.

lines.gr: εὐιέραις φωνῇ σι κικλήσκων δαίμονας ἁγνούς.
lines.en: calling upon pure daimones with holy-sacrificial voices,
lines.note: εὐιέραις (“of good sacrifice,” hence “holy”) marks ritual diction; φωνῇσι is epic dative plural. Δαίμονες here means “divine powers,” not “demons.” The spacing in “σι κικλήσκων” is typographical.

lines.gr: Ἀστέρες οὐράνιοι, Νυκτὸς φίλα τέκνα μελαίνης,
lines.en: Heavenly Stars, dear children of black Nyx,
lines.note: Nyx is the goddess of Night; μελαίνη (“black”) is a conventional cultic epithet.

lines.gr: ἐγκυκλίοις δίν ῃσι περιθρόνιοι κυκλέοντες.
lines.en: enthroned round about, wheeling in encircling eddies,
lines.note: περιθρόνιοι (“around the throne”) likely refers to encircling the celestial pole or divine throne; ἐγκυκλίοις δίναισι (“in encircling vortices”) evokes cosmic rotation. The spacing in δίναισι is typographical.

lines.gr: ἀνταυγε ῖς, πυρόεντες, ἀεὶ γενετ ῆρες ἁπάντων·
lines.en: gleaming back, fiery, ever the begetters of all things;
lines.note: ἀνταυγεῖς can suggest “gleaming back” (often of reflected light); γενετῆρες (“begetters”) points to the stars’ generative/cosmic influence. Spacing in ἀνταυγεῖς and γενετῆρες is typographical.

lines.gr: μοιρίδιοι, πάσης μοίρης σημάντορες ὄντες ·
lines.en: fate-dealing, being indicators of every allotment;
lines.note: μοιρίδιοι (“belonging to Moira,” hence “fate-dealing”); σημάντορες (“indicators, sign-givers”) presents the stars as signs of destiny (astrological nuance).

lines.gr: θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων θείην διέποντες ἀταρπόν ·
lines.en: guiding the divine path of mortal men;
lines.note: θείην ἀταρπόν (“divine path”) can denote both destiny and the navigational/astrological course governed by the stars.

lines.gr: ἑπταφαε ῖς ζώνας ἐφορώμενοι, ἠερόπλαγκτοι·
lines.en: wearing seven-lumined zones, wandering through the mist;
lines.note: ἑπταφαεῖς ζώνας (“seven-lumined zones”) probably the seven planetary circles or belts of the sky; ἠερόπλαγκτοι = “wandering through the mist.”

lines.gr: οὐράνιοι χθόνιοί τε, πυρίδρομοι, αἰὲν ἀτειρε ῖς
lines.en: both heavenly and chthonian, fire-running, ever-unwearied,
lines.note: οὐράνιοι χθόνιοί τε (“both heavenly and chthonian”) because they rise and set; πυρίδρομοι = “fire-running”; ἀτειρεῖς = “unwearied/unyielding.” Spacing in ἀτειρεῖς is typographical.

lines.gr: αὐγάξοντες ἀεὶ νυκτὸς ζοφοειδέα πέπλον,
lines.en: ever lighting up Night’s gloom-like veil,
lines.note: ζοφοειδές πέπλον (“gloom-like veil”) is a standard image for Night; αὐγάξοντες = “giving light, illuminating.”

lines.gr: μαρμαρυγαῖς στίλβοντες, ἐΰφρονες ἐννύχιοί τε ·
lines.en: shining with sparkles, kindly and nocturnal;
lines.note: μαρμαρυγαί = “sparkles, flickers”; ἐύφρονες (“kindly, benevolent”); ἐννύχιοι (“of the night, nocturnal”).

lines.gr: ἔλθετ’ ἐπ’ εὐιέρου τελετῆς πολυΐστορας ἄθλους,
lines.en: come to the well-hallowed rite, to its much-instructive labors,
lines.note: πολυΐστορας ἄθλους is difficult: either “much-instructive labors” of the rite or “widely-witnessed toils.” The translation adopts the former; many take πολυΐστορας as modifying ἄθλους.

lines.gr: ἐσθλο ὶ ἐπ’ εὐδόξοις ἔργοις δρόμον ἐκτελέοντες.
lines.en: noble, completing your course for illustrious works.
lines.note: δρόμον ἐκτελέοντες (“completing your course”) suits celestial motion; ἐπ’ εὐδόξοις ἔργοις (“for illustrious works”) likely refers to the honored outcomes of the rite.

lines.gr: Κλῦθι μάκαρ, πανδερκὲς ἔχων αἰώνιον ὄμμα,
lines.en: Hear, blessed one, having the all-seeing, eternal eye,
lines.note: πανδερκής literally “all-seeing”; αἰώνιον ὄμμα “eternal eye” is a standard solar epithet.

lines.gr: Τιτ ὰν χρυσαυγής, ὑπερίων , οὐράνιον φῶς·
lines.en: Titan of golden brightness, Hyperiōn, celestial light,
lines.note: Read Τιτάν χρυσαυγής, Ὑπερίων; Hyperiōn is a solar theonym; χρυσαυγής = “golden-rayed/bright.”

lines.gr: αὐτοφυής, ἀκάμας, ζώων ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι·
lines.en: self-born, untiring, the sweet countenance of living beings,
lines.note: αὐτοφυής “self-generated,” ἀκάμας “untiring”; πρόσοψις here “aspect/face,” hence “sweet to the sight of living beings.”

lines.gr: δεξι ὲ μὲν γενέτωρ ἠοῦς, εὐώνυμε νυκτός·
lines.en: right-hand begetter of Dawn, left-hand of Night,
lines.note: εὐώνυμος is the euphemistic “left(-handed)”; the line marks the Sun’s position relative to Dawn and Night.

lines.gr: κρᾶσιν ἔχων ὡρῶν, τετραβάμοσι ποσσὶ χορεύων.
lines.en: holding the mingling of the seasons, dancing with four-stepping feet,
lines.note: κρᾶσις ὡρῶν = “mixing of seasons”; “four-stepping feet” alludes to the four seasons.

lines.gr: εὔδρομε, ῥοιζήτωρ, πυρόεις, φαιδρωπέ, διφρευτά,
lines.en: swift-running, whirring, fiery, bright-faced, charioteer,
lines.note: ῥοιζητήρ/ῥοιζήτωρ = “one who makes a whirring noise”; διφρευτής “charioteer.”

lines.gr: ῥόμβου ἀπειρεσίου δινεύμασιν οἶμον ἐλαύνων·
lines.en: driving your course by the eddies of the boundless whorl,
lines.note: ῥόμβος is a “whorl/bull-roarer”; here the cosmic whorl, i.e., the revolving sphere; δινεύματα “eddies, gyrations.”

lines.gr: εὐσεβέσιν καθοδηγὲ καλῶν, ζαμενὴ ς ἀσεβο ῦσιν.
lines.en: guide to good for the pious, mighty against the impious,
lines.note: ζαμενής = “mighty/vehement”; thus benevolent to the pious, formidable to the impious.

lines.gr: χρησολύρη, κόσμου τὸν ἐναρμόνιον δρόμον ἕλκων ·
lines.en: golden-lyred, drawing the harmonious course of the cosmos,
lines.note: χρυσολύρη “golden-lyred” evokes Apollo; Orphic syncretism blends Hēlios–Apollo; ἐναρμόνιος “harmonious” (cosmic harmony).

lines.gr: ἔργων σημάντωρ ἀγαθῶ ν, ὡροτρόφε κοῦρε.
lines.en: sign-giver of good things, season-nurturing youth,
lines.note: σημάντωρ “sign-giver/revealer”; ὡροτρόφος “nourisher of the hours/seasons”; κοῦρος “youth.”

lines.gr: κοσμοκράτωρ, συρικτά, πυρίδρομε, κυκλοέλικτε,
lines.en: world-ruler, whistler, fire-runner, spiral-wheeling one,
lines.note: συρικτά “whistler/piper” (uncertain nuance); πυρίδρομος “fire-runner”; κυκλοέλικτος “coiling/spiralling in circles,” of the solar path.

lines.gr: φωσφόρος, α ἰολόδεικτα, φερέσβιε, κάρπιμε Παιάν·
lines.en: light-bringer, displayer of shifting signs, life-bringer, fruitful Paian,
lines.note: αἰολόδεικτος “showing variegated/shifting signs” (aiolos = changeful); φερέσβιος “life-bringing”; Παιάν = Paiān (Apollo).

lines.gr: ἀϊθαλής, ἀμίαντε, χρόνου πάτερ, ἀθάνατε Ζεῦ,
lines.en: sootless, undefiled, father of Time, immortal Zeus,
lines.note: ἀϊθαλής with diaeresis = “unsooty, clean-burning”; χρόνου πάτερ “father of Time” reflects Orphic Zeus–Aion/Helios syncretism.

lines.gr: εὔδιε, πασιφαής, κόσμου τὸ περίδρομον ὄμμα,
lines.en: giver of fair weather, all-shining, the world’s encircling eye,
lines.note: εὔδιος “fair-weathering”; περίδρομον ὄμμα “the encircling eye” = the Sun as the world’s eye.

lines.gr: σβεννύμενον λάμπων τε καλαῖς ἀκτῖσι φαεινα ῖς·
lines.en: both setting and shining with lovely, radiant rays,
lines.note: σβεννύμενον … λάμπων paradoxically expresses setting and shining (rising) with beautiful rays.

lines.gr: δεῖκτα δικαιοσύνης, φιλονάματε, δέσποτα κόσμου·
lines.en: index of justice, lover of streams, lord of the cosmos,
lines.note: δεῖκτα (sc. δείκτης) “indicator” of justice; φιλονάματος “lover of streams” (νάμα = stream), perhaps of the Sun’s horse-baths.

lines.gr: πιστοφύλαξ, αἰεὶ πανυπέρτατε, πᾶσιν ἀρωγέ ·
lines.en: trusty guardian, ever most high, helper to all,
lines.note: πιστοφύλαξ “faithful guardian”; πανυπέρτατος superlative “most supreme”; ἀρωγός “helper.”

lines.gr: ὄμμα δικαιοσύνης, ζωῆς φ ῶς· ὦ ἐλάσιππε,
lines.en: eye of justice, light of life; O driver of horses,
lines.note: Repetition of the justice motif; ἐλάσιππος “horse-driver.”

lines.gr: μάστιγι λιγυρ ῇ τετράορον ἅρμα διώκων,
lines.en: with shrill whip urging on your four-horsed chariot,
lines.note: τετράορον ἅρμα is an Orphic form meaning “four-horsed chariot” (cf. more common τέθριππον).

lines.gr: κλῦθι λόγων, ἡδὺν δὲ βίον μύστῃ σι πρόφαινε.
lines.en: hear my words, and show forth a sweet life to the initiates.
lines.note: μύστῃσι is dative plural “to the initiates”; πρόφαινε “manifest/show forth”—a typical Orphic closing petition.

lines.gr: Κλῦθι, θεὰ βασίλεια, φαεσφόρε, δῖα Σελήνη ·
lines.en: Hear, O queenly goddess, light-bringer, divine Selene;
lines.note: φαεσφόρε = “light-bringer”; θεὰ βασίλεια = “queenly goddess.” Retains the theonym Selene.

lines.gr: ταυρόκερως Μήνη, νυκτιδρόμος, ἠεροφο ῖτι,
lines.en: bull-horned Mene, night-roaming, air-wandering;
lines.note: Μήνη (Mene) is a lunar theonym; ταυρόκερως “bull-horned” evokes the crescent; ἠεροφοῖτι = “air-wandering” (var. ἠεροφοίτη/ἠεροφοίτις).

lines.gr: ἐννυχίη, δ ᾳδοῦχε , κόρη, εὐάστερε, Μήνη·
lines.en: nocturnal one, torch-bearer, maiden, well-starred Mene;
lines.note: ἐννυχίη = “nightly, nocturnal”; δᾳδοῦχε = “torch-bearer,” a ritual epithet; εὐάστερε = “well-starred.”

lines.gr: αὐξομένη καὶ λειπομένη, θῆλύς τε καὶ ἄρσην·
lines.en: waxing and waning, both female and male;
lines.note: θῆλύς τε καὶ ἄρσην “female and male” marks the Moon’s androgynous/dual nature alongside its phases (waxing/waning).

lines.gr: αὐγήτειρα , φίλιππε, χρόνου μῆτερ, φερέκαρπε·
lines.en: bringer of radiance, horse-loving, mother of Time, fruit-bearing;
lines.note: αὐγήτειρα “bringer of radiance/light”; φίλιππε “horse-loving” (chariot-imagery of lunar travel); χρόνου μῆτερ “mother of Time” (the Moon as measurer of time); φερέκαρπε “fruit-bearing” (fertility).

lines.gr: ἠλεκτρίς, βαρύθυμε, καταυγάστειρα, λοχείη·
lines.en: amber-bright, grave of heart, she who beams down, helper in childbirth;
lines.note: ἠλεκτρίς relates to ἤλεκτρον “amber,” hence “amber-bright” (by extension “electric, radiant”); βαρύθυμε = “grave-minded”; καταυγάστειρα = “she who shines down”; λοχείη = “of/for childbirth.”

lines.gr: πανδερκής, φιλάγρυπνε, καλοῖς ἄστροισι βρύουσα·
lines.en: all-seeing, lover of wakefulness, abounding in fair stars;
lines.note: φιλάγρυπνε = “lover of wakefulness” (friend to night-watchers); βρύουσα “teeming/abounding” with the fair stars of the night.

lines.gr: ἡσυχί ῃ χαίρουσα καὶ εὐφρόν ῃ ὀλβιομοίρ ῳ·
lines.en: rejoicing in stillness and in the kindly night of blessed lot;
lines.note: εὐφρόνη here = “kindly night” (not the Grace Euphrosyne); ὀλβιομοίρῳ “of blessed lot,” dative with εὐφρόνη.

lines.gr: λαμπετίη, χαριδῶτι, τελεσφόρε, νυκτὸς ἄγαλμα·
lines.en: shining one, grace-bestowing, bringer-to-fulfillment, ornament of the night;
lines.note: λαμπετίη “shining one” (cf. Lampetiê); τελεσφόρε “bringer to completion/fulfillment,” often with ritual nuance; νυκτὸς ἄγαλμα “ornament of night.”

lines.gr: ἀστράρχη, τανύπεπλ’, ἑ λικοδρόμε, πάνσοφε κούρη,
lines.en: ruler of the stars, long-robed, of winding course, all-wise maiden,
lines.note: ἀστράρχη “ruler of the stars”; τανύπεπλος “long-robed”; ἑλικοδρόμε “of winding/spiraling course.”

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρ’, εὔφρων, εὐάστερε, φέγγεϊ τῷ σῷ
lines.en: come, blessed one, gracious, well-starred, with your own radiance,
lines.note: εὔφρων = “gracious, kindly”; εὐάστερε = “well-starred”; φέγγεϊ τῷ σῷ = “with your own radiance.”

lines.gr: λαμπ ομένη, σ ώζουσα νέους ἱκέτας σέο κούρη.
lines.en: shining, and saving your young suppliants, O maiden.
lines.note: The participles λαμπομένη and σῴζουσα depend on “come” (ἐλθέ): “come … shining … and saving ….” Νέους ἱκέτας may mean “young” or “new/novice” suppliants.

lines.gr: Ὦ Φύσι, παμμήτειρα θεά, πολυμήχανε μῆτερ,
lines.en: O Physis, all-mother goddess, resourceful mother,
lines.note: Φύσι is the vocative of Physis (“Nature”); παμμήτειρα = “all‑mother,” πολυμήχανε = “resourceful, of many devices.”

lines.gr: οὐρανίη , πρέσβειρα, πολύκτιτε δαῖμον, ἄνασσα ·
lines.en: heavenly, venerable, much-possessing daimon, queen;
lines.note: πρέσβειρα = “venerable/elder”; πολύκτιτε = “much‑possessing, rich in possessions.”

lines.gr: πανδαμάτωρ, ἀδάμαστε, κυβερνήτειρα, παναυγής,
lines.en: all-subduer, untamed, helmswoman, all-radiant,
lines.note: πανδαμάτωρ = “all‑subduer”; ἀδάμαστε = “untamed”; κυβερνήτειρα = fem. “helmswoman/steerswoman”; παναυγής = “all‑radiant.”

lines.gr: παντοκράτειρα, τιτιμέν’ ἀεί, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον·
lines.en: all-ruling, ever-honored, daimon most high;
lines.note: τιτιμέν’ ἀεί = “ever‑honored”; πανυπέρτατε = “most high/supreme” (voc. used of a fem. addressee).

lines.gr: ἄφθιτε, πρωτογένεια, παλαίφατε, κυδιάνειρα·
lines.en: imperishable, first-born, of ancient fame, glory-bringing to mortals;
lines.note: πρωτογένεια = “first‑born”; παλαίφατε = “of ancient report/fame”; κυδιάνειρα = “glory‑bringing to men (mortals),” a traditional epic epithet.

lines.gr: ἐννυχίη , πολύπειρε, σελασφόρε, δεινοκάθεκτε,
lines.en: nocturnal, much-experienced, light-bearing, awesomely enthroned,
lines.note: ἐννυχίη = “nocturnal”; πολύπειρε = “much‑experienced/skilled”; σελασφόρε = “light‑bearing”; δεινοκάθεκτε = “awesomely (terribly) enthroned.”

lines.gr: ἄψοφον ἀστραγάλοισι ποδῶν ἴχνος εἱλίσσουσα·
lines.en: wheeling the noiseless trace with the ankle-bones of your feet;
lines.note: ἀστράγαλοι are the ankle‑bones; ἴχνος εἱλίσσειν “to coil/wheel a track,” an image for cosmic revolution.

lines.gr: ἁγνή, κοσμήτειρα θεῶν, ἀτελής τε τελευτή,
lines.en: holy, orderer of the gods, and an end that is unending,
lines.note: κοσμήτειρα = “arranger/orderer”; ἀτελής τε τελευτή is paradoxical (“an end that is unending”), and τελευτή can also mean “initiation/consummation” in mystery vocabulary.

lines.gr: κοιν ὴ μὲν πάντεσσιν, ἀκοινώνητε δὲ μούνη·
lines.en: common to all, yet alone sharing with none;
lines.note: Paradox of Nature as both universal and solitary: κοινή “common,” ἀκοινώνητος “sharing with none.”

lines.gr: αὐτοπάτωρ, ἀπάτωρ, ἄρσην, πολύμητι, μεγίστη·
lines.en: self-sired, fatherless, male, of many counsels, greatest;
lines.note: αὐτοπάτωρ “self‑sired” with ἀπάτωρ “fatherless,” and ἄρσην “male”: deliberate androgynous/self‑caused paradox; πολύμητι = “of many counsels.”

lines.gr: εὐανθής, πλοκίη, φιλίη , πολύμικτε, δαῆμον·
lines.en: fair-blooming, wreathed, friendly, much-mingled, knowing;
lines.note: πλοκίη = “plaited/wreathed/entwined”; δαῆμον is from δαήμων “knowing/skillful,” not δαίμων “daimon.”

lines.gr: ἡγεμόνη, κράντειρα, φερέσβιε, παντρόφε κούρη,
lines.en: leader, sovereign, life-bringing, all-nourishing maiden,
lines.note: φερέσβιε = “life‑bringing/life‑sustaining”; κούρη “maiden” coexists with maternal roles, a typical hymnic tension.

lines.gr: αὐτάρκεια, Δίκη· Χαρίτων πολυώνυμε πειθώ·
lines.en: Self-sufficiency, Dike; much-named Peitho of the Charites;
lines.note: Appositional theonyms: Dike (Justice) and Peitho (Persuasion) of the Charites (Graces).

lines.gr: αἰθερίη, χθονίη τε, καὶ εἰναλίη μεδέουσα·
lines.en: aetherial, earthy, and ruling the sea;
lines.note: αἰθερίη = “aetherial, of the upper air”; εἰναλίη μεδέουσα = “ruling over the sea.”

lines.gr: πικρ ὴ μέν φαύλοισι, γλυκεῖα δὲ πειθομένοισιν·
lines.en: bitter to the base, yet sweet to those who obey;
lines.note: φαῦλος = “base/worthless”; πειθόμενοι = “those who obey/are persuaded.”

lines.gr: πάνσοφε, πανδώτειρα, κομίστρια, παμβασίλεια·
lines.en: all-wise, all-giver, bringer, queen of all;
lines.note: πανδώτειρα = “all‑giver”; κομίστρια = “bringer/conveyor”; παμβασίλεια = “queen of all.”

lines.gr: αὐξιτρόφος, πίειρα, πεπαινομένων τε λύτειρα·
lines.en: nurturing growth, fertile, deliverer of what is ripened;
lines.note: αὐξιτρόφος = “growth‑nurturing”; πεπαινομένων from πεπαίνω “to ripen/soften”: hence “deliverer of what is ripened” (births, fruits).

lines.gr: πάντων μὲν σὺ πατήρ, μήτηρ, τροφὸς ἠδὲ τιθηνός·
lines.en: of all you are father, mother, nurse, and wet-nurse;
lines.note: τροφός vs. τιθηνός: both “nurse,” with nuance of “feeder” vs. “wet‑nurse.”

lines.gr: ὠκυλόχεια, μάκαιρα, πολύσπορος, ὡριάς, ὁρμή,
lines.en: swift in childbed, blessed, much-seeding, of due season, impulse,
lines.note: ὠκυλόχεια = “swift in childbirth”; πολύσπορος = “much‑seeded/very fruitful”; ὡριάς = “of due season”; ὁρμή = “impulse/prime drive.”

lines.gr: παντοτεχνές, πλάστειρα, πολύκτιτε, πότνιε δα ῖμον,
lines.en: all-skilled in crafts, shaper, much-possessing, mistress daimon,
lines.note: παντοτεχνές = “skilled in every craft”; πλάστειρα = “shaper/molder.”

lines.gr: ἀϊδίη, κινησιφόρος, πολύπειρε, περίφρων·
lines.en: everlasting, movement-bearing, much-experienced, very prudent;
lines.note: κινησιφόρος = “bearing movement” (source of motion); περίφρων = “very prudent/shrewd.”

lines.gr: ἀενά ῳ στροφάλιγγι θοὸν ῥύμα δινεύουσα·
lines.en: whirling the swift current in an ever-flowing eddy;
lines.note: στροφάλιγξ = “whorl/eddy”; ῥῦμα = “current/flow”: cosmic vortex imagery.

lines.gr: πάνρυτε, κυκλοτερής, ἀλλοτριομορφοδίαιτε·
lines.en: all-flowing, of circular form, subsisting in alien shapes;
lines.note: πανρυτε is a crux; commonly taken as “all‑flowing”; κυκλοτερής = “circular/round”; ἀλλοτριομορφοδίαιτος = “subsisting in alien forms” (inhabiting all shapes).

lines.gr: εὔθρονε, τιμήεσσα, μόνη τὸ κριθὲν τελέουσα,
lines.en: well-throned, honored, the only one accomplishing what has been decided;
lines.note: εὔθρονος = “well‑throned”; τὸ κριθέν = “what has been judged/decided (by Fate).”

lines.gr: σκηπτούχοῦς’ ἐφύπερθε, βαρυβρεμέτειρα, κρατίστη·
lines.en: scepter-bearing from on high, heavy-roaring, mightiest;
lines.note: σκηπτούχος = “scepter‑bearing”; βαρυβρεμέτειρα = “heavy‑roaring,” an epithet elsewhere of thunder‑gods, transferred to Physis.

lines.gr: ἄτρομε, πανδαμάτειρα, πεπρωμένη, αἶσα, πυρίπνους
lines.en: fearless, all-subduing, fate-ordained, Aisa, fire-breathing,
lines.note: πεπρωμένη = “fate‑ordained”; Αἶσα (Aisa) = “Allotment/Fate”; πυρίπνους = “fire‑breathing,” suggesting elemental energy.

lines.gr: ἀΐδιος ζωή, ἠδ’ ἀθανάτη τε πρόνοια.
lines.en: everlasting life and immortal Providence.
lines.note: πρόνοια = “Providence,” personified as an attribute of Physis.

lines.gr: πάντα σὺ ἔσσὶ · τὰ πάντα σὺ γὰρ μούνη τάδε τεύχεις.
lines.en: You are all things; for you alone bring all these things to pass.
lines.note: τεύχεις = “bring about, effect.” Statement of monism: Physis is all things and the sole cause.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεά, λίτομαί σε, σὺν εὐόλβοισιν ἐν ὥραις
lines.en: But, goddess, I entreat you, in prosperous seasons,
lines.note: ὥραι = “seasons/appointed times”; εὐόλβοι = “prosperous, blessed.”

lines.gr: εἰρήνην ὑγίειανἄγειν, αὔξησιν ἁπάντων.
lines.en: to bring peace and health, and the increase of all things.
lines.note: ἄγειν governs the objects of the prayer: “to bring” peace, health, and universal increase.

lines.gr: Πᾶνα καλῶ κρατερόν, νόμιον, κόσμοιο τὸ σύμπαν,
lines.en: I call upon Pan, the mighty, the Pastoral One, the All of the cosmos,
lines.note: “κόσμοιο τὸ σύμπαν” is appositional, playing on Pan’s name (“All”): Pan as the totality of the cosmos.

lines.gr: οὐρανὸν ἠδὲ θάλασσαν, ἰδὲ χθόνα παμβασίλειαν,
lines.en: heaven and sea, and the all-sovereign earth,
lines.note: “παμβασίλειαν” = “all-sovereign,” an Orphic epithet of Earth’s universal rule.

lines.gr: καὶ πῦρ ἀθάνατον· τάδε γὰρ μέλη ἐστὶ τὰ Πανός.
lines.en: and immortal fire; for these are the members of Pan.
lines.note: “μέλη” (“members/limbs”) presents the elements as Pan’s body in a cosmic-Pan theology.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σκιρτητά, περίδρομε, σύνθρονος ὅραις·
lines.en: Come, blessed one, leaper, all-ranging runner, co-throned with the Horai;
lines.note: “σύνθρονος ὅραις”: literally “sharing a throne with the Seasons” (the Horai), situating Pan in cosmic order/time.

lines.gr: αἰγομελές, βακχευτά, φιλένθεος, ἀστροδίαιτε·
lines.en: goat-limbed, Bacchic reveler, lover of divine possession, star-dwelling;
lines.note: “αἰγομελής” = “goat-limbed”; “φιλένθεος” here “lover of divine possession/enthusiasm”; “ἀστροδίαιτος” = “star-dwelling.”

lines.gr: ἁρμονίην κόσμοιο κρέκων φιλοπαίγμονι μολπῇ,
lines.en: weaving the harmony of the cosmos with playful song,
lines.note: “κρέκων” = “weaving” (of song); “φιλοπαίγμονι” = “play-loving/playful,” underscoring Pan’s musical play.

lines.gr: φαντασιῶν ἐπαρωγέ, φόβων ἔκπαγλε βροτείων·
lines.en: helper of visions, dread to mortal fears;
lines.note: “φαντασίαι” are visionary apparitions; “ἔκπαγλος” = “terrible/awful,” hence “dread to mortal fears.”

lines.gr: αἰγονόμοις χαίρων ἀνὰ πίδακας ἠδέ τε βούταις,
lines.en: rejoicing with goatherds by the springs and with cowherds,
lines.note: “πίδακες” are natural springs; the line evokes Pan’s pastoral haunts with goatherds and cowherds.

lines.gr: εὔσκοπε, θηρητήρ, Ἠχοῦς φίλε, σύγχορε νυμφῶ ν·
lines.en: keen-sighted, hunter, friend of Echo, chorus-mate of the Nymphs;
lines.note: “εὔσκοπος” = “keen-sighted”; “σύγχορος” = “chorus-mate/fellow dancer”; Ἠχώ (Echo) personified.

lines.gr: παντοφυής, γενέτωρ πάντων, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον·
lines.en: of every nature, begetter of all, many-named daimon;
lines.note: “παντοφυής” can mean “of every kind/nature” or “of all growths”; translation reflects the polyvalence.

lines.gr: κοσμοκράτωρ, αὐξητά, φαεσφόρε, κάρπιμε Παιάν·
lines.en: world-ruler, Increaser, Light-bringer, Fruitful Paian;
lines.note: “Παιάν” (Paian) is typically an epithet of Apollo as healer; its application to Pan here is syncretic. “αὐξητά” = “Increaser.”

lines.gr: ἀντροχαρές, βαρύμηνις, ἀληθὴς Ζε ὺς ὁκεράστης.
lines.en: cave-delighting, heavy in wrath, the true horned Zeus.
lines.note: Textually debated: many read ἀληθὴς Ζεὺς κεραστής (“true horned Zeus”). Our “true horned Zeus” reflects Pan’s horned form and his assimilation to Zeus. “βαρύμηνις” = “weighty in wrath.”

lines.gr: σοὶ γὰρ ἀπειρέσιον γαίης πέδον ἐστήρικται,
lines.en: For upon you the boundless expanse of earth is set firm,
lines.note: “ἐστήρικται” = “is set firm,” presenting Pan as the cosmic foundation/basis.

lines.gr: εἴκει δ’ ἀκαμάτου πόντου τὸ βαθύ ῤῥοον ὕ δωρ,
lines.en: and the deep-flowing water of the untiring sea yields,
lines.note: No special difficulty; “βαθυῤῥοον” = “deep-flowing,” “ἀκάματος” = “untiring.”

lines.gr: Ὠκεανός τε πέριξ ἐν ὕδασι γαῖαν ἑλίσσων·
lines.en: and Okeanos, encircling, coils the earth round with his waters;
lines.note: Okeanos as the encircling world-river, a standard cosmological image.

lines.gr: ἀέριόν τε μέρισμα τροφῆς, ζῳοῖσιν ἔναυσμα,
lines.en: and the airy portion of sustenance, the kindling for living beings,
lines.note: “ἀέριον μέρισμα τροφῆς” = the airy allotment of nourishment (breath); “ἔναυσμα” = “kindling/spark” for life.

lines.gr: καὶ κορυφ ῆς ἐφύπερθεν ἐλαφροτάτου πυρὸς ὄμμα.
lines.en: and, above the summit, the eye of the lightest fire.
lines.note: “the lightest fire” signifies aither; its “eye” is plausibly the Sun (or the aitherial luminaries).

lines.gr: βαίνει γὰρ τάδε θεῖα πολύκριτα σῇσιν ἐφετμα ῖς·
lines.en: For these divine realms move, manifoldly parted, at your commands;
lines.note: “πολύκριτα” likely “much-partitioned/finely distinguished,” referring to the ordered separations of the elements; “ἐφετμαί” = divine commands/behests.

lines.gr: ἀλλάσσεις δὲ φύσεις πάντων ταῖς σῇσι προνοίαις,
lines.en: and you alter the natures of all things by your providences,
lines.note: “πρόνοιαι” = providential cares; Pan as a cosmic provident force who alters/adjusts natures.

lines.gr: βόσκων ἀνθρώπων γενεὴν κα τ’ ἀπείρονα κόσμον.
lines.en: feeding the race of humans and the boundless cosmos as well.
lines.note: No special difficulty; “βόσκων” (“feeding”) keeps the pastoral image at a cosmic scale.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, βακχευτά, φιλένθεε, βαῖν’ ἐπὶ λοιβα ῖς
lines.en: But come, blessed one, Bacchic reveler, lover of possession, upon the holy libations,
lines.note: “βαῖν’” = imperative “come”; “εὐίερος” = “most holy/very holy.”

lines.gr: εὐιέροις· ἀγαθὴ ν δ’ ὄ πασον βιότοιο τελευτὴν,
lines.en: and grant a good completion of life,
lines.note: “τελευτή” = “completion/ending” (of life), not necessarily negative.

lines.gr: Πανικ ὸν ἐκπέμπων οἶστρον ἐπὶ τέρματα γαίης.
lines.en: sending forth the Pan-ic oistros to the bounds of the earth.
lines.note: “Πανικὸς οἶστρος” = “Panic goad/frenzy.” The prayer may imply directing that force outwards “to the ends of the earth,” i.e., away from the worshipers; the nuance is ambivalent in ritual context.

lines.gr: Ἥρακλες ὀμβριμόθυμε, μεγασθενές, ἄλκιμε Τιτάν,
lines.en: Herakles, storm-hearted, mighty of strength, valiant Titan,
lines.note: ὀμβριμόθυμε “storm-/thunder-spirited”; Titan is an Orphic epithet signaling cosmic scope rather than strict genealogy.

lines.gr: καρτερόχειρ, ἀδάμαστε, βρύων ἄθλοισι κραταιοῖς,
lines.en: strong-handed, indomitable, abounding in mighty labors,
lines.note: βρύων ἄθλοισι = “teeming/abounding in labors”; ἀδάμαστε = “untamed, indomitable.”

lines.gr: αἰολόμορφε, χρόνου πάτερ, ἀΐδιος τε εὔφρων,
lines.en: of changeful form, father of Chronos, eternal and kindly,
lines.note: αἰολόμορφε “of shifting/variegated form.” χρόνου πάτερ reflects Orphic cosmology (Herakles as cosmic fire/Time’s progenitor); εὔφρων = “kindly, gracious.”

lines.gr: ἄῤῥητ’, ἀγριόθυμε, πολύλλιτε, παντοδυνάστα·
lines.en: ineffable, fierce-spirited, much-invoked, almighty ruler;
lines.note: ἄρρητε = “ineffable.” πολύλιτε (“much-invoked”) is usually read; the given πολύλλιτε likely a scribal doubling of λ.

lines.gr: παγκρατ ὲς ἦτορ ἔχων, κάρτος μέγα, τοξότα, μάντι·
lines.en: holding an all-potent heart, great might—archer and seer;
lines.note: παγκρατές ἦτορ = “all-powerful heart.” μάντι = “seer,” an unusual but attested epithet of Herakles.

lines.gr: παμφάγε, παγγενέτωρ, πανυπέρτατε, πᾶσιν ἀρωγέ ·
lines.en: all-devouring, begetter of all, most high beyond all, helper of all;
lines.note: Cosmic epithets: παμφάγος “all-devouring,” παγγενέτωρ “begetter of all,” πανυπέρτατος “most high,” ἀρωγός “helper.”

lines.gr: ὃς θνητο ῖς κατέπαυσας ἀνήμερα φ ῦλα διώξας,
lines.en: you who for mortals checked the savage tribes, driving them away,
lines.note: ἀνήμερα φῦλα “savage tribes” may denote beasts/monsters; Herakles as a civilizing force “for mortals.”

lines.gr: εἰρήνην ποθέων κουροτρόφον, ἀγλαότιμον·
lines.en: yearning for Peace, child-nurturing, bright and honored;
lines.note: Peace (Eirene) as κουροτρόφος “nurse of youths”; ἀγλαότιμος “brightly/gloriously honored.”

lines.gr: αὐτοφυής, ἀκάμας, γαίης βλάστημα φέριστον·
lines.en: self-sprung, unwearied, the earth’s finest offshoot;
lines.note: αὐτοφυής “self-sprung/self-born”; βλάστημα “shoot, offshoot,” here honorific of origin.

lines.gr: πρωτογόν οις στράψας βολίσιν, μεγαλώνυμε δαῖμον,
lines.en: flashing with primeval bolts, great-named daimon,
lines.note: πρωτογόνοις βολίσιν “primeval bolts” (ambiguous: primordial fire/lightning); μεγαλώνυμος “great-named/of great renown.”

lines.gr: ὃς περ ὶ κρατ ὶ φορε ῖς ἠῶ καὶ νύκτα μέλαιναν,
lines.en: who wear about your head Eos and black Nyx,
lines.note: ἠώς = Eos (Dawn); νύξ = Nyx (Night). “Wearing around the head” conveys cosmic/sidereal sovereignty.

lines.gr: δώδεκ’ ἀπ’ ἀντολι ῶν ἄχρι δυσμ ῶν ἆθλα διέρπων·
lines.en: traversing twelve labors from the risings to the settings;
lines.note: “From risings to settings” (ἀντολαί/δύσεις) suggests both the mythic Twelve Labors and a zodiacal/cosmic circuit.

lines.gr: ἀθάνατοις, πολύπειρος, ἀπείριτος, ἀστυφέλικτος·
lines.en: immortal, much-experienced, boundless, city-smiting;
lines.note: The transmitted ἀθάνατοις is awkward; many take an implicit “being” or emend to ἀθάνατε. ἀστυφέλικτος “city-smiting” is a martial epithet (often of Ares) transferred here.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, νούσων θελκτήρια πάντα κομίζων.
lines.en: come, blessed one, bringing every charm that soothes diseases.
lines.note: θελκτήρια = “soothings/charms,” bridging healing and apotropaic magic.

lines.gr: ἐξέλασον δὲ κακὰ ς ἄτας, κλάδον ἐν χερ ὶ πάλλων ·
lines.en: and drive out evil banes, brandishing the branch in your hand;
lines.note: κλάδος “branch” may allude to Herakles’ club (originally a tree-branch) and/or a ritual purificatory bough.

lines.gr: πτηνο ῖς τ’ ἰοβόλοις κ ῆρας χαλεπὰς ἀπόπεμπε.
lines.en: and with winged shafts send the grievous Keres away.
lines.note: πτηνοῖς ἰοβόλοις “winged shafts/arrows.” Κῆρες (Keres) are death-spirits; the prayer is to avert them.

lines.gr: Ἀϊθαλής , μακάρων τε θεῶν πάτερ ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρ ῶν,
lines.en: O soot-dark one, father of the blessed gods and of men,
lines.note: ‘Aithalēs’ means ‘soot-dark/smoky,’ a possibly chthonic epithet with ritual (incense, fire) overtones.

lines.gr: ποικιλόβουλ’, ἀμίαντε, μεγασθενές, ἄλκιμε Τιτάν
lines.en: of manifold counsel, undefiled, of great might, valiant Titan,

lines.gr: ὃς δαπαν ᾷς μὲν ἅπαντα καὶ αὔξεις ἔμπαλιν αὐτός
lines.en: who consume all things and in turn yourself increase them,
lines.note: The paradox ‘consume all things and again increase’ suits Time’s devouring yet renewing power; Orphic poetry often conflates Kronos with Chronos.

lines.gr: δεσμο ὺς ἀρῥήκτους ὃς ἔχεις κατ’ ἀπείρονα κόσμον
lines.en: you who hold unbreakable bonds throughout the boundless cosmos,
lines.note: ‘Unbreakable bonds’ can denote the binding force of Time/Fate and, by ambiguity, recall Kronos’ own bindings; here the god is the binder of the cosmos.

lines.gr: αἰῶνος Κρόνε παγγενέτωρ, Κρόνε ποικιλόμυθε
lines.en: Kronos-Aion, father of all, Kronos of intricate speech,
lines.note: αἰῶνος Κρόνε is ambiguous: it may signal syncretism (‘Kronos-Aion’) or ‘Kronos, all-begetter of Aion/age’; παγγενέτωρ = ‘father of all.’

lines.gr: Γαίης τε βλάστημα καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος·
lines.en: offspring of Gaia and starry Ouranos;

lines.gr: γέννα, φυής , μείωσι, Ῥέας πόσι, σεμνὲ Προμηθε ῦ,
lines.en: birth, growth, and diminution; spouse of Rhea, august Prometheus,
lines.note: Abstract vocatives (γέννα, φυή, μείωσις) personify phases of temporal process; ‘Prometheus’ likely functions as the epithet ‘forethinker’ applied to Kronos rather than naming the separate Titan.

lines.gr: ὃς ναίεις κατὰ πάντα μέρη κόσμοιο, γενάρχα,
lines.en: who dwell through every part of the cosmos, founder of generation,
lines.note: γενάρχα = ‘founder/originator of generation’; ναίεις ‘you dwell’ implies omnipresence through the cosmos.

lines.gr: ἀγκυλομ ῆτα, φέριστε κλύων ἱκετηρίδα φωνήν,
lines.en: crook-counseled, most excellent, hearing the suppliant voice,
lines.note: ‘ἀγκυλομήτης’ (‘crook-counseled’) is a traditional crafty-epithet of Kronos.

lines.gr: πέμποις εὐόλβου βιότου τέλος αἰὲν ἄμεμπτον.
lines.en: send a prosperous, ever blameless end of life.
lines.note: ‘εὐόλβου’ = ‘of good fortune/wealth’; the optative πέμποις expresses the prayerful wish ‘may you send.’

lines.gr: Πότν α Ῥέα, θύγατερ πολυμόρφου Πρωτογόνοιο,
lines.en: Lady Rhea, daughter of polymorphous Protogonos,
lines.note: Protogonos (“First‑Born”) is the Orphic Phanēs; “polymorphous” evokes his protean nature, here transferred genealogically to Rhea as his daughter.

lines.gr: ᾗ λ ῖς ταυροφόνος ἱ ερότροχον ἅρμα τιταίνει·
lines.en: with your train, bull‑slaying, you strain the sacred‑wheeled chariot;
lines.note: ᾗλις is problematic: many take it as ἅλις “together, in company,” or as dative plural ἥλισι “with attendants/peers.” I render “with your train.” ταυροφόνος is usually “bull‑slaying” (not “bull‑bearing”); τιταίνει means “to stretch/put under tension,” of harnessing a chariot.

lines.gr: τυμπανόδουπε, φιλοιστρομανές, χαλκόκροτε κούρη,
lines.en: drum‑beating, lover of frenzy, bronze‑clashing maiden,
lines.note: φιλοιστρομανές is built on οἶστρος (“frenzy, rapture,” lit. “gadfly”); “bronze‑clashing” alludes to cymbals; “drum‑beating” to the tympanon of Rhea/Cybele’s rites.

lines.gr: μῆτερ Ζηνὸς ἄνακτος, Ὀ λυμπίου, αἰγιόχοιο·
lines.en: mother of lord Zeus, Olympian, the aegis‑bearing,
lines.note: “Aegis‑bearing” (aigiochos) is a traditional epithet of Zeus; the syntax is “mother of lord Zeus, the Olympian, the aegis‑bearing.”

lines.gr: πάντιμ’, ἀγλαόμορφε, Κρόνου σύλλεκτρε μάκαιρα·
lines.en: all‑honored, of splendid form, blessed bedfellow of Kronos;
lines.note: σύλλεκτρε (“bedfellow/consort”) is a rare compound; “all‑honored” (πάντιμος) and “splendid‑formed” (ἀγλαόμορφος) keep the elevated cultic tone.

lines.gr: οὔρεσιν ἣ χαίρεις, θνητῶν τ’ ὀλολύγμασι φρικτοῖς·
lines.en: who rejoice in the mountains and in the dread ululations of mortals;
lines.note: ὀλολύγματα are ritual ululations; φρικτός conveys awe/terror (“making one shudder”).

lines.gr: παμβασίλεια Ῥέα, πολεμόκλονος, ὀμβριμόθυμε·
lines.en: all‑sovereign Rhea, war‑rousing, of impetuous spirit;
lines.note: παμβασίλεια “all‑sovereign”; πολεμόκλονος “war‑rousing/war‑trembling”; ὀμβριμόθυμος “impetuous, storm‑spirited.”

lines.gr: ψευδομένη σώτειρα, λυτηριάς, ἀρχιγένεθλε·
lines.en: contriver of deceit, savioress, releaser, primal‑born;
lines.note: ψευδομένη literally “practising deceit”: many emend to σειομένη (“shaking”), but “contriver of deceit” fits Rhea’s trick on Kronos (the stone in swaddling-clothes). λυτηριάς may be taken as “releaser/deliverer” (Lytēriā); ἀρχιγένεθλε “primal‑born/prime‑origin.”

lines.gr: μήτηρ μέν τε θεῶν ἠδὲ θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων.
lines.en: mother both of the gods and of mortal humans.
lines.note: Conventional Orphic formula: the Mother as universal genitrix of gods and mortals.

lines.gr: ἐκ σο ῦ γὰρ καὶ γα ῖα καὶ οὐρανὸς εὐρὺς ὕπερθεν,
lines.en: for from you are Earth and broad Heaven above,
lines.note: Orphic cosmology credits the Mother’s primacy: Earth and broad Heaven are said to derive from her.

lines.gr: καὶ πόντος, πνοαί τε. φιλόδρομος, ἀερόμορφε,
lines.en: and Sea and the breaths, lover of the rush, airy‑formed,
lines.note: πνοαί (“breaths”) = winds; “lover of the rush” (φιλόδρομος) and “airy‑formed” (ἀερόμορφος) are epithets of the goddess, not of the elements.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρα θεά, σωτήριος εὔφρονι βουλ ῇ,
lines.en: come, blessed goddess, as a savioress with kindly counsel,
lines.note: σωτήριος with εὔφρονι βουλῇ “as a savioress with kindly counsel” is a standard hymnic request for benevolent presence.

lines.gr: εἰρήνην κατάγουσα σὺν εὐόλβοις κτεάτεσσιν,
lines.en: bringing peace together with well‑blest possessions,
lines.note: κατάγειν “bring down/bestow” peace; εὐόλβος “well‑blest, prosperous.”

lines.gr: λύματα καὶ κ ῆρας πέμπουσ' ἐπὶ τέρματα γαίης.
lines.en: sending defilements and banes away to the bounds of the earth.
lines.note: λύματα are ritual defilements/offscourings; κῆρες “banes/evil fates.” The goddess is asked to drive such ills away “to the bounds of the earth.”

lines.gr: Ζεῦ πολυτίμητε, Ζεῦ ἄφθιτε, τήνδε τοι ἡμεῖς
lines.en: Zeus much-honored, Zeus imperishable—this for you we
lines.note: “Polytimēte” (much-honored) and “aphthite” (imperishable) are traditional cult epithets of Zeus; syntax anticipates the objects in the next line.

lines.gr: μαρτυρίην τιθέμεσθα λυτήριον, ἠδὲ πρόσευξιν.
lines.en: set as a witness for deliverance, and as a supplication.
lines.note: μαρτυρίην … λυτήριον: “we set [this] as a witness for release/deliverance” describes the offering as testimony securing remission (λυτήριον often of purificatory or expiatory rites); πρόσευξις = formal “prayer/supplication.”

lines.gr: ὦ βασιλε ῦ, δι ὰ σὴν κεφαλ ὴν ἐφάνη τάδε πάντα,
lines.en: O king, by your head all these things have appeared:
lines.note: διὰ σὴν κεφαλήν “by your head” is a solemn formula; in Orphic context it can allude to Zeus’s sovereign counsel and to cosmogonic myths (e.g., Athena’s epiphany from Zeus’s head).

lines.gr: γαῖα θεὰ μήτηρ, ὀρέων θ’ ὑψαυχένες ὄχθοι,
lines.en: Gaia, goddess mother, and the lofty-crested slopes of the mountains,
lines.note: ὑψαυχένες “high-necked/lofty-crested” is a Homeric epithet, here transferred to mountain ridges; Gaia is treated as the theonym (hence transliterated).

lines.gr: καὶ πόντος, καὶ πάνθ’, ὁπόσ’ οὐραν ὸς ἐντὸς ἔταξε.
lines.en: and the sea, and all things whatsoever Ouranos has ordered within.
lines.note: Ouranos here can function as both the divine Sky and the cosmic vault; ἔταξε “arranged/ordered” evokes cosmogonic ordering “within” the heavens.

lines.gr: Ζεῦ Κρόνιε, σκηπτοῦχε, καταιβάτα, ὀμβριμόθυμε,
lines.en: Zeus Kronios, scepter-bearing, Descender, of impetuous spirit,
lines.note: Kronios = “son of Kronos.” Kataibates (translated “Descender”) is a cult title of Zeus as the god who “comes down,” especially in lightning; ὀμβριμόθυμος = “of storm-impetuous/furious spirit.”

lines.gr: παντογένεθλ’, ἀρχὴ πάντων, πάντων τε τελευτή.
lines.en: source of every birth, the beginning of all, and the end of all things,
lines.note: παντογένεθλ’ (voc.) is textually and morphologically difficult; rendered “source of every birth” to capture the universal generative force. “Beginning and end of all” echoes traditional cosmological formulae.

lines.gr: σεισίχθων, αὐξητά, καθάρσιε, παντοτινάκτα,
lines.en: earth-shaker, increaser, purifier, shaker of all,
lines.note: σεισίχθων “earth-shaker” is conventionally Poseidon’s epithet but here applied to Zeus as cosmic mover; παντοτινάκτα is best taken as “shaker of all (things)” (from τινάσσω); some editors report variant readings.

lines.gr: ἀστράπιε , βροντα ῖε, κεραύνιε, φυτάλιε Ζεῦ·
lines.en: lightning-flasher, thunderer, wielder of the bolt, plant-nurturing Zeus;
lines.note: φυτάλιος “plant-nourishing,” of Zeus as rain-bringer who fosters growth; paired with thunder epithets ἀστράπιε, βρονταῖε, κεραύνιε.

lines.gr: κλῦθί μευ, α ἰολόμορφε, δίδου δ’ ὑγίειανἀμεμφ ῆ
lines.en: hear me, changefully-formed, and grant blameless health,
lines.note: αἰολόμορφε “of changeful/variform shape” evokes Orphic theologies in which Zeus assumes or contains all forms; ὑγίειαν here likely “health” (not yet the deified Hygieia).

lines.gr: εἰρήνην τε θεὰν, καὶ πλούτου δόξαν ἄμεμπτον.
lines.en: and Eirene the goddess, and the blameless glory of wealth.
lines.note: Eirene is personified (“the goddess”); πλούτου δόξαν “the glory/splendor (or good repute) of wealth” may imply Ploutos but the noun itself is not named.

lines.gr: αὐτοπάτωρ· μακάρων τε θεῶν πάτερ ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρ ῶν.
lines.en: self-siring, father of the blessed gods and of men as well.
lines.note: αὐτοπάτωρ “self-siring” is a distinctive Orphic epithet asserting Zeus’s self-generation; “father of gods and men” is traditional.

lines.gr: ἀλλά χάριν λοιβ ῇσι δίδου, φρεσίν αἴσιμα πάντα.
lines.en: But grant favor to the libations, and all things auspicious for our minds,
lines.note: αἴσιμα “auspicious/fitting, according to destiny”; λοιβαῖσι “libations” marks the ritual context of the hymn.

lines.gr: ζωήν δ’ ὀλβιόθυμον. ὁμοῦ δ’ ὑγίειανἄνασσαν
lines.en: and a life of prosperous spirit; and together Hygieia the queen,
lines.note: ὀλβιόθυμον “of prosperous/blessed spirit”; Hygieia is explicitly personified and titled ἄνασσα “queen.”

lines.gr: εἰρήνη τε θεόν κουροτρόφον ἀγλαότιμον·
lines.en: and Eirene the goddess, child-nurturing, splendidly honored;
lines.note: κουροτρόφον “child-nurturing/nurse of youths”; ἀγλαότιμον “splendidly honored”; Eirene is again personified.

lines.gr: καί βίον εὐθύμοισιν ἀεί θάλλοντα λογισμοῖς.
lines.en: and a life ever blooming with cheerful counsels.
lines.note: εὐθύμοις λογισμοῖς “cheerful/steady-minded thoughts/counsels”; the wish concludes with an ethical-psychological blessing typical of Orphic prayer.

lines.gr: Κυανέοις κόλποισιν ἐνημένη, ἀερόμορφε,
lines.en: Enfolded in dark-blue bosoms, air-formed,
lines.note: kyaneois kolpoisin: kolpos can mean “bosom,” “fold (of a garment),” or “bay/recess”; here likely the dark-blue hollows of sky/air; aeromorphe “air-formed” signals Hera’s identification with the airy element in Orphic theology.

lines.gr: Ἥρη παμβασίλεια, Διὸς σύλλεκτρε μάκαιρα,
lines.en: Hera, all-sovereign, blessed bedfellow of Zeus,
lines.note: syllektre (“bedfellow/bedmate”) is a rare compound emphasizing Hera’s conjugal role with Zeus; panbasileia = “all-sovereign.”

lines.gr: ψυχοτρόφους αὔρας θνητοῖς παρέχουσα προσηνεῖς.
lines.en: granting to mortals kindly, soul-nurturing breezes.
lines.note: psychotrophous auras literally “soul-nourishing breezes/airs”; prosēneis “gracious, kindly (to mortals).”

lines.gr: ὄμβρων μὲν μήτηρ, ἀνέμων τροφέ, παντογένεθλε.
lines.en: Mother of rains, nurse of winds, all-begetting one,
lines.note: pantogenethle is debated: “all-begetting/all-producing” vs. “of every lineage.” Given the hymn’s cosmological scope, “all-begetting” suits the context; trophē “nurse” (not “mother”) of winds marks a secondary nurturing role.

lines.gr: χωρὶς γὰρ σέθεν οὐδὲν ὅλως ζωῆς φύσιν ἔγνω ·
lines.en: for apart from you nothing at all has known the nature of life;
lines.note: zōēs physis “the nature/principle of life”; the gnomic “has known” personifies all beings/things as recognizing life only through Hera’s presence.

lines.gr: κοινωνεῖς γὰρ ἅπασι κεκραμένη ἠέρι σεμνῷ.
lines.en: for you share in all things, being mingled with august air.
lines.note: kekramenē “mingled” evokes cosmological mixture; “august air” (aēr semnos) is the sacred, pervasive atmosphere with which Hera is identified.

lines.gr: πάντων γὰρ κρατέεις μούνη, πάντεσσί τ’ ἀνάσσεις.
lines.en: for you alone hold sway over all, and you are queen of all.
lines.note: krateis “hold sway” and anasseis “are queen” form an emphatic pair underscoring universal rule.

lines.gr: ἠερίοις ῥοίζοισι τινασσομένη κατὰ χεῦμα.
lines.en: quivering amid airy whirrings along the downrush.
lines.note: rhoizos “whizzing/whirring (of wind)”; kata cheuma “along the pour/stream,” likely the downpour of rain or the torrent-like rush of air; translation reflects this meteorological imagery.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαιρα θεά, πολυώνυμε, παμβασίλεια,
lines.en: But come, blessed goddess, much-named, all-sovereign,
lines.note: polyonyme “much-named” is a standard Orphic epithet; panbasileia repeated for emphasis.

lines.gr: ἔλθοις εὐμενέουσα καλῷ γήθοντι προσώπῳ.
lines.en: in kindness, with a fair and gladdening countenance.
lines.note: eumenousa “propitious, kindly”; gēthonti prosōpōi “with a rejoicing/gladdening face,” the favorable epiphany of the goddess.

lines.gr: Κλῦθι, Ποσειδάον γαιήοχε, κυανοχαῖτα,
lines.en: Hear me, Poseidōn, earth-holder, dark-maned,
lines.note: γαιήοχος “earth-holder” is a traditional Poseidon epithet; κυανοχαῖτα “dark-/blue-maned” evokes the sea’s color and the god’s hair.

lines.gr: ἵππιε, χαλκοτόρευτον ἔχων χείρεσσι τρίαιναν·
lines.en: horse-lord, holding in your hands the bronze-wrought trident;
lines.note: ἵππιε = “of horses,” hence “horse-lord”; χαλκοτόρευτος “bronze-wrought” (finely worked in bronze).

lines.gr: ὃς ναίεις πόντοιο βαθυστέρνοιο θέμεθλα,
lines.en: you who dwell at the foundations of the deep-bosomed sea,
lines.note: θέμεθλα “foundations” (of the sea); βαθυστέρνοιο “deep-bosomed,” a Homeric formula for vastness.

lines.gr: ποντομέδων, ἁλίδουπε, βαρύκτυπος, ἐννοσίγαιε,
lines.en: sea-lord, sea-roaring, heavy-thundering, Earth-shaker,
lines.note: ποντομέδων “sea-lord”; ἁλίδουπος “sea-roaring/sea-sounding”; βαρύκτυπος “heavy-thundering”; Ἐννοσίγαιος is the well-known “Earth-shaker” epithet.

lines.gr: κυμοθαλής, χαριτῶπα, τετράορον ἅρμα διώκων,
lines.en: heaving with waves, of gracious countenance, driving a chariot with a four-year-old team,
lines.note: κυμοθαλής “wave-swollen/heaving”; χαριτῶπα “grace-faced,” rendered “of gracious countenance.” τετράορον literally “four-year-old”: with ἅρμα this is difficult; commonly taken to imply a team of four-year-old horses drawing the chariot (some translate as if “four-horsed,” though the Greek is not τέθριππον).

lines.gr: εἰναλίοις ῥοίζοισι τινάσσων ἁλμυρ ὸν ὕδωρ·
lines.en: shaking the briny water with sea-born roarings;
lines.note: ῥοίζοι “whirrings/roarings” of motion; εἰναλίος “in/ of the sea.”

lines.gr: ὃς τριτάτης ἔλαχες μοίρης βαθὺ χεῦμα θαλάσσης,
lines.en: you who by the third portion obtained the deep flood of the sea,
lines.note: τριτάτης μοίρης “the third share,” alluding to the tripartite allotment of cosmos among the brothers.

lines.gr: κύμασι τερπόμενος θηρσίν θ’ ἅμα, πότνιε δαῖμον.
lines.en: delighting in the waves and with the beasts as well, august daimon.
lines.note: πότνιε δαῖμον “august daimon”: daimon here = divine power, not “demon.” θηρσίν = sea-creatures.

lines.gr: ἕδρανα γῆς σώζοις καὶ νηῶν ε ὔδρομον ὁρμήν,
lines.en: preserve the seats of the earth and the swift-sailing onrush of ships,
lines.note: ἕδρανα γῆς “seats/foundations of the earth” (i.e., steadiness against earthquakes); νηῶν εὔδρομος ὁρμή “swift-sailing impetus/course of ships.”

lines.gr: εἰρήνην, ὑγίειανἄγω ν, ἠδ’ ὄλβον ἀμεμφ ῆ.
lines.en: bringing peace and health, and unblamed prosperity.
lines.note: ἀμέμφῃ (dative used adverbially) = “blamelessly,” here “unblamed” qualifying prosperity (ὄλβος).

lines.gr: Κλῦθι Ποσειδάων, Ζηνός παῖ πρεσβυγένεθλε,
lines.en: Hear me, Poseidōn, child of Zeus, eldest-born,
lines.note: Textually problematic: Ζηνός παῖ “child of Zeus” is at odds with mainstream genealogy (son of Kronos); πρεσβυγένεθλος “eldest-born.” Likely secondary influence from Zeus-language; translation follows the transmitted reading.

lines.gr: οὐρανίων μακάρων τε θεῶν πάτερ ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρ ῶν.
lines.en: father of the blessed heavenly gods and of men as well.
lines.note: A stereotyped Zeus formula (“father of gods and men”); many editors suspect interpolation or formulaic contamination.

lines.gr: ὃς ναίεις κορυφαῖος ἐπ’ Οὐλύμποιο καρήνων
lines.en: you who dwell upon the crest of Olympos’ peaks,
lines.note: κορυφαῖος … καρήνων = “at the very crest of the peaks,” epic pleonasm for the summit of Olympos.

lines.gr: δεύτερος ἐκ Δι ὸς εἰληχ ὼς πάντεσσιν ἀνάσσειν.
lines.en: having received to rule over all as second after Zeus;
lines.note: δεύτερος ἐκ Διός “second after Zeus”; εἰληχώς (perf. of λαγχάνω) links to the cosmic allotment motif.

lines.gr: ἵππιε, χαλκοτόρευτον ἔχων χείρεσσι τρίαιναν.
lines.en: horse-lord, holding in your hands the bronze-wrought trident,
lines.note: Repetition of line 2 is an epic/Orphic liturgical refrain.

lines.gr: εὐρύμεδον, χαριτῶπα, τετράορον ἅρμα διώκων.
lines.en: wide-ruling, of gracious countenance, driving a chariot with a four-year-old team.
lines.note: εὐρύμεδον “wide-ruling” (lit. “of broad sway”); τετράορον as at line 5 (see note there).

lines.gr: ὦ ἄναξ παντοκράτωρ, ἱερώτατος, ἀγλαότιμε,
lines.en: O lord almighty, most holy, gloriously honored,
lines.note: παντοκράτωρ “almighty” is a traditional high-epic epithet (later prominent in other contexts too); ἀγλαότιμος “gloriously honored.”

lines.gr: σεμνο ῖς μυστοπόλοις χαίρων ὁσίοις τε σεβασμοῖς,
lines.en: rejoicing in august mystic rites and in holy reverences,
lines.note: μυστοπόλοις “mystic-officiants/celebrants of mysteries”; σεβασμοί “acts of reverence, venerations.”

lines.gr: ἵλαος ε ἴης, εὐτυχίην μύστῃσι προφαίνων.
lines.en: be gracious, revealing good fortune to the initiates.
lines.note: μύσται “initiates” in the mysteries; προφαίνων “revealing/manifesting,” with epiphanic nuance.

lines.gr: Ὠ τὸν ὑποχθόνιον ναίων δόμον, ὀμβριμόθυμε,
lines.en: O you who dwell in the house beneath the earth, impetuous of heart,
lines.note: ὀμβριμόθυμος = “impetuous, vehement in spirit,” a solemn epithet; ὑποχθόνιος “beneath the earth.”

lines.gr: Ταρτάριον λειμῶνα βαθύσκιον ἠδὲ λιπαυγ ῆ,
lines.en: in the Tartaric meadow, deep-shadowed and richly radiant,
lines.note: λιπαυγής “richly radiant, gleaming”; the “Tartaric meadow” (λειμών) is a traditional Orphic topos for the underworld’s precincts, paradoxically both shaded and luminous.

lines.gr: Ζεῦ χθόνιε σκηπτο ῦχε, τάδ’ ἱερὰ δέξο προθύμως·
lines.en: Zeus Chthonios, Scepter-holder, receive these sacred rites with good will;
lines.note: σκηπτούχος “scepter-bearing/scepter-holder”; “Zeus Chthonios” reflects the Orphic/Homeric identification of Hades with a chthonic Zeus.

lines.gr: Πλούτων, ὃς κατέχεις γαίης κληῖδας ἁπάσης,
lines.en: Plouton, you who hold the keys of all the earth,
lines.note: “keys of all the earth” (κληῖδες) denotes control over access to and the locking of the underworld (and, by extension, hidden earthly wealth).

lines.gr: πλουτοδοτῶν γενε ὴν βροτέην καρποῖς ἐνιαυτ ῶν.
lines.en: bestowing wealth upon the mortal race with the fruits of the seasons.
lines.note: ἐνιαυτῶν “of the years/seasons”; Plouton as wealth-giver via agricultural produce and seasonal harvests.

lines.gr: ὃς τριτάτης μοίρης ἔλαχες χθόνα παμβασίλειαν,
lines.en: who by lot obtained as the third share the all-sovereign earth,
lines.note: “third share” (τριτάτης μοίρης) alludes to the cosmic division among the sons of Kronos; χθόνα παμβασίλειαν “the all-sovereign earth/realm” = the underworld domain.

lines.gr: ἕδρανον ἀθανάτων, θνητῶν στήριγμα κραταιόν
lines.en: the seat of the immortals, the mighty support of mortals,
lines.note: ἕδρανον “seat/throne-base” is striking; the phrase makes the earth the “seat of the immortals” and “support of mortals,” i.e., the cosmic foundation. The syntax is compressed but traditional.

lines.gr: ὃς θρόνον ἐστήριξας ὑπὸ ζοφοειδέα χῶρον,
lines.en: who fixed your throne beneath the gloom-dark region,
lines.note: ζοφοειδής “gloom-like, murk-dark,” a standard descriptor of the underworld’s region.

lines.gr: τηλέπορον τ’, ἀκάμαντα, λιπόπνοον, ἄκριτον ᾅδην,
lines.en: and Hades—far-reaching, unwearied, breathless, indiscriminate,
lines.note: τηλέπορος “far-reaching/remote-reaching”; ἀκάμαντος “unwearied”; λιπόπνοος “bereft of breath, breathless”; ἄκριτος “undiscriminating/indistinct,” here of Hades as a realm receiving all without distinction.

lines.gr: κυάνεόν τ’ Ἀχέρονθ’, ὃ ς ἔχει ῥιζώματα γαίης.
lines.en: and dark Acheron, which holds the roots of the earth.
lines.note: κυάνεος “dark, blue-black”; Acheron “holds the roots of the earth,” an Orphic cosmological image of the underworld river girding/supporting the earth’s foundations.

lines.gr: ὃς κρατέεις θνητῶν θα νάτου χάριν, ὦ πολυδέγμων,
lines.en: who hold sway over mortals in respect to death, O Receiver-of-Many,
lines.note: θανάτου χάριν is difficult; taken as “in respect to death/on account of death.” Some traditions read κλείδας (“keys”) here; I retain the transmitted sense of dominion regarding mortals’ death. Πολυδέγμων = “Receiver-of-Many,” a title of Hades.

lines.gr: Εὔβουλ’· ἁγνοπόλου Δημήτερος ὅς ποτε πα ῖδα
lines.en: Euboulos, who once the daughter of Demeter of holy service,
lines.note: Εὔβουλος (Euboulos/Eubouleus) functions as an epithet of Plouton in Orphic cult and Eleusinian lore. ἁγνοπόλου modifies Demeter: “of holy service/holy rites,” i.e., the pure/holy officiant.

lines.gr: νυμφεύσας λειμῶνος ἀποσπαδίην διὰ πόντου,
lines.en: having made her your bride, snatched from the meadow, through the sea,
lines.note: ἀποσπαδίη “one torn/plucked away,” of Persephone snatched from the meadow; νυμφεύσας “having made [her] a bride.” The passage recounts the abduction-marriage of Kore.

lines.gr: τετρώροις ἵπποισιν ὑπ’ Ἀτθίδος ἤγαγες ἄντρον,
lines.en: with a four-horsed team you led to the cave beneath Attica,
lines.note: τετρώροις ἵπποισιν “with a four-horsed team.” ὑπ’ Ἀτθίδος ἄντρον “to the cave beneath Attica,” a reference to the Eleusinian Ploutonion.

lines.gr: δήμου Ἐλευσῖνος, τόθι περ πύλαι εἴσ’ Ἀΐδαο.
lines.en: of the deme of Eleusis, where indeed are the gates of Aidēs.
lines.note: Eleusis as the place “where the gates of Aidēs are” reflects local cult-topography and mystery-tradition.

lines.gr: μοῦνος ἔφυς ἀφανῶ ν ἔργων φανερῶν τε βραβευτής.
lines.en: you alone are by nature the arbiter of works unseen and seen.
lines.note: βραβευτής “arbiter/umpire”; the pair ἀφανῶν/φανερῶν “unseen/seen” marks jurisdiction over both the invisible and visible realms.

lines.gr: ἔνθεε, παντοκράτωρ, ἱερώτατος, ἀγλαότιμε,
lines.en: Divine One, All-ruler, most holy, splendid in honor,
lines.note: ἔνθεε “divine/inspired one”; παντοκράτωρ “All-ruler/almighty”; ἀγλαότιμος “splendidly honored.”

lines.gr: σεμνο ῖς μυστιπόλοις χαίρων ὁσίοις τε σεβασμοῖς·
lines.en: rejoicing in august mystic rites and holy reverences;
lines.note: μυστιπόλοις (dat. pl.) “mystic rites/ministrations” or “mystic ministers”; the line evokes delight in mystery-cult observance.

lines.gr: ἵλαον ἀγκαλέω σε μολεῖν κεχαρηότα μύσταις.
lines.en: I call upon you to come gracious, delighted with the initiates.
lines.note: ἀγκαλέω “I summon/invoke”; μολεῖν “to come”; κεχαρηότα μύσταις “pleased with the initiates,” a conventional Orphic closing wish.

lines.gr: Ζεῦ πάτερ, ὑφίβρομον πυρσαυγέα κόσμον ἐλαύνων,
lines.en: Zeus, Father, high-thundering, driving the fire-rayed cosmos,
lines.note: ὑφίβρομον is likely a corruption of ὑψίβρομον (“high-thundering”); κόσμον ἐλαύνων uses the chariot-driving metaphor for divine governance; πυρσαυγέα = “fire-rayed, fire-flashing.”

lines.gr: στράπτων αἰθερίου στεροπῆς πανυ πέρτατον αἴγλην,
lines.en: flashing the loftiest brilliance of aetherial lightning,
lines.note: The spacing πανυ πέρτατον should be πανυπέρτατον (“most supremely”); αἰθερίου στεροπῆς = “aetherial lightning”; στράπτων = “flashing.”

lines.gr: παμμακάρων ἕδρανον θείαις βροντ ῇσι τινάσσων,
lines.en: shaking the seat of the all-blessed with divine thunders,
lines.note: παμμακάρων ἕδρανον = “seat/throne of the all-blessed (gods)”; βρονταῖσι (here written with irregular spacing) is instrumental dative plural.

lines.gr: νάμασι παννεφέλοις στεροπὴν φλεγέθουσαν ἀναίθων
lines.en: kindling, with all-cloudy streams, the blazing lightning,
