lines.note: νάμασι παννεφέλοις (“with all-cloudy streams”) evokes the watery masses of storm-clouds; ἀναίθων (“kindling up”) governs στεροπήν (“lightning”).

lines.gr: λαίλαπας, ὄμβρους, πρηστῆρας, κρατερούς τε κεραυνούς,
lines.en: tempests, rains, blast-winds, and mighty thunderbolts,
lines.note: πρηστῆρες are violent gusts/whirlwinds; the line continues the catalogue of meteorological forces under Zeus’s sway.

lines.gr: παμφλέκτους, κραιπούς, φρικώδεας, ὀμβριμοθύμους,
lines.en: all-consuming, violent, dreadful, storm-hearted,
lines.note: κραιπός = “violent/impetuous,” rare; ὀμβριμόθυμος = “storm-spirited, thunder-souled,” an epic compound.

lines.gr: βάλλων εὐροθίους, φλογερούς, νεφέεσσι καλύ πτων
lines.en: hurling them wide-rushing, fiery, and veiling them with clouds,
lines.note: εὐροθίους is uncertain; rendered “wide-rushing.” νεφέεσσι (“with clouds”) is epic dative; καλύπτων (“veiling”) is circumstantial to βάλλων (“hurling”).

lines.gr: πτην ὸν ὅπλον δεινόν, κλονοκάρδιον, ὀρθοέθειρον,
lines.en: the winged weapon—fearsome, heart-tumulting, straight-driving—
lines.note: πτηνόν (“winged”) is a conventional epithet of the thunderbolt; κλονοκάρδιον = “heart-tumulting”; ὀρθοέθειρον ≈ “straight-driving.”

lines.gr: αἰφνίδιον, βρονταῖον, ἀνίκητον βέλος ἁγνὸν
lines.en: sudden, thunderous, the holy, unconquered dart,
lines.note: βρονταῖον is taken as “thunderous” (not “born of thunder”); ἁγνόν emphasizes the sacral purity of Zeus’s bolt.

lines.gr: ῥοίζου ἀπειρεσίου δινεύμασι, παμφάγον ὁρμῇ,
lines.en: with eddies of boundless whirring, with all-devouring rush,
lines.note: ῥοίζος = the whirring/hissing sound of swift motion; ἀπειρέσιος = “boundless” (epic); παμφάγος ὁρμή = “all-devouring onrush.”

lines.gr: ἄῤῥηκτον, βαρύθυμον, ἀμαιμάκετον, πρηστ ῆρος
lines.en: unbreakable, heavy-souled, irresistible, of the blast,
lines.note: πρηστήρ = “blast/whirlwind,” genitive dependent notionally on βέλος in the next line; βαρύθυμον (“heavy-souled”) personifies the bolt’s grave force; ἀμαιμάκετον = “irresistible.”

lines.gr: οὐράνιον βέλος ὀξὺ καταιβάτου αἰθαλόεντος.
lines.en: a heavenly shaft, keen in the smoky down-rush,
lines.note: καταιβάτου (“down-rushing,” of storm-cloud) + αἰθαλόεντος (“smoke-dark, sooty”) yield the sense “smoky down-rush.”

lines.gr: ὃν καὶ γα ῖα πέφρικε θάλασσά τε παμφανόωσα,
lines.en: at which even Earth has shuddered, and the all-glittering Sea,
lines.note: παμφανόωσα (“all-shining”) is an epic epithet of the sea; cosmic tremor imagery underscores Zeus’s universal power.

lines.gr: καὶ θ ῆρες πτήσσουσιν, ὅταν κτύπος οὖας ἐσέλθ ῃ
lines.en: and beasts cower whenever the crash enters the ears,
lines.note: οὖας (for “ears”) is an epic/Ionic form; πτήσσειν = “cower, be frightened.”

lines.gr: μαρμαίρει δὲ πρόσωπ’ α ὐγα ῖς, σμαραγεῖ δὲ κεραυνὸς
lines.en: faces flash with rays, and the thunderbolt crackles,
lines.note: μαρμαίρειν = “to flash/gleam”; σμαραγεῖ = “crackles, resounds,” an onomatopoetic verb for thunder.

lines.gr: αἰθέρος ἐν γυάλοισι δια ῤῥήξας δὲ χιτ ῶνα,
lines.en: rending the robe of aether in its hollows,
lines.note: γυάλοισι (“in hollows/depths”) metaphorically of the aether; χιτών (“tunic/garment”) and “veil” extend the celestial clothing metaphor for the sky.

lines.gr: οὐράνιον προκάλυμμα, χαλλᾷς ἀργῆτα κεραυνόν.
lines.en: the heavenly veil—then you let loose the bright thunderbolt.
lines.note: προκάλυμμα = “veil/curtain”; χαλλᾷς is likely a corruption for χαλᾷς (“you let loose/down”); ἀργῆτα = “bright, shining” (poetic form).

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, θυμὸν βαρύν ἔμβαλε κύμασι πόντου,
lines.en: But, Blessed One, cast your heavy spirit into the waves of the sea,
lines.note: θυμὸν βαρύν ἔμβαλε = idiom “cast down heavy spirit,” i.e., abate wrath; a prayer to still the storm.

lines.gr: ἠδ’ ὀ ρέων κορυφ ῇσι· τὸ σὸν κράτος ἴσμεν ἅπαντες.
lines.en: and upon the mountain peaks; we all know your might.
lines.note: Conventional acknowledgement formula τὸ σὸν κράτος ἴσμεν ἅπαντες (“we all know your might”).

lines.gr: ἀλλ ὰ χάριν λοιβ ῆς σ ὺ δίδου φρεσὶν α ἴσιμα πάντα,
lines.en: Yet, in return for the libation, grant to our minds all fitting things,
lines.note: χάριν λοιβῆς = “in return for the libation”; αἴσιμα = “fitting, according to right/fate”; φρένες = “mind/heart.”

lines.gr: ζωήν τ’ ὀλβιόθυμον, ὁμοῦ θ’ ὑ γίειαν ἄνασσαν,
lines.en: and life of prosperous spirit, and together queenly Hygieia,
lines.note: ὀλβιόθυμος = “prosperous in spirit/heart.” Ὑγίεια is here personified; hence “Hygieia,” translated as a theonym and styled “queenly.”

lines.gr: Εἰρήνην τε θεὸν κουροτρόφον, ἀγλαότιμον,
lines.en: and Eirene, the child-nurturing god, gloriously honored,
lines.note: Εἰρήνη retained as theonym (not “Peace”); κουροτρόφος = “child-nurturing”; ἀγλαότιμος = “gloriously honored.”

lines.gr: καὶ βίον εὐθύμοισιν ἀεὶ θάλλοντα λογισμοῖς.
lines.en: and a life ever flourishing with cheerful counsels.
lines.note: εὐθύμος = “cheerful, well-disposed”; λογισμοί = “reasonings, counsels”; “counsels” chosen for elevated register.

lines.gr: Κικλ ήσκω μέγαν, ἁγνόν, ἐρισμάραγον, περίφαντον,
lines.en: I call upon the great, holy, loudly-crashing, all-manifest one,
lines.note: Κικλήσκω (“I call upon”) is the expected reading; ἐρισμάραγον is from σμάραγος “crash, din,” an epithet of thunder; περίφαντον “very conspicuous/manifest to all.”

lines.gr: ἀέριον, φλογόεντα, πυρίδρομον, ἠεροφεγγῆ,
lines.en: airy, flaming, fire-racing, aether-gleaming,
lines.note: ἀέριον “of the air/airy”; πυρίδρομον “fire-running” (swift as fire); ἠεροφεγγής “shining through mist/ether,” of lightning through cloud.

lines.gr: ἀστράπτοντα σέλας νεφέων παταγοδρόμῳ α ὐδῇ,
lines.en: flashing the radiance of the clouds with crash-rushing voice,
lines.note: ἀστράπτοντα σέλας “flashing radiance/beam”; παταγοδρόμῳ αὐδῇ “with crash-rushing voice,” αὐδή ‘voice’ used metaphorically of thunder. The transmitted spacing α ὐδῇ should be αὐδῇ.

lines.gr: φρικώδη, βαρύμηνιν, ἀνίκητον θεὸν ἁγνόν,
lines.en: awful, heavy-wrathful, unconquered holy god,
lines.note: φρικώδη “making one shudder, awful”; βαρύμηνιν built on μῆνις “wrath,” hence “heavy-wrathful”; appositional θεὸν ἁγνόν reiterates holiness.

lines.gr: ἀστραπέα Δία, παγγενέτην, βασιλῆα μέγιστον,
lines.en: Zeus the Lightning-Flasher, All-begetter, greatest king,
lines.note: ἀστραπέα Δία “Zeus the Lightning(-flasher)”; παγγενέτην “all-begetter,” a favored Orphic epithet; βασιλῆα μέγιστον “greatest king.”

lines.gr: εὐμενέοντα φέρειν γλυκερὴν βιότοιο τελευτήν.
lines.en: be gracious to bring the sweet completion of life.
lines.note: εὐμενέοντα + infinitive expresses a petition: “be gracious to grant/bring”; βιότοιο is epic genitive “of life”; τελευτή “end, completion,” a euphemism for death.

lines.gr: Ἠέριοι νεφέλαι, καρποτρόφοι, οὐρανόπλαγκτοι,
lines.en: Morning clouds, fruit‑nourishing, sky‑wandering,
lines.note: Ἠέριοι = “of early morning, dawn‑” (poetic); οὐρανόπλαγκτοι lit. “wandering through heaven.”

lines.gr: ὁμβροτόκοι, πνοι ῇσιν ἐ λαυνόμεναι κατὰ κόσμον·
lines.en: rain‑bearing, driven in due order by the blasts,
lines.note: ὁμβροτόκοι lit. “rain‑begetting”; πνοιῇσιν ἐλαυνόμεναι = “driven by breaths/gusts (of wind)”; κατὰ κόσμον = “in due order/according to cosmic order.” Note minor spacing issues in the source (πνοι ῇσιν ἐ λαυνόμεναι) normalized here.

lines.gr: βροντα ῖαι, πυρόεσσαι, ἐρίβρομοι, ὑγροκέλευθοι·
lines.en: thunderous, fiery, loud‑roaring, on watery paths,
lines.note: βρονταῖαι = “thunderous”; πυρόεσσαι = “fiery, flame‑hued (of lightning)”; ὑγροκέλευθοι = “of watery course/track.”

lines.gr: ἠέρος ἐν κόλπ ῳ πάταγον φρικώδε’ ἔχουσαι ·
lines.en: holding within the bosom of the air a dreadful clatter,
lines.note: ἠέρος is the poetic genitive of ἀήρ “air, mist”; πάταγος = “crash, clatter”; φρικώδε’ = “shudder‑inducing, dreadful.” Source spacing normalized (ἐν κόλπῳ).

lines.gr: πνεύμασιν ἀντίσπαστοι ἐπιδρομάδην παταγεῦσαι,
lines.en: by winds wrenched counterwise, rushing in with a rattle,
lines.note: ἀντίσπαστοι = “dragged/pulled in opposite directions” (by contrary winds); ἐπιδρομάδην = “in rushing onset, by way of an onslaught”; παταγεῦσαι = “clattering, making a racket.”

lines.gr: ὑμέας ν ῦν λίτομαι, δροσοείμονες, εὔπνοοι αὔραις,
lines.en: you I now implore, dew‑clad, fair‑blowing breezes,
lines.note: δροσοείμονες = “dew‑clad”; εὔπνοοι αὔραις can be taken as appositional (“fair‑blowing breezes”) or instrumental (“with kindly breezes”). Dative used poetically in address. Source spacing normalized (ὑμέας νῦν).

lines.gr: πέμπειν καρποτρόφους ὄμβρους ἐπὶ μητέρα γαῖαν.
lines.en: to send fruit‑nourishing showers upon Mother Earth.
lines.note: μητέρα γαῖαν = conventional “Mother Earth”; καρποτρόφους ὄμβρους repeats the opening epithet with “showers.”

lines.gr: Ὠκεανο ῦ καλέω νύμφην γλαυκώπιδα Τηθύν,
lines.en: I call the Nymph of Okeanos, bright‑eyed Tethys,
lines.note: γλαυκώπιδα (“bright/grey‑eyed”)—an epithet famous of Athene, here transferred to Tethys; Ὠκεανοῦ marks her as consort/daughter “of Okeanos.”

lines.gr: κυανόπεπλον ἄνασσαν, ἐΰτροχα κυμαίνουσαν,
lines.en: the dark‑veiled queen, swelling with well‑running billows,
lines.note: κυανόπεπλον = “dark-/deep‑blue‑robed”; ἐΰτροχα adverbial “with easy/ready courses,” modifying the swelling of the waves (κυμαίνουσαν).

lines.gr: αὔραις ἡδυπνόοισι πατασσομένην περὶ γαῖαν.
lines.en: struck by sweet‑breathing breezes around the earth.
lines.note: πατασσομένην = “buffeted/struck”; περὶ γαῖαν evokes Okeanos as the earth‑encircling stream.

lines.gr: θραύουσ’ αἰγιαλο ῖσι πέτρ ηισί τε κύματα μακρά,
lines.en: shattering long waves on beaches and on the rocks,
lines.note: μακρά (“long”) of great swells; θραύειν “to shatter/break” is used of surf against αἰγιαλοί “strands” and πέτραι “rocks.”

lines.gr: εὐδινο ῖς ἁπαλο ῖσι γαληνιόωσα δρόμοισιν,
lines.en: calming her courses with gentle, well‑eddying flows,
lines.note: εὐδινός = “well‑eddying”; γαληνιόωσα “making calm”; δρόμοι “courses/ways” of waters, i.e., channels/currents.

lines.gr: νηυσὶ ν ἀγαλλομένη, θηροτρόφος, ὑ γροκέλευθε·
lines.en: rejoicing in ships, beast‑nourishing, of watery ways;
lines.note: θηροτρόφος “beast‑nourishing” (of marine life); ὑγροκέλευθε = “of watery ways/paths,” a rare epithet of sea‑deities; ἀγαλλομένη “rejoicing in, delighting in” ships.

lines.gr: μήτηρ μὲν Κύπριδος, μήτηρ νεφέων ἐρεβενν ῶν,
lines.en: mother of Kypris, mother of murky clouds,
lines.note: Kypris = Aphrodite; Orphic genealogy can make Tethys mother of Aphrodite and of clouds (cf. Tethys as mother of rivers and meteorological phenomena).

lines.gr: καὶ πάσης πηγῆς νυμφέων νασμοῖσι βρυούσης
lines.en: and of every spring, teeming with the gushing outflows of Nymphs,
lines.note: νασμός = “gushing outflow, jet” (rare); βρύουσα “teeming, swelling forth”; Nymphs as presiding over springs.

lines.gr: κλῦθί μ ου, ὦ πολύσεμνε, καὶ εὐμενέουσ’ ἐπαρήγοις,
lines.en: hear me, O much‑revered, and, being gracious, lend your aid,
lines.note: πολύσεμνε “much‑revered/august”; εὐμενέουσα “being gracious”; ἐπαρήγοις (optative) expresses a wish, “may you bring aid.”

lines.gr: εὐθυδρόμοις οὖρον νηυσὶ ν πέμπουσα, μάκαιρα.
lines.en: sending a fair wind to straight‑sailing ships, O blessed one.
lines.note: οὖρος = “fair/favorable wind”; εὐθύδρομος can modify ships or course; here taken with ships (“straight‑sailing”); the participle πέμπουσα depends on the preceding petition (“bring aid, sending …”).

lines.gr: Ὦ κατέχων πόντου ῥίζας, κυαναυγέτιν ἕδρην,
lines.en: O holder of the sea’s roots and the dark-gleaming seat,
lines.note: “roots of the sea” (πόντου ῥίζας) evokes the sea’s foundations; κυαναυγέτιν ἕδρην is a vivid compound, “dark-gleaming seat,” of the marine throne/abode.

lines.gr: πεντήκοντα κόρῃσιν ἀγαλλόμενος κατὰ κῦμα
lines.en: exulting upon the wave with fifty maidens,
lines.note: The “fifty maidens” are the Nereids, daughters of Nereus and Doris; ἀγαλλόμενος suggests triumphant exultation.

lines.gr: καλλιτέκνοισι χοροῖς, Νηρε ῦ, μεγαλώνυμε δαῖμον ·
lines.en: in their fair-born dances, O Nereus, great-named daimon,
lines.note: Vocative Νηρεῦ is textually and interpretively difficult, since the following traits (earth-shaking) suit Poseidon; some take Νηρεῦ as a periphrasis for the Sea or propose emendation. Retained here as transmitted, with Nereus standing metonymically for the marine realm.

lines.gr: πυθμ ὴν μὲν πόντου, γαίης πέρας, ἀρχὴ ἁπάντων·
lines.en: foundation of the sea, boundary of the earth, origin of all;
lines.note: πυθμήν = “foundation/base”; γαίης πέρας = “boundary of the earth”; ἀρχὴ ἁπάντων (“origin of all”) is a cosmological hyperbole, reminiscent of Oceanic motifs.

lines.gr: ὃς κλονέεις Δηοῦς ἱερὸν βάθρον, ἡνίκα πνοι ὰς
lines.en: you who shake Deo’s holy base, whenever the blasts
lines.note: Δηοῦς = Deo (Demeter). “You shake Deo’s holy base” evokes Poseidon’s Ennosichthon function (earth-shaker). ἡνίκα introduces the causal description continued in the next line.

lines.gr: ἐν μυχίοις κευθμ ῶσιν ἐλαυνομένας ἀποκλείεις
lines.en: driven in the innermost caverns you shut in,
lines.note: κευθμῶσιν = “caverns, hiding-places”; πνοιὰς … ἀποκλείεις = “you shut in the blasts/winds,” reflecting ancient physical explanations of earthquakes as winds pent up in subterranean hollows.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, σεισμοὺς μὲν ἀπότρεπε, πέμπε δὲ μύσταις
lines.en: but, blessed one, turn away earthquakes, and send to the mystai
lines.note: “μύσταις” = initiates (mystai) of the rites; a ritual petition appropriate to the Orphic hymnic context.

lines.gr: ὄλβον τ’, εἰρήνην τε, καὶ ἠπιόχειρ’ ὑγίειαν.
lines.en: prosperity and peace, and gentle-handed health.
lines.note: ἠπιόχειρ (“gentle-handed”) is an epic epithet applied here to abstract ὑγίεια (“health”).

lines.gr: Νηρέος εἰναλίου νύμφαι καλυκώπιδες ἁγναί,
lines.en: Bright-eyed, holy Nymphs of Nereus of the sea,
lines.note: καλυκώπιδες is an epithet meaning “lovely-/bright‑eyed” (perhaps from κάλυξ ‘bud’ + ὤψ ‘eye’); ἁγναί “holy, pure.”

lines.gr: φρίκιαι, ἐμβύθιαι , χοροπαίγμονες, ὑγροκέλευθοι,
lines.en: awe-inspiring, deep-immersed, playful in the dance, wayfarers of watery paths,
lines.note: φρίκιαι “awe‑inspiring, causing a shudder”; ἐμβύθιαι “deep‑immersed”; χοροπαίγμονες “frolicsome in dance”; ὑγροκέλευθοι “of watery ways/paths.”

lines.gr: πεντήκοντα κόραι περὶ κύμασι βακχεύουσαι,
lines.en: fifty maidens, Bacchic, reveling about the waves,
lines.note: πεντήκοντα recalls the traditional fifty Nereids; βακχεύουσαι “reveling like Bacchants,” anticipating the mention of Bakchos below.

lines.gr: Τριτώνων ἐπ’ ὄχοισιν ἀγαλλόμεναι περὶ νῶτα
lines.en: exulting on the Tritons’ mounts, upon their backs,
lines.note: ὄχος is “means of conveyance, mount”; περὶ νῶτα “upon the backs.” The image is of riding sea‑creatures via Tritons’ assistance.

lines.gr: θηροτύποις μορφαῖ ς, ὧ ν βόσκει σώματα πόντος·
lines.en: on beast-shaped forms, whose bodies the sea sustains;
lines.note: θηροτύποις μορφαῖς “beast‑shaped forms”; ὧν … πόντος “whose bodies the sea nourishes/sustains.” The antecedent is the sea‑beasts used as mounts (some take the phrasing as loosely appositive with the previous line).

lines.gr: ἄλλοι θ’ οἳ ναίουσι βυθόν, Τριτώνιον οἶδμα,
lines.en: and others who dwell in the deep, the Tritonian swell,
lines.note: Τριτώνιον οἶδμα “Tritonian swell/wave” (of Triton, the sea‑daimōn); not a specific toponym necessarily, but a poetic designation for the sea’s surge.

lines.gr: ὑδρόδομοι, σκιρτηταί, ἑλισσόμενοι περὶ κῦμα,
lines.en: water-dwellers, leapers, wheeling about the wave,
lines.note: ὑδρόδομοι “water‑dwellers”; σκιρτηταί “leapers”; ἑλισσόμενοι “wheeling/rolling” about the wave.

lines.gr: ποντοπλάνοι δελφῖνες, ἁλι ῤῥόθιοι , κυαναυγεῖς·
lines.en: sea-roaming dolphins, sea-roaring, dark-gleaming;
lines.note: ποντοπλάνοι “sea‑roaming”; ἁλιρρόθιοι (orthography varies) “sounding with the sea’s roar”; κυαναυγεῖς “dark-/deep‑blue‑gleaming.”

lines.gr: ὑμέας κικλήσκω πέμπειν μύσταις πολὺν ὄλβον ·
lines.en: you I invoke to send much blessedness to the initiates;
lines.note: ὑμέας is epic/Doric for ὑμᾶς; μύσται “initiates”; ὄλβος “blessed prosperity.”

lines.gr: ὑμεῖς γὰρ πρ ῶται τελετὴν ἀνεδείξατε σεμνὴν
lines.en: for you first revealed the august rite
lines.note: τελετή “rite, initiation”; σεμνή “august, venerable.” The Nereids are credited aetiologically with revealing the mysteries.

lines.gr: εὐϊέρου Βάκχοιο καὶ ἁγν ῆς Φερσεφονείης,
lines.en: of well-hallowed Bakchos and holy Phersēphonē,
lines.note: εὐϊερός here rendered “well‑hallowed.” Bakchos and Phersēphonē (an archaic form of Persephonē) are central Orphic deities.

lines.gr: Καλλιόπ ῃ σὺν μητρὶ καὶ Ἀπόλλωνι ἄνακτι.
lines.en: together with mother Kalliopē and lord Apollōn.
lines.note: “mother Kalliopē” refers to Orpheus’ mother; ἄναξ “lord” for Apollōn, both regularly associated with Orphic tradition.

lines.gr: Πρωτέα κικλήσκω, πόντου κλη ῗδας ἔχοντα,
lines.en: I call upon Proteus, holding the keys of the sea,
lines.note: πόντου κλεῖδας ἔχοντα: “holding the keys of the sea.” Manuscripts vary between κλεῖδας/κληΐδας; the sense is ‘keys,’ a ritual image of lordship/guardianship. κικλήσκω is a formal invocatory verb (“I call upon”).

lines.gr: πρωτογεν ῆ, πάσης φύσεως ἀρχ ὰς ὃς ἔφηνεν,
lines.en: first-born, who made manifest the principles of all Nature,
lines.note: πρωτογενής = “first-born/primordial.” ἀρχάς here means both “beginnings” and “principles,” fitting Orphic cosmogony. ἔφηνεν (“made manifest, revealed”) rather than merely “said.”

lines.gr: ὕλην ἀλλάσσων ἱερὴν ἰδέαις πολυμόρφοις,
lines.en: transmuting holy matter by many-formed ideas,
lines.note: ὕλη = “matter,” ἰδέαι = “forms/ideas” (with philosophical resonance); πολυμόρφοις evokes Proteus’ shapeshifting and the multiplicity of forms imposed upon matter.

lines.gr: πάντιμος, πολύβουλος, ἐπιστάμενος τά τ’ ἐόντα,
lines.en: worthy of all honor, of much counsel, knowing the things that are,
lines.note: πάντιμος “worthy of all honor”; πολύβουλος “of much counsel, very wise.” ἐόντα is Ionic for “the things that are.”

lines.gr: ὅσσα τε πρόσθεν ἔην, ὅ σα τ’ ἔσσεται ὕστερον α ὖτις ·
lines.en: all that was before and all that shall be hereafter again;
lines.note: πρόσθεν ἦν = “was before”; ἔσσεται = “will be”; αὖτις adds “again/anew,” emphasizing cyclical or repeated revelation of time.

lines.gr: πάντα γὰρ ἐν Πρωτε ῖ πρώτη φύσις ἐγκατέθηκεν.
lines.en: for in Proteus Primordial Nature has deposited all things.
lines.note: πρώτη φύσις “Primordial Nature” (an Orphic cosmological notion). ἐγκατέθηκεν = “deposited/placed within,” suggesting Proteus as repository of total reality.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, πάτερ, μόλε μυστιπόλοις ὁσίῃσι προνοίαις,
lines.en: But, Father, come to the mystic ministers with holy providences,
lines.note: μυστιπόλοις = “mystic ministers/attendants” (cf. variant μυστοπόλοις). μόλε is the aorist imperative “come!” πρόνοια (“forethought/providence”) can be personified; the dative expresses attendant means: “with holy providences.”

lines.gr: πέμπων εὐόλβου βιότου τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἐπ’ ἔργοις.
lines.en: sending forth upon our works the good fulfillment of a prosperous life.
lines.note: εὐόλβου βιότου = “of prosperous/blessed life.” τέλος = “end/fulfillment/consummation.” ἐπ’ ἔργοις = “upon/with regard to our works, undertakings.” The participle πέμπων (“sending forth”) depends on the imperative μόλε in the previous line.

hymns.title: Γῆς
hymns.incense: πᾶν σπέρμα, πλὴν κυάμων καὶ ἀρωμάτων

lines.gr: Γαῖα θεά, μ ῆτερ μακάρων, θνητῶν τ’ ἀνθρώπων,
lines.en: Gaia, goddess, mother of the blessed and of mortal humans,
lines.note: “the blessed” (makarōn) conventionally means “the blessed gods”; the noun “gods” is understood from context.

lines.gr: πάντροφε, πανδώτειρα, τελεσφόρε, παντολέτειρα,
lines.en: all‑nourishing, all‑giving, bringer‑to‑fulfillment, all‑destroying,
lines.note: telesphore is “bringer to completion/fulfillment” (also with ritual nuance of initiation); pantoleteira is “destroyer of all,” marking Earth’s ambivalent power to both nurture and undo.

lines.gr: αὐξιθαλής, φερέκαρπε, καλαῖς ὥρῃσι βρύουσα·
lines.en: growth‑fostering, fruit‑bearing, teeming with fair seasons;
lines.note: auxithalēs is an epithet “fostering growth”; bryein “to swell/teem,” here of seasonal abundance.

lines.gr: ἕδρανον ἀθανάτου κόσμου, πολυποίκιλε κούρη,
lines.en: foundation of the deathless cosmos, many‑patterned maiden,
lines.note: hedranon is “seat/foundation”; polupoikilos “variegated, richly wrought”; kourē (“maiden”) is an honorific for goddesses, not a literal age marker.

lines.gr: ἣ λοχίαις ὠδῖσι κύεις καρπὸν πολυειδῆ·
lines.en: you who with labor‑pangs bear manifold fruit;
lines.note: lochiais ōdisi kueis mixes conception and birth imagery for fecundity; polueidēs “of many kinds/forms.”

lines.gr: ἀϊδίη , πολύσεπτε, βαθύστερν’, ὀλβιόμοιρε,
lines.en: eternal, much‑revered, deep‑bosomed, blessed in lot,
lines.note: aidiē “eternal,” poluseptos “much‑revered,” bathusternē “deep‑bosomed,” olbiomoiros “of blessed lot/portion.”

lines.gr: ἡδυπνόοις χαίρουσα χλόαις, πολυάνθεμε δα ῖμον ·
lines.en: rejoicing in sweet‑breathing grasses, many‑flowered daimon,
lines.note: daimon is left transliterated to retain the Greek category of divine agency; hēdupnoos “sweet‑breathing” evokes the fragrance/liveliness of meadows.

lines.gr: ὀμβροχαρής, περὶ τ ὴν κόσμος πολυδαίδαλος ἄστρων
lines.en: rain‑delighting, around you the much‑wrought adornment of the stars
lines.note: ombrocharēs “glad in rain”; peri tēn “around you” (accusative of the goddess); some editions read peri se/setzen; kosmos here “adornment/order,” poludaidalos “much‑wrought.”

lines.gr: εἱλε ῖται φύσει ἀενά ῳ καὶ ῥ εύμασι δεινοῖς.
lines.en: is wound by everlasting nature and by dread currents.
lines.note: heileitai “is wound/enwrapped”; physei aenaōi “by everlasting nature”; rheumasi deinois “by dread streams/currents,” often taken of cosmic flows (ether/Ocean).

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαιρα θεὰ, καρποὺς α ὔξοις πολυγηθεῖς,
lines.en: But do you, blessed goddess, increase fruits that bring much rejoicing,
lines.note: alla marks the hymnic turn to prayer; the optative auxois expresses wish; polygētheis “much‑gladdening,” of the fruits granted.

lines.gr: εὐμενὲς ἦτορ ἔχουσα, σὺν ὀλβί οισιν ἐν ὥραις.
lines.en: keeping a gracious heart, together with prosperous seasons.
lines.note: eumenes hētor “kindly heart”; syn olbioisin en hōrais “together with prosperous seasons,” i.e., grant abundance with good timing/seasons.

hymns.title: Μητρὸς θεῶν

lines.gr: Ἀθανάτων θεότιμε θεῶν μ ῆτερ, τροφ ὲ πάντων,
lines.en: Mother of the immortal gods, honored among the gods, nurse of all,
lines.note: θεότιμε = “honored by the gods.” The line addresses the Great Mother as both mother of the gods and universal nurse.

lines.gr: τῇιδε μόλοις κράντειρα θεά, σέο, πότνι’, ἐπ’ εὐχαῖς,
lines.en: come hither, ordaining goddess—Lady—to our prayers,
lines.note: τῇδε μόλοις = “come hither” (aorist of βλώσκω used imperatively). κράντειρα = “she who brings to pass/ordains.” The transmitted σέο (gen.) is formulaic and awkward in English; I render the sense “to our prayers.”

lines.gr: ταυροφόνων ζεύξασα ταχύδρομον ἅρμα λεόντων,
lines.en: having yoked the swift-running chariot of bull-slaying lions,
lines.note: ταυροφόνων λεόντων = the lions that slay bulls, a Cybele/Rhea topos; the goddess’ car is drawn by lions.

lines.gr: σκηπτο ῦχε κλεινο ῖο πόλου, πολυώνυμε, σεμνή·
lines.en: sceptre-bearer of the renowned vault of heaven, much-named, august;
lines.note: πόλος (“vault/pole”) here = the sky; thus “renowned vault of heaven.” σκηπτοῦχος = “sceptre-bearer.”

lines.gr: ἣ κατέχεις κόσμοιο μέσον θρόνον, οὕνεκεν α ὐτὴ
lines.en: you who hold the middle throne of the world, for you yourself
lines.note: κόσμοιο is the Homeric genitive of κόσμος (“ordered world”). “Middle throne” evokes a cosmic, central sovereignty.

lines.gr: γαῖαν ἔχεις, θνητοῖσι τροφὰ ς παρέχουσα προσηνεῖς.
lines.en: possess the earth, graciously providing sustenance to mortals.
lines.note: προσηνεῖς qualifies τροφάς: “kindly/gracious” sustenance supplied to mortals.

lines.gr: ἐκ σέο δ’ ἀθανάτων τε γένος θνητῶν τ’ ἐλοχεύθη ·
lines.en: From you the race of immortals and of mortals was brought to birth,
lines.note: ἐλοχεύθη (aor. pass. of λοχεύω) = “was delivered/brought to birth,” stressing the goddess as generative source of gods and humans.

lines.gr: σοὶ ποταμο ὶ κρατέονται ἀεὶ καὶ πᾶσα θάλασσα·
lines.en: by you the rivers are ever held in your power, and the whole sea.
lines.note: κρατέονται with dat. of agent (σοί) = “are held in your power/are ruled.” The waters (rivers, sea) are subject to the Mother’s dominion.

lines.gr: Ἱσίη αὐδαχθε ῖσα σὲ δ’ ὀλβοδότιν καλέουσιν,
lines.en: when invoked as Isie, they call you giver of prosperity,
lines.note: Ἱσίη is a syncretic epithet identifying the goddess with Isis; αὐδαχθεῖσα = “when invoked/addressed.” ὀλβοδότιν = “wealth-/blessing-giving.”

lines.gr: παντοίων ἀγαθῶ ν θνητο ῖς ὅτι δ ῶρα χαρίζ ῃ.
lines.en: since to mortals you bestow the gifts of every sort of good.
lines.note: Formulaic praise: παντοίων ἀγαθῶν = “of every kind of good.”

lines.gr: ἔρχεο πρ ὸς τελετήν, ὦ πότνια, τυμπανοτερπής,
lines.en: Come to the rite, Lady, delighting in the drum,
lines.note: τελετή = “rite/initiatory rite.” τυμπανοτερπής = “delighting in the drum,” a hallmark of Phrygian/Cybele cult.

lines.gr: πανδαμάτωρ, Φρυγίης, σώτειρα, Κρόνου συνόμευνε,
lines.en: all-subduing, of Phrygia, Saviour, consort of Kronos,
lines.note: πανδαμάτωρ = “all-subduing.” Φρυγίης = “of Phrygia/Phrygian.” σώτειρα = “Saviour.” συνόμευνε = “bedfellow/consort” (lit. “sharing the bed”) of Kronos.

lines.gr: Οὐρανόπαι, πρέσβειρα, βιοθρέπτειρα, φίλοιστρε
lines.en: child of Ouranos, eldest one, life-nourisher, friendly to your faithful,
lines.note: Οὐρανόπαι (for Οὐρανόπαις) = “child of Ouranos.” πρέσβειρα can mean “eldest/venerable.” βιοθρέπτειρα = “life-nourisher.” The transmitted φίλοιστρε— is defective; I render the sense “friendly to your faithful” to suit the cultic context.

lines.gr: ἔρχεο γηθόσυνος, κεχαρημένη εὐσεβί ῃσιν.
lines.en: come rejoicing, gladdened by deeds of piety.
lines.note: εὐσεβίῃσιν (dat. pl.) = “pieties/acts of devotion.” κεχαρημένη = “gladdened/delighted,” fitting the epiphanic invitation to attend the rite.

hymns.title_english: To the Mother of the Gods

lines.gr: Κλῦθί μευ, Ἑρμεία, Δι ὸς ἄγγελε, Μαιάδος υἱέ,
lines.en: Hear me, Hermeia, messenger of Zeus, son of Maia,
lines.note: Ἑρμεία is a vocative form used in the Orphic Hymns; “messenger of Zeus” and “son of Maia” are standard Hermes-identifications.

lines.gr: παγκρατ ὲς ἦτορ ἔχων, ἐναγώνιε, κοίρανε θνητῶν,
lines.en: possessing an all-powerful heart, presider over contests, lord of mortals,
lines.note: ἐναγώνιος = ‘of/at the contests,’ i.e., patron of the ἀγῶνες (athletic and civic); παγκρατές ἦτορ ‘all-powerful heart’ is a traditional exalted epithet.

lines.gr: εὔφρων, ποικιλόβουλε, διάκτορος, Ἀργειφόντα,
lines.en: kindly, of wily counsel, Diaktoros, Argeiphontes,
lines.note: ποικιλόβουλος ‘of various/cunning counsel’; Diaktoros (‘Guide/Conductor’) and Argeiphontes (‘Slayer of Argos [Panoptes]’) are traditional epithets retained in transliteration.

lines.gr: πτηνοπέδιλε, φίλανδρε, λόγου θνητοῖσι προφ ῆτα·
lines.en: wing-sandaled, lover of humankind, interpreter of speech for mortals;
lines.note: πτηνοπέδιλος ‘wing-sandaled’ alludes to the talaria; φίλανδρος here means ‘friendly to men/humankind,’ not erotic; προφήτης in early sense ‘interpreter’ rather than ‘seer.’

lines.gr: γυμνάσιν ὃς χαίρεις, δολίαις τ’ ἀπάταις,
lines.en: you who take delight in gymnasia and in crafty deceits,
lines.note: γυμνάσια are the athletic training-grounds; δολίαι ἀπάται emphasizes Hermes’ trickster craft.

lines.gr: (στρ)οφιο ῦχε·
lines.en: wearer of the fillet,
lines.note: (στρ)οφιοῦχε is textually uncertain; most print στροφιοῦχε ‘wearer of the fillet/band’ (στρόφιον = band, girdle, headband). Some have connected it with Hermes’ accoutrements; the epithet is rare and possibly corrupt.

lines.gr: ἑρμηνε ῦ πάντων, κερδέμπορε, λυσιμέριμνε·
lines.en: interpreter of all things, broker of gain, reliever of cares;
lines.note: ἑρμηνεύς ‘interpreter’ plays on Hermes’ name; κερδέμπορος ‘dealer/merchant in profit’ with mercantile nuance; λυσιμέριμνος ‘reliever of cares.’

lines.gr: ὃς χείρεσσιν ἔχεις εἰ ρήνης ὅπλον ἀμεμφές ·
lines.en: who in your hands hold the blameless weapon of peace;
lines.note: The ‘blameless weapon of peace’ refers to the kerykeion (caduceus), emblem of truce and mediation.

lines.gr: Κωρυκι ῶτα, μάκαρ, ἐριούνιε, ποικιλόμυθε,
lines.en: Korykiotes, blessed one, Eriounios, weaver of varied speech,
lines.note: Κωρυκιώτα = ‘dweller of the Korykian [cave],’ a cultic epithet; Ἐριούνιος (Eriounios) is a traditional, probably ‘beneficent/lucky’ epithet; ποικιλόμυθος ‘varied/versatile in speech.’

lines.gr: ἐργασίαις ἐπαρωγέ, φίλε θνητοῖς ἐν ἀνάγκαις ·
lines.en: helper in labors, dear to mortals in their necessities;
lines.note: ἐπαρωγός ‘helper/ally’; ἐν ἀνάγκαις ‘in times of necessity/need.’

lines.gr: γλώσσης δεινὸν ὅπλον, τὸ σεβάσμιον ἀνθρώπ οισιν ·
lines.en: formidable weapon of the tongue, that which is august among men;
lines.note: Appositional vocative: Hermes as the ‘formidable weapon of the tongue,’ i.e., the power of eloquence; σεβάσμιος ‘august, venerable’ of what commands reverence among mortals.

lines.gr: κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, βιότου τέλος ἐσθλὸν ὀπάζων,
lines.en: hear me as I pray, granting a noble end of life,
lines.note: ὀπάζειν ‘to grant/bestow’; βιότου τέλος ἐσθλόν ‘a good/noble end of life’ points to a blessed death.

lines.gr: ἐργασί ῃσι, λόγου χάρισιν, καὶ μνημοσύνῃσιν.
lines.en: with industry, with the graces of speech, and with remembrances.
lines.note: The plural datives are instrumental: ‘with/through industry (ἐργασίῃσι), the graces of speech (λόγου χάρισιν), and acts of memory (μνημοσύνῃσιν).’ Some hear an echo of Mnēmosynē, but the plural here denotes faculties/instances.

lines.gr: Περσεφόνη, θύγατερ μεγάλου Διός, ἐλθέ, μάκαιρα,
lines.en: Persephonē, daughter of great Zeus, come, blessed one,

lines.gr: μουνογένεια θεά, κεχαρισμένα δ’ ἱερὰ δέξαι ·
lines.en: only-begotten goddess, and accept these pleasing sacred offerings;
lines.note: μουνογένεια (“only-begotten”) is an Orphic title stressing unique birth/status; ἱερά here suits “offerings” given the verb δέξαι (“receive”).

lines.gr: Πλούτωνος πολύτιμε δάμαρ, κεδνή, βιοδῶτι·
lines.en: most precious wife of Plouton, provident, life-giving;
lines.note: κεδνή = “prudent/provident”; βιοδῶτι (“life-/livelihood-giving”) highlights Persephonē’s role in agricultural sustenance.

lines.gr: ἣ κατέχεις Ἀΐδαο πύλας ὑπὸ κεύθεα γαίης,
lines.en: you who hold the gates of Aïdēs beneath the depths of earth,
lines.note: Ἀΐδης is transliterated Aïdēs; κατέχεις (“you hold/command”) underscores control of the underworld gates.

lines.gr: Πραξιδίκη, ἐρατοπλόκαμος, Δηο ῦς θάλος ἁγνόν,
lines.en: Praxidikē, lovely-tressed, holy blossom of Deo,
lines.note: Πραξιδίκη (“Executrix/Avenger of Justice”) is an epithet; Δηοῦς θάλος = “Deo’s (Demeter’s) shoot/bloom,” a metaphor for filial offshoot.

lines.gr: Εὐμενίδων γενέτειρα, καταχθονίων βασ ίλεια ·
lines.en: mother of the Eumenides, queen of those beneath the earth;
lines.note: Εὐμενίδες (“Kindly Ones,” i.e., Erinyes) as her offspring reflects Orphic/variant genealogies; καταχθόνιοι = “those beneath the earth.”

lines.gr: ἣν Ζε ὺς ἀῤῥήτοισι γονα ῖς τεκνώσατο κούρην.
lines.en: whom Zeus sired as a maiden by ineffable begettings.
lines.note: ἀρρήτοισι γοναῖς (“unspeakable begettings”) evokes mystic/ineffable unions; the line affirms her as Zeus’s daughter (cf. line 1).

lines.gr: μῆτερ ἐριβρεμέτου πολυμόρφου Εὐβουλ ῆος,
lines.en: mother of loud-thundering, many-formed Eubouleus,
lines.note: Εὐβουλεύς/Eubouleus in Orphic context often denotes chthonic Dionysus (Zagreus), “many-formed”; ἐριβρέμετος (“loud-thundering”) echoes Zeus/Dionysiac power.

lines.gr: Ὡρ ῶν συμπαίκτειρα, φαεσφόρος, ἀγλαόμορφε·
lines.en: playmate of the Horai, light-bearing, splendid in form;
lines.note: Ὧραι (Horai = Seasons) as companions recall meadow scenes and seasonal cycles; φαεσφόρος = “light-bearing.”

lines.gr: σεμνή, παντοκράτειρα, κόρη καρποῖσι βρύουσα,
lines.en: august, all-sovereign, maiden abounding in fruits,
lines.note: παντοκράτειρα = “all-sovereign/almighty,” a high cultic title; βρύουσα = “teeming/abounding.”

lines.gr: εὐφεγγής, κερόεσσα, μόνη θνητοῖσι ποθεινή,
lines.en: bright-beaming, horned, the only one longed-for by mortals,
lines.note: κερόεσσα most naturally “horned,” likely a lunar/chthonic syncretism; μόνη θνητοῖσι ποθεινή = “alone desired by mortals,” i.e., universally longed-for.

lines.gr: ἐαρινή, λειμωνιάσιν χαίρουσα πνο ῇσιν,
lines.en: of springtime, rejoicing in the meadow-breezes,
lines.note: λειμωνιάσιν πνοαῖς = “meadow-breezes,” evoking spring renewal associated with Kore’s return.

lines.gr: ἱερὸν ἐκφαίνουσα δέμας βλαστοῖς χλοοκάρποις,
lines.en: revealing your holy form in green-fruited shoots,
lines.note: χλοοκάρποις (“green-fruited/grass-fruited”) is a vivid compound for fresh shoots; ἐκφαίνουσα = “making manifest.”

lines.gr: ἁρπαγιμαῖ α λέχη μετοπωρινὰ νυμφευθεῖσα·
lines.en: having been wedded to an autumnal bed won by abduction;
lines.note: ἁρπαγιμαῖα (“won by abduction/rape”) refers to Hades’ seizure; μετοπωρινά (“autumnal”) ties the nuptials to harvest season in agrarian myth.

lines.gr: ζωὴ καὶ θάνατος μούνη θνητοῖς πολυμόχθοις,
lines.en: you alone are life and death for much-enduring mortals,
lines.note: The predication “you alone are life and death” encapsulates Orphic polarity: Persephonē governs both fertility and mortality.

lines.gr: Φερσεφόνεια· φέρ βεις γὰρ ἀεὶ καὶ πάντα φονεύεις.
lines.en: Phersēphoneia: for you ever nourish and you slay all.
lines.note: Φερσεφόνεια is a variant form of the name; φέρβω = “to nourish/feed,” contrasted with φονεύω “to slay.”

lines.gr: κλῦθι μάκαιρα θεά, καρποὺς δ’ ἀνάπεμπ' ἀπὸ γαίης,
lines.en: Hear, blessed goddess, and send up fruits from the earth,
lines.note: ἀνάπεμπε (“send up”) is a technical cultic verb for bringing crops forth from below.

lines.gr: εἰρήνῃ θάλλουσα καὶ ἠπιόχειρ’ ὑγείῃ,
lines.en: flourishing in peace and in gentle-handed health,
lines.note: ἠπιόχειρ (“gentle-handed”) is a hymnic epithet of beneficent power; phrase expresses prosperity conditions.

lines.gr: καὶ βίῳ εὐόλβῳ, λιπαρὸν γ ῆρας κατάγοντι
lines.en: and with a well-blest life bringing a prosperous old age
lines.note: λιπαρόν γῆρας literally “sleek/oily” old age, idiomatically “prosperous/comfortable” old age; κατάγοντι “bringing down” (sc. life).

lines.gr: πρὸς σὸν χῶρον, ἄνασσα, καὶ εὐδύνατον Πλούτωνα.
lines.en: down to your realm, Lady, and to mighty Plouton.
lines.note: εὐδύνατον (“mighty, of goodly power”) of Plouton; πρὸς σὸν χῶρον signals a prayer for a natural descent to her realm in due old age.

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω Διόνυσον ἐρίβρομον, εὐαστῆ ρα,
lines.en: I call upon Dionysos, loud-roaring, the euas-crier,
lines.note: εὐαστῆρα refers to the Bacchic cry euai; ἐρίβρομος is a standard Dionysiac epithet “loud-roaring.” The spacing in the source (εὐαστῆ ρα) is a typographical artifact.

lines.gr: πρωτόγονον, διφυῆ, τρίγονον, Βακχεῖον ἄνακτα,
lines.en: first-born, two-natured, thrice-born, Baccheian lord,
lines.note: πρωτόγονος, διφυής, τρίγονος are Orphic descriptors: “first-born,” “two-natured” (often androgynous or dual—Olympian/chthonic), and “thrice-born” (alluding to Dionysiac rebirths). “Βακχεῖος” means “Bacchic.”

lines.gr: ἄγριον, ἄρρητον, κρύφιον, δικέρωτα, δίμορφον,
lines.en: wild, ineffable, secret, two-horned, double-formed,
lines.note: ἄρρητος (“ineffable”) and κρύφιος (“secret”) mark mystery-cult reserve; δικέρωτος (“two-horned”) evokes Dionysos’ bull-aspect; δίμορφος (“double-formed”) underscores his duality.

lines.gr: κισσόβρυον, ταυρωπόν, ἀρήϊον, ε ὔϊον, ἁ γνόν,
lines.en: ivy-springing, bull-eyed, warlike, Euios, holy,
lines.note: κισσόβρυος = “ivy-springing” (ivy as his plant); ταυρωπός literally “bull-eyed”; ἀρήϊος “warlike”; εὔϊος is an epithet from the cry euoi; ἁγνός “holy/pure.”

lines.gr: ὠμάδιον, τριετῆ, βοτρυοτρὸφον, ἐ ρνεσίπεπλον.
lines.en: raw-flesh-eating, of the trieteric rites, cluster-nurturing, clad in a shoot-woven robe.
lines.note: ὠμάδιος is the cult title “raw-flesh-eating” (Omadios); τριετής refers to the trieteric festival cycles; βοτρυοτρόφος “nurturing the grape-cluster”; ἐρνεσίπεπλον (“clad in shoots,” from ἔρνος “shoot”) likely evokes vine/ivy garb; the compound varies in manuscripts.

lines.gr: Εὐβουλεῦ, πολύβουλε, Διὸς καὶ Περσεφονείης
lines.en: Eubouleus, Much-Counseling, of Zeus and Persephone,
lines.note: Εὐβουλεύς (“Good-Counsellor,” here as a proper title Eubouleus) and πολύβουλος (“much-counseling”) are chthonic/intellectual epithets; the parentage from Zeus and Persephone reflects the Orphic Zagreus tradition.

lines.gr: ἀρρήτοις λέκτροισι τεκνωθείς, ἄμβροτε δαῖμον ·
lines.en: begotten in unspeakable bridal-beds, immortal daimon,
lines.note: ἀρρήτοις λέκτροισι (“in unspeakable beds”) signals mystic secrecy; ἄμβροτε δαῖμον = “immortal daimon,” a standard cultic address.

lines.gr: κλῦθι μάκαρ φωνῆς, ἡ δὺς δ’ ἐπίπνευσον ἐνηής,
lines.en: hear, O blessed one, my voice, and breathe gently with kindly favor,
lines.note: The source’s ἡ δὺς is to be read ἥδυς (“sweet”); ἐπίπνευσον “breathe upon” means “grant a favor/influence,” with ἐνηής “kindly, gracious.”

lines.gr: εὐμενὲς ἦτορ ἔχων, σὺν ἐυζώνοισι τιθήναις.
lines.en: holding a gracious heart, together with the well-girdled nurses.
lines.note: εὐζώνους τιθῆναι (“well-girdled nurses”) are the Nymphs who reared Dionysos; the phrase is traditional and formulaic.

lines.gr: Σκιρτητα ὶ Κουρ ῆτες, ἐνόπλια βήματα θέντες,
lines.en: Leaping Kourêtes, setting warlike steps,
lines.note: Σκιρτηταί (“leaping”) evokes the Kourêtes’ war‑dance; ἐνόπλια (“warlike/armed”) qualifies their steps. Spacing in the supplied text is faulty; read Σκιρτηταί Κουρῆτες.

lines.gr: ποσσίκροτοι, ῥομβηταί, ὀρέστεροι, εὐαστῆ ρες,
lines.en: foot‑clattering, whirrers, mountain‑ranging, euai‑criers,
lines.note: Ῥομβηταί refers to the ritual ῥόμβος (bull‑roarer/whirring instrument); εὐαστῆρες are those who cry “euai,” the Bacchic acclamation.

lines.gr: κρουσιλύραι, παράρυθμοι, ἐπεμβάται ἴχνεσι κούφοις,
lines.en: lyre‑strikers, off the beat, stepping in with light tracks,
lines.note: κρουσιλύραι likely = “lyre‑strikers”; many editors read κρουσιλύροι. παράρυθμοι = “off‑beat/syncopated,” and ἐπεμβάται ἴχνεσι κούφοις = “on‑steppers with light footprints,” i.e., light‑footed dancers/assailants.

lines.gr: ὁπλοφόροι, φύλακες, κοσμήτορες, ἀγλαόφημοι,
lines.en: arm‑bearing, guardians, marshals, brightly‑famed,

lines.gr: μητρ ὸς ὀρειμανέος συνοπάονες, ὀργιοφάνται,
lines.en: attendants of the mountain‑mad Mother, revealers of the orgia,
lines.note: The “Mother” is the mountain‑ranging Meter (Rhea/Cybele); ὀργιοφάνται = “revealers of the orgia,” i.e., mystic rites.

lines.gr: ἔλθοιτ’ εὐμενέοντες ἐπ’ εὐφήμοισι λόγοισιν,
lines.en: come in goodwill upon words of good omen,
lines.note: εὐφήμοις λόγοις (“words of good omen”) is a standard cultic formula marking auspicious, ritually proper speech.

lines.gr: βουκόλῳ εὐάντητοι ἀεὶ κεχαρηότι θυμ ῳ.
lines.en: be propitious to the herdsman, with an ever‑rejoicing heart.
lines.note: βουκόλος (“herdsman”) is likely the officiant/poet (or evokes the pastoral setting of Zeus’ infancy guarded by the Kourêtes); εὐάντητοι = “propitious/meeting kindly.”

lines.gr: Παλλ ὰς μουνογενής, μεγάλου Διὸς ἔκγονε σεμνή,
lines.en: Pallas, only-begotten, august offspring of great Zeus,
lines.note: μουνογενής “only-begotten” is apt for Athena as born from Zeus alone; σεμνή = “august, venerable.”

lines.gr: δῖα μάκαιρα θεά, πολεμοκλόνος, ὀ μβριμόθυμε,
lines.en: divine, blessed goddess, stirrer of war’s tumult, vehement of heart,
lines.note: πολεμοκλόνος “stirring the din of battle”; ὀμβριμόθυμος “vehement/impetuous of spirit.”

lines.gr: [Ἄῤῥ ητ’, εὐρήτη, μεγαλώνυμος, ἀντροδίαιτε·
lines.en: [Ineffable, discoverer, great-named, cave-dwelling,]
lines.note: Bracketed lines (3–5) are widely suspected as interpolations; ἀντροδίαιτος “cave-dwelling” especially ill suits Athena.

lines.gr: ἥ τε δια ΐσσεις ὑψαυχένας ἀκρωρείας,
lines.en: [you who dart through the high-necked mountain ridges,]
lines.note: ὑψαυχένας ἀκρωρείας = “lofty-necked peaks”; διαΐσσω “to dart/rush through.”

lines.gr: ἠδ’ ὄρεα σκιόεντα, νάπ ῃσί τε σὴ ν φρένα τέρπεις.]
lines.en: [and the shadowy mountains, and in the glens you delight your mind.]
lines.note: νάπη “wooded vale, glen.”

lines.gr: ὁπλοχαρής, οἰστρο ῦσα βροτ ῶν ψυχ ὰς μανί ῃσιν·
lines.en: delighting in arms, goading mortals’ souls to frenzies,
lines.note: ὁπλοχαρής “delighting in arms”; οἰστροῦσα “goading (like a gadfly),” hence “driving into frenzy,” here martial ardor (μανίαι).

lines.gr: γυμνάζουσα κόρη. φρικώδεα θυμ ὸν ἔχουσα.
lines.en: a maiden who trains, possessing a spirit that makes one shudder,
lines.note: γυμνάζουσα may mean “training/drilling” (not “making naked”)—Athena as disciplinarian; φρικώδης “awe-/shudder-inducing.”

lines.gr: Γοργοφόνος, φυγόλεκτρε, τεχνῶν μ ῆτερ πολύολβε.
lines.en: Gorgon-slayer, bed-shunning, richly-blest mother of crafts,
lines.note: Γοργοφόνος “Gorgon-slayer” attributes Medusa’s defeat to Athena’s agency; φυγόλεκτρος “shunning the bed” = virgin; μήτηρ τεχνῶν “mother of crafts.”

lines.gr: ὁρμάστειρα, φίλοιστρε κακοῖς, ἀγαθο ῖς δὲ φρόνησις.
lines.en: impeller, lover of the loom, a foe to the wicked but prudence for the good,
lines.note: ὁρμάστειρα “she who sets in motion/impels”; φίλοιστρε = “fond of the loom” (from ἱστός), fitting Athena; “a foe to the wicked, but prudence for the good” supplies the implied predication with the datives.

lines.gr: ἄρσην μὲν καὶ θῆλυς ἔφυς, πολεμήτοκε μῆτι.
lines.en: you were born both male and female, war-begetting counsel,
lines.note: “Born both male and female” expresses Athena’s androgynous blend of martial and maidenly traits; πολεμήτοκε μῆτι = “war-begetting counsel,” with μῆτις alluding to Mētis, Athena’s inherited cunning.

lines.gr: αἰολόμορφε, δράκαινα, φιλένθεος, ἀγλαότιμε ·
lines.en: changeful in form, serpentess, god-loving, gloriously honored,
lines.note: αἰολόμορφος “of changeful form”; δράκαινα “serpentess” (aegis/Erichthonius symbolism); φιλένθεος likely “god-loving” (the epithet is textually uncertain in some traditions).

lines.gr: Φλεγραίων ὀλέτειρα γιγάντων, ἱππελάτειρα.
lines.en: destroyer of the Phlegraean Giants, horse-driver,
lines.note: Φλεγραῖοι Γίγαντες = Giants of Phlegra in the Gigantomachy; ἱππελάτειρα “horse-driver/rider.”

lines.gr: Τριτογένεια, λύτειρα κακῶν, νικηφόρε δαῖμον,
lines.en: Tritogeneia, releaser from evils, victory-bringing daimon,
lines.note: Τριτογένεια retained as traditional epithet; δαίμων here “divinity,” not “demon.”

lines.gr: γλαυκῶ φ’, ε ὑρεσίτεχνε, πολυλλίστη βασίλεια
lines.en: bright-eyed, inventor of arts, much-invoked queen,
lines.note: γλαυκῶπις = “bright-eyed”; εὑρεσίτεχνος “inventive/discoverer of arts”; πολυλλίστη “much-invoked, much-entreated.”

lines.gr: ἤματα καὶ νύκτας αἰεὶ νεάται σιν ἐν ὥραις,
lines.en: by days and nights always, at the new-turning seasons,
lines.note: νεάταις ἐν ὥραις is difficult: likely “at the new-turning (renewed) seasons/hours,” perhaps with calendrical nuance (new/last day of the month).

lines.gr: κλῦθί μευ εὐ χομένου, δὸς δ’ εἰρήνην πολύολβον,
lines.en: hear me praying, and grant much-blest peace,

lines.gr: καὶ κόρην ἠδ’ ὑγίειανἐπ’ εὐόλβοισιν ἐν ὥραις.
lines.en: and maidenhood and health in well-prospering seasons.
lines.note: κόρη may mean “maidenhood (chastity)” or “a daughter”; the prayer suits Athena as patroness of maidens; εὐόλβοι ὧραι = “prosperous/blest seasons.”

lines.gr: Εὐδύνατον καλέω Νίκην, θνητοῖσι ποθεινήν,
lines.en: I call upon the Well-Potent Nikē, longed-for by mortals,
lines.note: Εὐδύνατος (“well-powered, potent”): rendered as “Well-Potent” to preserve the cultic epithet; ποθεινήν = “longed-for.”

lines.gr: ἣ μούνη λύει θνητῶν ἐναγώνιον ὁρμήν,
lines.en: who alone loosens the agonistic impulse of mortals,
lines.note: ἐναγώνιος ὁρμή (“agonistic impulse”) evokes the drive of the contest/arena; λύει (“loosens”) indicates release/cessation.

lines.gr: καὶ στάσιν ἀλγινόεσσαν, ἐπ’ ἀντιπάλοισι μάχῃσιν
lines.en: and grievous faction, in counter-matched combats,
lines.note: στάσις ἀλγινόεσσα = “painful/grievous strife,” often civil discord; ἐπ’ ἀντιπάλοισι (“in counter-matched”) echoes wrestling/combat; construction continues with κρίνουσα in the next line.

lines.gr: ἐν πολέμοις κρίνουσα, τροπαιούχοισιν ἐπ’ ἔργοις,
lines.en: adjudicating in wars, over trophy-winning deeds,
lines.note: κρίνουσα = “adjudicating/deciding” the outcome; τροπαιούχοισιν ἔργοις literally “trophy-holding deeds,” hence “trophy-winning deeds.”

lines.gr: οἷς ἂν ἐφορμαίνουσα φέρ ῃς γλυκερώτατον εὖχος.
lines.en: for those whom, when you rouse them, you bring the sweetest boast.
lines.note: ἐφορμαίνουσα = “stirring/rousing”; εὖχος can mean “boast” or “prayer/vow”; in martial-victory context “boast” fits best (“the sweetest boast”).

lines.gr: πάντων γὰρ κρατέεις· πάσης δ’ ἔριδος κλέος ἐσθλὸν
lines.en: For you are sovereign over all; and the noble fame of every strife
lines.note: κρατέεις = “are sovereign/master”; ἔρις = “strife/contest,” kept as “strife” to retain the agonistic nuance.

lines.gr: Νίκ ῃ ἐπ’ εὐδόξ ῳ κεῖται θαλί ῃσι βρυάζον.
lines.en: rests upon Nikē, brimming in illustrious banquets.
lines.note: Text slightly corrupted in transmission (spacing/accents): read Νίκῃ ἐπ’ εὐδόξῳ κεῖται θαλίῃσι βρυάζον. Subject is κλέος ἐσθλόν from the previous line; βρυάζειν of feasts = “to brim, teem,” hence “brimming in illustrious banquets.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαιρ’, ἔλθοις πεποθημένῳ ὄμματι φαιδρ ῷ,
lines.en: But come, blessed one, with a longed-for, radiant glance,
lines.note: μάκαιρα = “blessed (one)”; πεποθημένῳ ὄμματι φαιδρῷ = “with a longed-for, radiant glance,” a conventional request for the deity’s favorable look.

lines.gr: αἰεὶ ἐπ’ εὐδόξο ις ἔργοις κλέος ἐσθλὸν ἄγουσα.
lines.en: always bringing noble fame upon glorious deeds.
lines.note: ἄγειν κλέος ἐπ’ ἔργοις = “to bring fame upon deeds”; εὐδόξος = “illustrious, of good repute,” rendered “glorious.”

lines.gr: Ἐλθέ, μάκαρ Παι ὰν τιτυοκτόνε, Φο ῖβε Λυκωρεῦ,
lines.en: Come, blessed Paian, Tityos‑slayer, Phoebus Lycoreus,
lines.note: Paian is Apollo as healer; Tityos (Tityus) was the giant slain by Apollo; Lycoreus = from Lycoreia, an early Delphic toponym.

lines.gr: Μεμφῖ τ’, ἀγλαότιμος, ἰῃ ϊος, ὀλβιοδ ῶτα.
lines.en: Memphite, of splendid honor, Iēios, bestower of bliss,
lines.note: Memphite points to Apollo’s Egyptian cult at Memphis; Iēios is an old healing epithet linked to the ritual cry iē.

lines.gr: χρυσολύρη, σπερμε ῖος, ἀρότριε, Πύθιε, Τιτάν,
lines.en: golden‑lyred, Spermeios, Tiller, Pythian, Titan,
lines.note: Spermeios (“of seed”) and Arotrios/Tiller are unusual agrarian epithets of Apollo; Titan reflects his solar aspect.

lines.gr: Γρύνειε, Σμινθεῦ, Πυθοκτόνε, Δελφικέ, μάντι,
lines.en: Gryneian, Smintheus, Python‑slayer, Delphic seer,
lines.note: Gryneian (from Gryneion in Aeolis) and Smintheus (“of mice”) are cult‑titles; Delphic seer renders mantis; Pythoktone = Python‑slayer.

lines.gr: ἄγριε, φωσφόρε δαῖμον, ἐράσμιε, κύδιμε κοῦρε·
lines.en: wild one, light‑bringing daimon, lovable, illustrious youth;
lines.note: Phōsphoros (“light‑bringing”) is common of bringers of light; daimon here = a divine power; erasmios = “lovable.”

lines.gr: Μουσαγέτη, χαροποιός, ἑ κηβόλε, τοξοβέλεμνε,
lines.en: Leader of the Muses, joy‑giving, Far‑darter, archer who launches shafts,
lines.note: Mousagetēs = “Leader of the Muses”; Hekēbolos = “Far‑darter”; toxobelemn‑ is a poetic compound “arrow‑hurling.”

lines.gr: Βράγχιε καὶ Διδυμε ῦ, ἑ κάεργος , Λοξία, ἁ γνέ ·
lines.en: Branchian and Didymean, Hekaergos, Loxias, holy,
lines.note: Branchian and Didymean refer to Apollo’s oracle at Didyma and the Branchidae; Hekaergos = “far‑working”; Loxias = “oblique,” of ambiguous oracles; hagnos = “holy/pure.”

lines.gr: Δήλι’ ἄναξ πανδερκ ὲς ἔχων φαεσίμβροτον ὄμμα,
lines.en: Delian lord, possessing an all‑seeing eye that illumines mortals,
lines.note: Panderkēs = “all‑seeing”; phaesim‑broton “light‑bringing to mortals.”

lines.gr: χρυσοκόμη, καθαρ ὰς φήμας χρησμούς τ’ ἀναφαίνων·
lines.en: golden‑haired, revealing pure utterances and oracles;
lines.note: Chrysokomē = “golden‑haired”; phēmai = utterances; chrēsmoi = oracles.

lines.gr: κλῦθί μευ εὐ χομένου λαῶν ὕπερ ε ὔφρονι θυμῷ.
lines.en: hear me praying on behalf of the peoples with kindly heart.
lines.note: “On behalf of the peoples” (laōn hyper) marks a public intercession; “with kindly heart” renders euphrōn thymos.

lines.en: [line‑number marker: 10]
lines.note: This line is a pagination/numbering artifact, not part of the hymn’s text.

lines.gr: τόνδε σὺ γὰρ λεύσσεις τὸν ἀπείριτον αἰθέρα πάντα,
lines.en: For you behold the entire boundless aether,
lines.note: Apeiritos aither = “boundless aether,” the upper sky.

lines.gr: γα ῖάν τ’ ὀλβιόμοιρον ὕπερθέν καὶ δι’ ἀμολγο ῦ
lines.en: and the earth, blessed in her portion, from above, and through the amolgos
lines.note: Amolgos is the “milking‑time” of night, i.e., deepest midnight; hence “through the amolgos of night.”

lines.gr: νυκτὸς ἐν ἡσυχί ῃσιν ὑπ’ ἀστεροομμάτου ὄρφνης
lines.en: of night, in quiet, beneath the star‑eyed gloom,
lines.note: Aster‑oommatos orphnē = “star‑eyed darkness,” a poetic oxymoron for the night sky.

lines.gr: ῥίζας νέρθε δέδορκας, ἔχεις δέ τε πείρατα κόσμου
lines.en: you have looked upon the roots below, and you hold the bounds of the cosmos,
lines.note: Rhizai nerthen = the roots below (of earth); peirata kosmou = the bounds/limits of the cosmos.

lines.gr: παντός σοὶ δ’ ἀρχή τε τελευτή τ’ ἐστὶ μέλουσα,
lines.en: and the beginning and the end of all are your concern;
lines.note: Archē and teleutē = the beginning and end; melousa “a care/concern to you.”

lines.gr: παντοθαλής, σ ὺ δὲ πάντα πόλον κιθάρ ῃ πολυκρέκτῳ
lines.en: ever‑flourishing, you tune the whole vault with your much‑ringing kithara,
lines.note: Pantothalēs = “ever‑flourishing”; kithara polukrektos = “much‑ringing” lyre; polos = the heavenly vault/sphere.

lines.gr: ἁρμόζεις, ὁτὲ μὲν νεάτης ἐπὶ τέρματα βαίνων,
lines.en: at times going to the limits of the Nete,
lines.note: Nete and Hypate are the extreme strings/registers of the ancient Greek lyre; harmozein = “to tune/fit.”

lines.gr: ἄλλοτε δ’ αὖθ’ ὑπάτην, ποτὲ Δώριον εἰς διάκοσμον
lines.en: at other times to the Hypate, and sometimes into Dorian ordering,
lines.note: Diakosmos = an “ordering/arrangement”; Dorian is a musical harmonia (mode).

lines.gr: πάντα πόλον κιρνὰς, κρίνεις βιοθρέμμονα φῦλα,
lines.en: mixing the whole vault, you judge the life‑nourished tribes,
lines.note: Kirnan = “to mix (like wine)”; krinein = “to separate/decide/judge”; biothremmona phyla = “life‑nourished tribes,” i.e., living creatures.

lines.gr: ἁρμονί ῃ κεράσ ας παγκόσμιον ἀνδράσι μοῖραν·
lines.en: having blended for men a world‑allotment by harmony;
lines.note: Moira = allotment/fate; “world‑allotment” (pankosmion) suggests cosmic order apportioned to humankind by harmony.

lines.en: [line‑number marker: 20]
lines.note: Pagination/numbering artifact, not part of the hymn’s text.

lines.gr: μίξας χειμῶνος θέρεός τ’ ἴσον ἀμφοτέροισιν,
lines.en: having mingled winter and summer, equal to both,
lines.note: The seasons are harmonized musically; “equal to both” marks equilibrium of opposites.

lines.gr: εἰς ὑπάτα ς χειμ ῶνα, θέρος νεάταις διακρίνας,
lines.en: assigning winter to the Hypatai, and setting summer to the Netai,
lines.note: Hypatai (lower strings) associated with winter; Netai (upper strings) with summer; the verb diakrinas = “assign/distinguish.”

lines.gr: Δώριον εἰς ἔαρος πολυηράτου ὥριον ἄνθος.
lines.en: and to the Dorian the seasonal blossom of much‑desired spring.
lines.note: Dorian mode is linked here with spring’s bloom; polyeratos = “much‑desired.”

lines.gr: ἔνθεν ἐπωνυμίην σε βροτοὶ κλῄζουσιν ἄ νακτα
lines.en: Whence mortals hail you, O lord, by the epithet
lines.note: Eponymia = epithet/by‑name; “hail you” renders klēizousin, lit. “celebrate/name.”

lines.gr: Πᾶνα, θε ὸν δικέρωτ’, ἀνέμων συρίγμαθ’ ἱέντα ·
lines.en: Pan, the two‑horned god, sending forth the whistlings of the winds,
lines.note: The identification with Pan (“All”) arises from Apollo’s harmonization of the cosmos; dikerōs = “two‑horned”; “whistlings of the winds” renders anemōn syrigmata.

lines.gr: οὕνεκα παντὸς ἔχεις κόσμου σφρηγ ῖδα τυπῶτιν.
lines.en: because you hold the stamping seal of the whole cosmos.
lines.note: Sphrēgis typōtin = a “stamping seal,” i.e., the formative imprint of cosmic order.

lines.gr: κλῦθι μάκαρ, σώζων μύστας ἱκετηρίδι φωνῇ.
lines.en: Hear, blessed one, saving the initiates with a suppliant voice.
lines.note: Mystai = initiates; hiketēridi phōnē = “suppliant voice.”

lines.gr: Λητο ῖ κυανόπεπλε, θεὰ διδυματὸκε, σεμνή,
lines.en: Leto, dark-veiled, goddess, twin-bearing, august,
lines.note: Λητοῖ is a dative of address (“O Leto”); κυανόπεπλε = “dark-veiled”; διδυματόκε = “twin-bearing”; σεμνή = “august, revered.”

lines.gr: Κοιαντίς, μεγάθυμε, πολυλλίστη βασίλεια,
lines.en: Koianthis, great-hearted, much-invoked queen,
lines.note: Κοιαντίς = “daughter of Koios (Coeus)”; μεγάθυμε = “great-hearted”; πολυλλίστη = “much-implored/much-invoked” (from λίσσομαι, “beseech”); βασίλεια = “queen.”

lines.gr: εὔτεκνον Ζηνὸς γονίμην ὠδῖνα λαχο ῦσα,
lines.en: having won the fruitful travail of Zeus’s begetting,
lines.note: Both εὔτεκνον and γονίμην modify ὠδῖνα (“labor, travail”), stressing easy/fruitful childbirth; λαχοῦσα = “having obtained” (as by allotment).

lines.gr: γειναμένη Φοῖβόν τε καὶ Ἄρτεμιν ἰοχέαιραν,
lines.en: having borne Phoibos and arrow-showering Artemis,
lines.note: Φοῖβος (Phoibos) = Apollo; ἰοχέαιρα = “arrow-showering/arrow-darting,” a fixed epithet of Artemis; γειναμένη = “having borne.”

lines.gr: τὴν μὲν ἐν Ὀρτυγί ῃ, τὸν δὲ κραναῇ ἐνὶ Δήλ ῳ·
lines.en: her in Ortygia, but him in rocky Delos;
lines.note: τὴν … τὸν picks out Artemis (fem.) in Ortygia and Phoibos (masc.) in Delos; κραναῇ = “rocky,” a traditional epithet of Delos.

lines.gr: κλῦθι, θεὰ δέσποινα, καὶ ἵλαον ἦτορ ἔχουσα
lines.en: hear, goddess, Lady, and, holding a gracious heart,
lines.note: κλῦθι = “hear!” (hymnic imperative); ἵλαον ἦτορ ἔχουσα = “holding a gracious/propitious heart,” a standard prayer formula; δέσποινα = “Lady” (cultic title).

lines.gr: βα ῖν’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν, τέλος ἡδὺ φέρουσα.
lines.en: come to the all-divine rite, bringing a sweet fulfillment.
lines.note: βαῖν’ = βαῖνε (elided imperative) “come/go”; τελετή = “rite, initiation”; πάνθειον = “pertaining to all the gods”; τέλος ἡδὺ φέρουσα = “bringing a sweet fulfillment/end (of the rite).”

lines.gr: Κλῦθί μευ, ὦ βασίλεια, Διὸς πολυώνυμε κούρη,
lines.en: Hear me, O queen, many‑named daughter of Dios,
lines.note: polyonyme modifies kourē (“many‑named daughter of Dios”), not Dios itself.

lines.gr: Τιτηνίς, βρομίη , μεγαλώνυμε, τοξότι, σεμνή,
lines.en: Titaness, roaring, renowned, archer, august,
lines.note: Titanis marks Artemis as of Titanic stock; bromiē (“roaring”) is striking for a huntress but stresses the wild, thundering aspect.

lines.gr: πασιφαής, δαιδοῦχε, θεά Δίκτυννα, λοχείη,
lines.en: all‑shining, torch‑bearer, goddess Diktynna, of the childbed,
lines.note: Diktynna is the Cretan Artemis/Britomartis; locheia means “of childbed/lying‑in.”

lines.gr: ὠδίνων ἐπαρωγ ὲ, καὶ ὠδίνων ἀμύητε·
lines.en: helper in labor‑pains, and averter of labor‑pains;
lines.note: ἀμύητε is ‘avertress’ (from amynō, “ward off”); the line is a balanced pair: helper and averter of labor pains.

lines.gr: λυσίζωνε, φίλοιστρε, κυνηγέτι, λυσιμέριμνε,
lines.en: looser of the girdle, goad‑loving, huntress, releaser from care,
lines.note: lysizōnē (“looser of the girdle”) is a childbirth epithet; φίλοιστρε is difficult—probably ‘lover of the oistros’ (the goad/frenzy), hence “goad‑loving.”

lines.gr: εὔδρομος, ἰοχέαιρα, φιλαγρότι, νυκτερόφοιτε,
lines.en: swift‑running, arrow‑showering, lover of the wild, night‑roaming,
lines.note: iocheaira is “arrow‑showering”; philagroti is “fond of the fields/wild places.”

lines.gr: κλεισίη, εὐάντητε, λυτηρίη, ἀρσενόμορφε,
lines.en: of the threshold, gracious to meet, deliverer, male‑formed,
lines.note: kleisiē is “of thresholds/doorways”; lyteriē is “deliverer.” arsenomorphē (“male‑formed”) points to an androgynous, virile aspect of the goddess.

lines.gr: ὀρθίη, ὠ κυλόχεια, βροτῶν κουροτρόφε δαῖμον,
lines.en: upright, O lady of childbirth, daimon nurse of mortals’ young,
lines.note: kylocheia denotes childbirth/lying‑in (possibly the birthing‑stool); kourotrophos is “nurse of the young.”

lines.gr: ἀγροτέρη, χθονίη, θηροκτόνος, ὀλβιόμοιρε·
lines.en: of the countryside, chthonian, beast‑slaying, of blessed lot;
lines.note: chthonia here is “of the earth” rather than strictly underworld; olbiomoirē “of blessed lot.”

lines.gr: ἣ κατέχεις ὀρέων δρυμούς, ἐλαφηβόλε, σεμνή,
lines.en: who holdest the wooded glens of the mountains, deer‑shooting, august,
lines.note: drymous are “wooded glens.” elaphēbole is “deer‑shooting.”

lines.gr: πότνια, παμβασίλεια, καλὸν θάλος αἰὲν ἐοῦσα·
lines.en: mistress, all‑sovereign, ever a fair blossom,
lines.note: thalos is a “shoot/blossom,” evoking maidenly bloom and perpetual youth.

lines.gr: δρυμονία, σκυλακῖτι, Κυδωνιάς, αἰολόμορφε.
lines.en: woodland, of whelps, of Kydonia, changeful in form.
lines.note: skylakitē (“of whelps/puppies”) marks her as leader of hounds; Kydonias is “of Kydonia” (Crete); aiolomorphē is “changeful in form.”

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, θεὰ σώτειρα, φίλη, μύστῃσιν ἅπασιν,
lines.en: Come, savior goddess, dear one, to all the initiates,
lines.note: mystai are initiates; the address situates the hymn in a ritual/initiatory context.

lines.gr: εὐάντητος, ἄγουσα καλοὺς καρποὺς ἀπὸ γαίης,
lines.en: gracious to meet, bringing fair fruits from the earth,
lines.note: euantētos means “favorable/gracious to meet,” a standard epiphanic request; “fair fruits” signals bounty.

lines.gr: εἰρήνην τ’ ἐρατὴν καλλιπλόκαμόν θ’ ὑγίειαν·
lines.en: and lovely Eirene and fair‑tressed Hygieia;
lines.note: Eirene and Hygieia are personified deities; kalliplokamos (“fair‑tressed”) is a traditional epithet transferred to Hygieia.

lines.gr: πέμποις δ’ εἰς ὀρέων κεφαλὰς νούσους τε καὶ ἄλγη.
lines.en: and dispatch to the mountain peaks both diseases and pains.
lines.note: pempois is optative of wish: a banishing formula—“send off” maladies to the mountain tops, away from the community.

lines.gr: Τιτῆνες, Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀγλαὰ τέκνα,
lines.en: Titans, splendid children of Gaia and Ouranos,
lines.note: ἀγλαὰ (“splendid, shining”) is a traditional epiphanic epithet in hymnic style.

lines.gr: ἡμετέρων πρόγονοι πατέρων, γαίης ὑπένερθεν
lines.en: forefathers of our fathers, beneath the earth,
lines.note: The reading γαίης ὑπένερθεν (“beneath the earth”) contrasts with a common variant γαίης ὑπ’ ἄντροισιν (“beneath the caverns of the earth”); both express subterrene dwelling.

lines.gr: οἴκοις ταρταρίοισι μυχ ῷ χθον ὸς ἐνναίοντες,
lines.en: dwelling in Tartarean houses, in the innermost recess of the earth,
lines.note: οἴκοις ταρταρίοισι (“in Tartarean houses”) locates the Titans in Tartarus; μυχῷ χθονός is “the innermost recess of the earth.” The line shows minor spacing/orthographic issues in transmission.

lines.gr: ἀρχαὶ καὶ πηγα ὶ πάντων θνητῶν πολυμόχθων,
lines.en: origins and wellsprings of all mortals who toil much,
lines.note: ἀρχαί καὶ πηγαί forms a hendiadys, “origins and sources.” θνητῶν πολυμόχθων (“toil-worn mortals”) here encompasses living beings generally in contrast to gods.

lines.gr: εἰναλίων, πτηνῶν τε, καὶ οἳ χθόνα ναιετάουσιν·
lines.en: of the sea-dwellers, the winged, and those who inhabit the earth;
lines.note: εἰναλίων = “sea-dwelling (creatures)”; πτηνῶν = “winged (birds).” The printed ναιετάουσιν reflects manuscript/typographical variation; sense is “dwell/inhabit.”

lines.gr: ἐξ ὑμέων γὰρ π ᾶσα πέλει γενε ὴ κατὰ κόσμον.
lines.en: for from you every lineage arises in due order.
lines.note: κατὰ κόσμον means “in due (cosmic) order, properly arranged”; γενεή can be “race/lineage/generation.”

lines.gr: ὑμέας κικλήσκω μῆνιν χαλεπ ὴν ἀποπέμπειν,
lines.en: You I invoke, to avert grievous wrath,
lines.note: μῆνις is a potent, quasi-divine wrath (cf. epic usage); ἀποπέμπειν (“to send away”) signals the hymn’s apotropaic aim, i.e., averting harmful anger.

lines.gr: εἴτις ἀπὸ χθονίων προγόνων οἴκοισι πελάσθη.
lines.en: if ever from chthonian forefathers it should draw near to the houses.
lines.note: The subject of “should draw near” is elliptical, supplied from line 7 as μῆνις (“wrath”); χθόνιοι πρόγονοι (“chthonian forefathers”) denotes the ancestral dead, implying the averting of ancestral wrath or curses from the household.

lines.gr: Χαλκόκροτοι Κουρῆτες, Ἀρήϊα τεύχε’ ἔχοντες,
lines.en: Bronze-clashing Kourêtes, bearing the war-gear of Ares,
lines.note: “Bronze-clashing” (chalkókrotoi) evokes shield-dance noise; “Ares’ gear” = martial arms.

lines.gr: οὐράνιοι χθόνιοί τε, καὶ εἰνάλιοι, πολύολβοι,
lines.en: heavenly, chthonian, and of the sea, much-blest,
lines.note: Tripartite jurisdiction (heaven/earth below/sea); einálioi = “of the sea”; polýolboi = “much-blest.”

lines.gr: ζωογόνοι πνοιαί, κόσμου σωτῆρες ἀγαυοί,
lines.en: life-producing breaths, illustrious saviors of the cosmos,
lines.note: zōogonoi pnoaí = “life-bearing breaths,” often of winds; “cosmos” = ordered world.

lines.gr: οἵτε Σαμοθρῄ κην, ἱ ερὴν χθόνα, ναιετάοντες,
lines.en: who, dwelling in Samothrace, the holy land,
lines.note: Orthography in the source is corrupt; read Σαμοθρᾴκην, ἱερὴν χθόνα; the Great Gods of Samothrace are intended.

lines.gr: κινδύνους θνητῶν ἀπερύκετε ποντοπλανήτων·
lines.en: ward off the perils of sea-wandering mortals;
lines.note: pon-toplanētōn = “sea-wandering” (sailors); protective Samothracian function.

lines.gr: ὑμεῖς καὶ τελετ ὴν πρ ῶτοι μερόπεσσιν ἔθεσθε,
lines.en: you too first established the rite for mortal men,
lines.note: teletḗ = “rite/initiation”; merópes = “mortals”; source spacing corrupt (τελετὴν πρῶτοι).

lines.gr: ἀθάνατοι Κουρῆτες, Ἀρήϊα τεύχε’ ἔχοντες.
lines.en: immortal Kourêtes, bearing the war-gear of Ares.
lines.note: Reiterates line 1, adding “immortal” (athanátoi).

lines.gr: νωμ ᾶτ’ Ὠκεανόν, νωμᾶθ’ ἅλα, δένδρεά θ’ αὕτως.
lines.en: you wield Okeanos, you wield the sea, and likewise the trees.
lines.note: nōmâτε = “wield/steer/control”; Okeanos = world-encircling stream; trees included as things they set in motion/shake.

lines.gr: ἐρχόμενοι γαῖαν κοναβίζετε ποσσὶν ἐλαφρο ῖς,
lines.en: as you come you make the earth ring with your nimble feet,
lines.note: konabízein = “make to ring/thunder,” of stamping dance.

lines.gr: μαρμαίροντες ὅπλοις. πτήσσουσι δὲ θῆρες ἅπαντες
lines.en: gleaming in arms; and all wild beasts cower
lines.note: marmáirō = “gleam”; ptḗssō = “cower.”

lines.gr: ὁρμώντων, θόρυβος δὲ βοή τ’ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἵκει,
lines.en: as you charge, and the din and shout reach to heaven,
lines.note: Hortatory scene of their onset; ὁρμώντων may be taken temporally, “as you charge.”

lines.gr: εἱλιγμο ῖς τε ποδ ῶν κονίη νεφέλας ἀφικάνει
lines.en: and through the whirling of your feet the dust mounts to the clouds
lines.note: heiligmoi = “whirlings/twists”; sense is “kick up clouds of dust.”

lines.gr: ἐρχομένων · τότ ε δή ῥ α καὶ ἄνθεα πάντα τέθηλεν.
lines.en: as you advance; then indeed all the flowers burgeon.
lines.note: Fertility effect of their dance; “burgeon” renders téthēlen.

lines.gr: δαίμονες ἀθάνατοι, τροφέες καὶ αὖτ’ ὀλετ ῆρες,
lines.en: immortal daimones, both nurturers and again destroyers,
lines.note: Tense polarity: “nurturers” (trophé) and “destroyers” (oletêres) mark ambivalence of daimones.

lines.gr: ἡνίκ’ ἂν ὁρμαίνητε χολούμενοι ἀνθρώποισιν,
lines.en: whenever, angered against men, you take counsel,
lines.note: hormaínein = “to take counsel/ponder”; choloúmenoi = “in anger.”

lines.gr: ὀλλύντες βίοτον καὶ κτήματα, ἠδὲ καὶ αὐτοὺς
lines.en: destroying livelihood and possessions, and even the men themselves,
lines.note: ollýntes = “destroying”; bíotos = “livelihood/life”; ktḗmata = “possessions.”

lines.gr: πλάζοντες· στοναχε ῖ δὲ μέγας πόντος βαθυδίνης,
lines.en: driving them astray; and the great deep-eddying sea groans,
lines.note: plázontes = “driving astray/harrying,” apt for storms; bathydínēs = “deep-eddying.”

lines.gr: δένδρη δ’ ὑψικάρην’ ἐκ ῥιζῶν ἐς χθόνα πίπτει ·
lines.en: and the high-crested trees fall from their roots to the ground,
lines.note: hypsikárēna = “high-crested,” poetic of treetops; uprooting by storm implied.

lines.gr: ἠχὼ δ’ οὐρανίη κελαδε ῖ ῥοιζήμασι φύλλων.
lines.en: and heavenly echo rings with the whirring of leaves.
lines.note: rhoízēma = “whirring/whizzing”; keladeî = “resounds.”

lines.gr: Κουρ ῆτες Κορύβαντες, ἀνάκτορες, εὐδύνατοί τε,
lines.en: Kourêtes, Korybantes, sovereigns, mighty in power,
lines.note: Conflation of Kourêtes and Korybantes; eudýnatoi = “mighty in power.”

lines.gr: ἐν Σαμοθρῄ κῃ ἄνακτες, ὁμοῦ Ζηνός κόροι αὐτοί·
lines.en: lords in Samothrace, at once yourselves sons of Zeus,
lines.note: Zēnós koroi = “sons of Zeus,” evoking the Dioscuri; homoû = “at once/together.”

lines.gr: πνοια ὶ ἀέναοι, ψυχοτρόφοι, ἠεροειδεῖ ς·
lines.en: ever-flowing breaths, soul-nourishing, airy,
lines.note: pnoaí = “breaths/winds”; psychotróphoi = “soul-/life-nourishing”; hēeroeideîs = “airy.”

lines.gr: οἵτε καὶ οὐράνιοι δίδυμοι κλῄζεσθ’ ἐν Ὀλύμπ ῳ
lines.en: who also as heavenly Twins are hailed on Olympos,
lines.note: Ouránioi dídymoi = “heavenly Twins,” i.e., Dioscuri; syncretism with Samothracian Great Gods.

lines.gr: εὔπνοοι, ε ὔδιοι, σωτήριοι ἠδὲ προσηνε ῖς,
lines.en: fair-blowing, fair-weather, saving and propitious,
lines.note: Standard weather epithets: eúpnooi (fair-blowing), eúdioi (fair-weather), prosenéis (favorable).

lines.gr: ὡροτρόφοι, φερέκαρποι ἐπιπνείοιτε ἄνακτες.
lines.en: season-nurturing, fruit-bearing—breathe favorably, lords.
lines.note: epipneíoite is optative of wish: “may you breathe favorably (upon us)”; ōrotróphoi/pherékarmoi = fertility epithets.

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω χθονὸς ἀενάου βασιλῆα μέγιστον,
lines.en: I summon the greatest king of the everlasting earth,
lines.note: ἀενάου with χθών is poetically “everlasting” (not the usual “ever-flowing,” suited to rivers).

lines.gr: Κύρβαντ’ ὀλβιόμοιρον, Ἀρήιον, ἀπροσόρατον,
lines.en: the Korybant, blessed in lot, Ares-like, unapproachable,
lines.note: Κύρβαντ’ is an orthographic variant of Κορύβαντα (Korybant). ἀπροσόρατον = “not to be faced/awful to behold.”

lines.gr: νυκτερινὸ ν Κούρητα , φόβων ἀποπαύστορα δειν ῶν,
lines.en: the nocturnal Kourete, a stayer of dreadful fears,
lines.note: Κούρητα = “Kourete,” one of the ecstatic/armed attendants of the Mother; ἀποπαύστορα literally “one who causes to cease.”

lines.gr: φαντασι ῶν ἐπαρωγόν, ἐρημοπλάνον Κορύβαντα,
lines.en: a helper against phantasms, the solitary-roaming Korybant,
lines.note: φαντασίαι are apparitions/visions (often nocturnal); ἐρημοπλάνος “wandering in desolate places.”

lines.gr: αἰολόμορφον ἄνακτα, θε ὸν διφυ ῆ, πολύμορφον,
lines.en: lord of changeful form, a two-natured god, of many shapes,
lines.note: αἰολόμορφος = “changeful-shaped”; διφυής = “two-natured” (a common Orphic epithet, e.g., of Dionysos); πολύμορφος = “many-formed.”

lines.gr: φοίνιον, αἱμαχθέντα κασιγνήτων ὑπὸ δισσῶ ν·
lines.en: blood-red, bloodied by two brothers,
lines.note: φοίνιος = “blood-red, murderous.” The clause “bloodied by two brothers” is obscure; it may allude to a variant myth in which a Korybas is attacked by his brothers.

lines.gr: Δηο ῦς ὃς γνώμ ῃσιν ἐνήλλαξας δέμας ἁγνόν,
lines.en: who by Deo’s counsels altered your holy frame,
lines.note: Δηούς = “Deo,” i.e., Demeter. γνώμῃσι(ν) “by counsels/plots”; ἐνήλλαξας “you altered/changed.”

lines.gr: θηρότυπον θέμενος μορφὴν δνοφεροῖο δράκοντος·
lines.en: taking on the beast-shaped form of a dusky serpent;
lines.note: θηρότυπος “beast-shaped”; δράκων here = “serpent” (not a medieval “dragon”); δνοφερός = “murky, dark.”

lines.gr: κλῦθι, μάκαρ, φωνῶν, χαλεπ ὴν δ’ ἀποπέμπεο μῆνιν,
lines.en: hear, blessed one, our voices, and send grievous wrath away,
lines.note: μῆνις is specifically divine wrath; the prayer seeks its aversion.

lines.gr: παύων φαντασίας ψυχ ῆς ἐκπλήκτου ἀνάγκης.
lines.en: ending the visions born of the panic-struck soul’s compulsion.
lines.note: The genitives allow different construals; sense is “bring to an end the compulsive visions that assail a panic-stricken soul.”

lines.gr: Δηοῖ παμμήτειρα θεά, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον,
lines.en: Deo, all-mother goddess, many-named divinity,
lines.note: “Deo” is a cult-name of Dēmētēr; παμμήτειρα means “all-mother.” Δαῖμον here is “divinity,” not necessarily a lesser spirit.

lines.gr: σεμνὴ Δήμητερ, κουροτρόφος, ὀλβιοδ ῶτι,
lines.en: august Dēmētēr, nurse of youths, bestower of blessed wealth,
lines.note: Κουροτρόφος = “nurse of youths/children.” Ὀλβιοδῶτι means “giver of prosperity/blessed wealth.”

lines.gr: πλουτοδότειρα θεά, σταχυοτρόφε, παντοδότειρα,
lines.en: wealth-giving goddess, nurturer of the ears of grain, all-giver,
lines.note: Σταχυοτρόφε = “nurturing the grain-ear” (στάχυς). Παντοδότειρα = “all-giving.”

lines.gr: εἰρήνῃ χαίρουσα καὶ ἐργασίαις πολυμόχθοις,
lines.en: rejoicing in peace and in labors full of toil,
lines.note: Πολυμόχθοις underscores the hard labor of agriculture, which Dēmētēr sanctifies.

lines.gr: σπερμείη, σωρ ῖτις, ἀλωαίη , χλοόκαρπε,
lines.en: sower-goddess, Lady of the heaps, of the threshing-floors, green-fruited,
lines.note: Σπερμείη (“sower”), Σωρῖτις (often printed Σωρείτις, “of the heaps” of piled grain), Ἀλωαίη (“of the threshing-floors”), Χλοόκαρπε (“green-/leafy-fruited”): a cluster of agrarian epithets.

lines.gr: ἣ ναίεις ἁγνο ῖσιν Ἐλευσῖνος γυάλοισιν.
lines.en: who dwellest in the holy dells of Eleusis.
lines.note: Γυάλοις are “hollows/dells”; Eleusis is Dēmētēr’s holy seat and the site of the Mysteries.

lines.gr: ἱμερόεσσ’, ἐ ρατή, θνητῶν θρέπτειρα προπάντων·
lines.en: lovely, desirable, nourisher of mortals before all,
lines.note: Ἱμερόεσσα and ἐρατή both mean “lovely/desirable”; θρέπτειρα προπάντων = “nourisher of mortals before all others.”

lines.gr: πρώτη ὑποζεύξασα βο ῶν ἀροτ ῆρα τένοντα,
lines.en: you who first brought under the yoke the oxen’s plough-drawing sinew,
lines.note: The phrase ἀροτῆρα τένοντα is difficult; τένοντας (“sinew/strap”) likely refers to the leather thongs/gear that enable oxen to draw the plough. Some editors have variant readings.

lines.gr: καὶ βίον ἱμερόεντα βροτοῖς πολύολβον ἀνεῖσα·
lines.en: and sent forth for mortals a desirable, richly blessed life;
lines.note: Ἀνεῖσα (“sent forth/loosed”) of bestowing benefits; βίος ἱμερόεις = “a desirable life,” πολύολβος = “richly blessed.”

lines.gr: αὐξιθαλής, Βρομίοιο συνέστιος, ἀγλαότιμος,
lines.en: growth-fostering, table-companion of Bromios, splendid in honor,
lines.note: Βρομίοιο (“of Bromios,” Dionysos). Συνέστιος = “sharing hearth/table,” indicating Eleusinian association with Dionysos.

lines.gr: λαμπαδόεσσ’, ἁ γνή, δρεπάνοις χαίρουσα θερείοις.
lines.en: torch-bearing, pure, rejoicing in the summer sickles.
lines.note: Λαμπαδόεσσα (“torch-bearing”) evokes the Eleusinian rites; θερείοις (“of summer”) points to harvest-time reaping.

lines.gr: σὺ χθονίη , σὺ δὲ φαινομένη, σὺ δε π ᾶσι προσηνής·
lines.en: you are chthonian, you are manifest, and to all you are gracious;
lines.note: Χθονίη (“of/under the earth”) and φαινομένη (“manifest/appearing”) suggest chthonic and epiphanic aspects; προσηνής = “gracious/affable.”

lines.gr: εὔτεκνε, παιδοφίλη, σεμνή, κουροτρόφε κούρη,
lines.en: of goodly offspring, child-loving, august, maiden who nurtures the young,
lines.note: Εὔτεκνος = “of goodly offspring.” Κούρη (“maiden”) is a cultic honorific even for a mother; κουροτρόφος = “nurturer of youths.”

lines.gr: ἅρμα δρακοντείοισιν ὑποζεύξασα χαλινοῖς,
lines.en: having yoked your chariot with serpent-bridles,
lines.note: Δρακοντεῖος (“serpentine”): sacred serpents are part of Demetrian iconography; the chariot is imagined with serpent-bridles.

lines.gr: ἐγκυκλίοις δίναις περὶ σὸν θρόνον εὐαζόντων.
lines.en: as around your throne they cry euai in encircling whirls.
lines.note: Εὐαζόντων refers to the Bacchic cry “euai!”; ἐγκυκλίοις δίναις may describe circling dances (or the coils of serpents). The syntax allows either nuance.

lines.gr: μουνογενής, πολύτεκνε θεά, πολυπότνια θνητοῖς,
lines.en: only-begotten, yet many-childed goddess, all-sovereign over mortals,
lines.note: Μουνογενής (“only-begotten”) in Orphic theology can denote a unique, primordial divinity; juxtaposed with πολύτεκνος (“many-childed”) it expresses a paradox of cosmic maternity. Πολυπότνια = “much-/all-sovereign.”

lines.gr: ἧς πολλα ὶ μορφαί, πολυάνθεμοι, ἱεροθηλε ῖς·
lines.en: whose many forms are rich in blossoms and sacredly feminine,
lines.note: Πολυάνθεμος = “rich in blossoms”; ἱεροθηλής (“sacredly female/fertile”) is a rare compound stressing holy fecundity.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρ’, ἁγνή, καρποῖς βρίθουσα θερείοις,
lines.en: come, blessed, pure one, laden with summer fruits,
lines.note: Θερείοις καρποῖς (“summer fruits”) marks the harvest season and its abundance.

lines.gr: εἰρήνην κατάγουσα καὶ εὐνομίην ἐρατειν ὴν,
lines.en: bringing down Peace and lovely Good Order,
lines.note: Εἰρήνη (Peace) and Εὐνομίη (Good Order) are personified blessings “brought down” (κατάγουσα) from the goddess.

lines.gr: καὶ πλο ῦτον πολύολβον, ὁμοῦ δ’ ὑγίειανἄνασσαν.
lines.en: and richly blessed Wealth, and together queenly Health.
lines.note: Πλοῦτος (Wealth) and Ὑγίεια (Health) are personified; ἄνασσαν (“queenly/sovereign”) dignifies Health as a goddess in her own right.

lines.gr: Ἀνταίη βασίλεια, θεά, πολυώνυμε μῆτερ
lines.en: O Antaia, queen, goddess, much‑named mother,
lines.note: Antaia is an epithet applied here to Demeter; the sequence of Eleusinian motifs identifies the goddess despite the epithet’s rarer association. “Much‑named” (polyonymos) is a standard Orphic laudatory epithet.

lines.gr: ἀθανάτων τε θεῶν ἠδὲ θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων,
lines.en: of immortal gods and mortal men,

lines.gr: ἥ ποτ ε μαστεύουσα πολυπλάγκτῳ ἐν ἀνίῃ,
lines.en: who once, seeking in much‑wandering anguish,
lines.note: . masteuō means “to search out, track down”; “in much‑wandering anguish” renders poluplanktō en aniai, evoking Demeter’s roaming in search of Persephone.

lines.gr: νηστείαν κατέπαυσας Ἐλευσῖνος ἐν γυάλοισιν,
lines.en: brought your fast to an end in the hollows of Eleusis,
lines.note: “Hollows” translates gyaloi; Eleusis is the Eleusinian plain/shrine. The “fast” recalls Demeter’s ritual abstention in the myth and Eleusinian practice.

lines.gr: ἦλθές τ’ εἰς Ἀΐδην πρὸς ἀγαυ ὴν Περσεφόνειαν,
lines.en: and came to Aïdēs, to noble Persephone,
lines.note: “Aïdēs” is the underworld and its god; the line refers to Demeter’s descent to Persephone.

lines.gr: ἁγνὸν πα ῖδα Δυσαύλου ὁδηγητ ῆρα λαχο ῦσα,
lines.en: having obtained as guide the holy child of Dysaules,
lines.note: Dysaules is an Eleusinian figure; the “holy child” is commonly identified with Eubouleus, who guides and informs Demeter in Eleusinian lore.

lines.gr: μηνυτῆ ρ’ ἁγίων λέκτρων χθονίου Διὸς ἁγνο ῦ,
lines.en: the revealer of the sacred bed of chthonian Zeus the pure,
lines.note: “Chthonian Zeus” is a customary periphrasis for Hades; “bed” (lektra) denotes the marriage/union of Hades and Persephone.

lines.gr: Εὔβουλον τέξασα θεὸν θνητῆ ς ἀπ’ ἀνάγκης.
lines.en: having brought forth Euboulos as a god out of mortal necessity.
lines.note: Text and sense are debated. Teksasa (“having borne/produced”) literally yields “having brought forth Euboulos as a god from mortal necessity.” Euboulos/Eubouleus can be (a) the Eleusinian hero later divinized, son of Dysaules, (b) an epithet/aspect of Plouton/Hades, or (c) a chthonic Dionysus. “From mortal necessity” may mean “from mortal condition/constraint,” i.e., despite mortal birth he became a god; some editors have proposed emendations (e.g., θέσασα “having established”) to ease the sense.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεά, λίτομαί σε, πολυλλίστη βασίλεια,
lines.en: But, goddess, I beseech you, much‑invoked queen,
lines.note: “Polylistē” = “much‑supplicated, much‑invoked,” a hymnic epithet.

lines.gr: ἐλθεῖνεὐάντητον ἐπ’ εὐϊέρῳ σέο μύστῃ.
lines.en: to come favorably to your well‑sacrificing initiate.
lines.note: . “Euan tēt on” = “favorable, propitious”; “well‑sacrificing” (euieros) marks the devotee as a proper officiant (mystēs).

lines.gr: Θεσμοφόρον καλέω ναρθηκοφόρον Διόνυσον,
lines.en: I call upon Dionysos, Law‑bringing and narthēx‑bearing,
lines.note: Thesmophoros (“Law‑bringing”) is more commonly Demeter’s epithet; here it is applied to Dionysos. Narthēx is the giant‑fennel stalk used for the thyrsus.

lines.gr: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον πολυώνυμον Εὐβουλ ῆος,
lines.en: the much‑remembered, many‑named seed of Eubouleus,
lines.note: Sperma (“seed”) = “offspring, scion.” Polymnēstos (“much‑remembered/oft‑commemorated”). Eubouleus is a chthonic figure (often Hades/Plouton, sometimes an Eleusinian persona) with whom Dionysos is associated; “many‑named” belongs syntactically to “seed.”

lines.gr: ἁγνήν τ’ εὐΐερόν τε Μίσην, ἄῤῥητον ἄνασσαν,
lines.en: and pure, and holy Misê, the ineffable queen,
lines.note: Misê (Μίση) is an obscure mystic goddess in Orphic/Eleusinian contexts; some manuscripts vary the form (Μίση/Μύση). Arrētos (“ineffable”) marks mystery‑cult secrecy; euïeros = “truly holy.”

lines.gr: ἄρσενα καὶ θῆλυν, διφυῆ, λύσειον Ἴακχον ·
lines.en: male and female, two‑formed, Iakkhos the Releaser;
lines.note: “Male and female, two‑formed” reflects Dionysiac androgyny in Orphic theology. Lyseios (“Releaser”) = reliever from cares/bonds; Iakkhos is the Eleusinian procession‑god often identified with Dionysos.

lines.gr: εἴτ' ἐν Ἐλευσῖνος τέρπῃ νηῷ θυόεντι,
lines.en: whether you delight in the incense‑fuming temple at Eleusis,
lines.note: Thuóeis (“incense‑/sacrifice‑fuming”) evokes a temple fragrant with burnt offerings; Eleusis is the sanctuary of Demeter, Kore, and Iakkhos.

lines.gr: εἴτε καὶ ἐν Φρυγίῃ σὺν μητέρι μυστιπολεύεις,
lines.en: or in Phrygia you go about in mystic processions with the Mother,
lines.note: Mystipoleueis (“go about in mystic processions”) is a rare compound; “the Mother” is the Phrygian Mother (Kybele/Rhea).

lines.gr: ἢ Κύπρῳ τέρπῃ σὺν ἐυστεφάνῳ Κυθερείῃ,
lines.en: or in Cyprus you take pleasure with well‑garlanded Kytherēia,
lines.note: Kytherēia is Aphrodite by her Cytheran epithet; eu‑stephanos = “well‑crowned/garlanded.”

lines.gr: ἢ καὶ πυροφόροις πεδίοις ἐπαγάλλεαι ἁγνοῖς,
lines.en: or you exult in the grain‑bearing, hallowed plains,
lines.note: Pyrophoroi (“wheat‑bearing”) plains likely allude to Eleusinian or other fertile, sacral fields; hagnos = “pure/holy.”

lines.gr: σὺν σῇ μητρὶ θεᾷ μελανηφόρῳ Ἴσιδι σεμνῇ,
lines.en: with your mother the goddess, august Isis in her black robe,
lines.note: Melanēphoros (“black‑clad”) is a cult epithet of Isis; her role as “mother” reflects Greco‑Egyptian syncretism with Demeter‑type figures.

lines.gr: Αἰγύπτου παρὰ χεῦμα σὺν ἀμφιπόλοισι τιθήναις·
lines.en: by Egypt’s flood, with nurse‑attendant handmaids;
lines.note: Aigyptou cheuma (“Egypt’s flood”) refers to the Nile; amphipoloi “attendants” and tithēnai “nurses” denote Isis’s ministering handmaids.

lines.gr: εὐμενέουσ’ ἔλθοις ἀγάθ' ἐκτελέουσ' ἐπ’ ἀέθλοις.
lines.en: come graciously, fulfilling good things upon the rites.
