lines.note: Elthois (optative) expresses a prayerful wish, “may you come.” Aethlois (“labors/contests”) in hymnic/mystery context = ritual performances; “fulfill good things” is a conventional benediction.

lines.gr: Ὧραι, θυγατέρες Θέμιδος καὶ Ζηνὸς ἄνακτος,
lines.en: Horai, daughters of Themis and lord Zeus,
lines.note: Horai: the Seasons/Hours; “lord” renders anaktos, a cultic epithet of Zeus.

lines.gr: Εὐνομίη τε Δίκη τε, καὶ Εἰρήνη πολύολβε,
lines.en: Eunomia and Dike, and richly-blest Eirene,
lines.note: The three named Horai (Eunomia, Dike, Eirene) follow Hesiod; poly-olbe = “richly-blest.”

lines.gr: εἰαριναί, λειμωνιάδες, πολυάνθεμοι, ἁγναί,
lines.en: vernal, meadow-maidens, many-flowered, holy,
lines.note: eiarinai = “vernal”; leimoniades suggests nymph-like “meadow-maidens”; hagnai = “holy/pure.”

lines.gr: παντόχροοι, πολύοδμοι ἐν ἀνθεμοειδέσι πνοιαῖς,
lines.en: all-hued, much-scented in flowerlike breaths,
lines.note: pantokhrooi = “all-hued” (from khrōs, “complexion/colour,” not from khronos, “time”); anthemoeidesi pnoiais literally “flower-like breaths/breezes,” i.e., fragrances.

lines.gr: Ὧραι ἀειθαλέες, περικυκλάδες, ἡδυπρόσωποι·
lines.en: Horai ever-blooming, circling, sweet-faced,
lines.note: perikuklades is a rare epithet, “circling/all-circling,” evoking both round dances and the seasonal cycle (some MSS have similar forms like perikykl-).

lines.gr: πέπλους ἑννύμεναι δροσεροὺς ἀνθέων πολυθρέπτων,
lines.en: arrayed in dewy robes of much-nurturing flowers,
lines.note: peplous hennymenai = “arrayed in robes”; anthēon polythreptōn may be active (“much-nurturing [to many]”) or passive (“much-nurtured”); I take it as active of flowers that feed many (e.g., bees, mortals).

lines.gr: Περσεφόνης συμπαίκτορες, εὖτέ ἑ Μοῖραι
lines.en: playmates of Persephone, when the Moirai
lines.note: sympaiktores = “playmates”; eute he = “when (they) her,” with enclitic he referring to Persephone.

lines.gr: καὶ Χάριτες κυκλίοισι χοροῖς πρ ὸς φ ῶς ἀνάγωσιν.
lines.en: and the Charites lead her up to the light with circling dances,
lines.note: Reading pros phōs anagōsin (“lead her up to the light”); kyklioisi khorois = “in circular dances.” (The spacing in the source is a typographical artifact.)

lines.gr: Ζην ὶ χαριζόμεναι καὶ μητέρι καρπ οδοτείρ ῃ·
lines.en: showing favor to Zeus and to the fruit-bestowing Mother;
lines.note: kharizomenai = “showing favor to/pleasing”; “the fruit-bestowing Mother” is Demeter (Mētēr karpodoteira). (Spacing in source ‘karp-’ is accidental.)

lines.gr: ἔλθετ’ ἐπ’ εὐφήμους τελετὰς ὁσίας νεομύστοις,
lines.en: come to the auspicious, holy rites for the newly-initiated,
lines.note: euphēmous in ritual contexts = “requiring/marked by auspicious silence”; teletai hosiai = “holy rites”; neomystois = “newly-initiated.”

lines.gr: εὐκάρπους καιρῶν γενέσεις ἐπάγουσαι ἀμεμφ ῶς.
lines.en: bringing on without reproach the well-fruited births of the seasons.
lines.note: eukarpous geneseis = “well-fruited births/becomings”; kairōn = “of the seasons/appointed times”; amemphōs = “without reproach.” (Source spacing ‘amemph-’ is accidental.)

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω κούρην Καδμη ΐδα παμβασίλειαν,
lines.en: I invoke the Kadmeian maiden, the all-queen,
lines.note: Καδμηΐδα = “Kadmeian,” i.e., Theban (of Kadmos). Παμβασίλειαν literally “all-queen,” a typical Orphic superlative epithet.

lines.gr: εὐειδ ῆ Σεμέλην, ἐρατοπλόκαμον, βαθύκολπον,
lines.en: fair-formed Semelê, lovely-tressed, deep-bosomed,
lines.note: Epic epithets: εὐειδής “fair-formed,” ἐρατοπλόκαμος “lovely-haired,” βαθύκολπος “deep-/full-bosomed.”

lines.gr: μητέρα θυρσοφόροιο Διωνύσου πολυγηθοῦς,
lines.en: mother of thyrsus-bearing Dionysos, much-rejoicing,
lines.note: θυρσοφόρος “thyrsus-bearing” marks Dionysos’ cult; πολυγηθής “much-rejoicing,” an epithet of Bacchic joy.

lines.gr: ἣ μεγάλας ὠδῖνας ἐλάσσατο πυρφόρ ῳ αὐγῇ,
lines.en: who endured great birth-pangs beneath the fire-bearing ray,
lines.note: πυρφόρῳ αὐγῇ “fire-bearing ray” alludes to Zeus’ lightning; ἐλάσσατο (mid.) “underwent/forced through” of labor-pangs.

lines.gr: ἀθανάτοιο τεκο ῦσα Διὸς βουλα ῖς Κρονίοιο·
lines.en: having borne by the counsels of immortal Zeus, the Kronian;
lines.note: Διὸς βουλαῖς Κρονίοιο = “by the counsels of Kronian Zeus”; Κρόνιος is Zeus’ epithet (“son of Kronos”).

lines.gr: τιμ ὰς τευξαμένη παρ’ ἀγαυ ῆς Περσεφονείης
lines.en: having won honors from august Persephoneia,
lines.note: τιμὰς τευξαμένη “having obtained honors” from Persephoneia hints at Semele’s posthumous deification (as Thyônê) in the Underworld.

lines.gr: ἐν θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἀνὰ τριετηρίδας ὥρας,
lines.en: among mortal men throughout the trieteric seasons,
lines.note: τριετηρίδες “trieteric” refers to the (bi‑)annual/triennial Dionysiac festival cycle; θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσι is a pleonastic “among mortals.”

lines.gr: ἡνίκα σο ῦ Βάκχου γονίμην ὠδῖνα τελ ῶσιν,
lines.en: whenever they perform the fruitful birth-pang of your Bakchos,
lines.note: γονίμην ὠδῖνα “fruitful birth-pang”: ritual reenactment of Semelê’s labor in Bacchic rites; “your Bakchos” = her son Dionysos.

lines.gr: εὐΐερόν τε τράπεζαν ἰδὲ μυστήριά θ’ ἁγνά.
lines.en: both the well-holy table and the pure mysteries.
lines.note: εὐίερον “well-holy” (perhaps echoing the Bacchic cry euoi); τράπεζα “table” = cultic banquet; μυστήρια ἁγνά “pure mysteries.”

lines.gr: νῦν σέ, θεά, λίτομαι, κούρη Καδμηῒς ἄνασσα,
lines.en: Now you, goddess, I beseech, Kadmeian maiden, queen,
lines.note: Vocative accumulation heightens the prayer; “Kadmeian” again stresses Semelê’s Theban identity.

lines.gr: πρη ΰνοον καλέων αἰεὶ μύστῃσιν ὑπάρχειν.
lines.en: to be ever present, gentle of mind, for the initiates.
lines.note: πρηΰνοον “gentle of mind, kindly-disposed”; ὑπάρχειν “be present/assist” is a conventional Orphic prayer ending; μύσται = initiates.

hymns.title: Ὕμνος Διονύσου Βασσαρέως Τριετηρικού.

lines.gr: Ἐλθέ, μάκαρ Διόνυσε, πυρίσπορε, ταυρομέτωπε,
lines.en: Come, blessed Dionysos, fire-sown, bull-browed,
lines.note: πυρίσπορε literally “fire-sown” (often understood of Dionysos’ thunder/fire birth); ταυρομέτωπε = “bull-browed,” a standard Bacchic epithet.

lines.gr: Βάσσαρε καὶ Βακχε ῦ, πολυώνυμε, παντοδυνάστα,
lines.en: O Bassareus and Bakkhos, much-named, all-sovereign ruler,
lines.note: Βάσσαρε is the Thracian epithet Bassareus (from the fox-skin, bassaris); Βακχεῦ is a vocative form related to Bakkhos (many mss. read Βάκχε). παντοδυνάστα = “all-powerful ruler.”

lines.gr: ὃς ξίφεσιν χαίρεις ἠδ’ αἵματι, Μαινάσι θ’ ἁγνα ῖς·
lines.en: who delight in swords and in blood, and in holy Mainads;
lines.note: The delight “in swords and blood” evokes orgiastic/sacrificial aspects of Bacchic rites; Μαινάδες (“Mainads”) are his possessed female votaries, here called “holy.”

lines.gr: εὐάζων κατ’ Ὄλυμπον, ἐρίβρομε, μαινόλα Βάκχε,
lines.en: uttering the euai-cry through Olympus, loud-roaring, frenzied Bakkhos,
lines.note: εὐάζων denotes the ritual cry euai/euoi; ἐρίβρομε = “loud-roaring”; μαινόλα = “raving, frenzied.”

lines.gr: θυρσεγχής, βαρύμηνι, τετιμένε πᾶσι θεοῖσιν
lines.en: thyrsus-armed, of heavy wrath, honored by all the gods
lines.note: θυρσεγχής is “thyrsus-armed” (—εγχής ‘spear-wielding’ used with the thyrsus); βαρύμηνι = “of heavy wrath”; τετιμένε is passive “honored by.”

lines.gr: καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν, ὅσοι χθόνα ναιετάουσιν·
lines.en: and by mortal men, all who dwell upon the earth;
lines.note: θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν is a pleonastic “mortal mortals,” intensifying universality; ναιετάουσιν = “dwell.”

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σκιρτητά, φέρων πολὺ γῆθος ἅπασιν.
lines.en: come, blessed one, leaper, bringing abundant rejoicing to all.
lines.note: σκιρτητά = “leaper/dancer,” a Bacchic epithet; γῆθος = “gladness, rejoicing.”

hymns.title_english: Hymn to Dionysos Bassareus, of the Trieteric rite

lines.gr: Βικνίτην Διόνυσον ἐπ’ ευχα ῖς τα ῖσδε κικλήσκω,
lines.en: I call upon Dionysos Liknitēs at these prayers,
lines.note: Βικνίτην = Λικνίτην (Liknitēs), the epithet of Dionysos associated with the liknon (winnowing‑fan/cradle) used in his mysteries; I translate with the cult title preserved.

lines.gr: ȃύσιον, ἀμφιθαλ ῆ, πεποθημένον, εὔφρονα Ǻάκχον·
lines.en: holy, both‑thriving, much‑desired, kindly Bakchos;
lines.note: The transmitted ȃύσιον is likely ἁγνίον/ἁγνόν (“holy”). ἀμφιθαλής can mean “having both parents alive” (apt for the divine child) or “flourishing on both sides,” a viticultural image; I render it as “both‑thriving.” “εὔφρων” in cultic address = “kindly/propitious.”

lines.gr: νυμφέων ἔρνος ἐραστόν, ἐ Ȩστεφάνου τ’ ਝφροδίτης,
lines.en: beloved shoot of bridal chambers, and of well‑crowned Aphroditē,
lines.note: νυμφέων ἔρνος = “shoot/offshoot of bridal chambers,” a genealogical and fertility metaphor; ἐὖ/εὐ‑στεφάνου (“well‑crowned/garlanded”) modifies Aphroditē, highlighting festal adornment.

lines.gr: ὅς ποτ’ ἀνὰ δρυμο ઃς κεχορευμένα βήματα πάλλες
lines.en: who once amid the woodlands you shook with your danced steps,
lines.note: κεχορευμένα βήματα πάλλεις is a vivid idiom: “you shake/brandish danced steps,” i.e., set dancing in motion; I keep the energetic metaphor of πάλλειν.

lines.gr: σઃν νύμφαις χαρίεσσιν, ἐλαυνόμενος μανί ૉσιν.
lines.en: with the graceful Nymphs, driven along by frenzies.
lines.note: μανίαισιν (“frenzies”) is the Bacchic mania that drives the dance; Nymphs are Dionysiac companions.

lines.gr: καὶ βουλ ૌσι Διὸς πρ ὸς ἀγαυ ήν ĭερσεφόνειαν
lines.en: and, by the counsels of Zeus, to proud Persephonē
lines.note: βουλαῖσι Διός… πρὸς ἀγαυὴν Περσεφόνειαν alludes to the Orphic myth in which Zeus’ counsel sends the divine child to Persephonē (the Zagreus/Dionysos tradition).

lines.gr: ἀχθε ὶς ἐȟετράφης, φίλος ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν.
lines.en: being borne, you were reared, dear to the immortal gods.
lines.note: ἀχθεὶς ἐξετράφης is the likely reading (text shows corruption): “having been borne/carried, you were reared.” φίλος ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν is a standard hymn formula (“dear to the immortal gods”).

lines.gr: εὔφρων ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, κεχαρισμένα δ’ ੂερὰ δέȟαι.
lines.en: Come propitious, blessed one, and receive these pleasing rites.
lines.note: δέχαι is a poetic/variant imperative for “receive” (cf. δέξαι/δέχου). κεχαρισμένα ἱερά = “pleasing/gracious rites,” the offerings of the hymnists.

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω Βάκχον περικιόνιον, μεθυδώτην,
lines.en: I summon Bakchos, pillar‑encircling, bestower of wine,
lines.note: perikionion literally “around‑pillared,” an epithet evoking ivy that twines about columns; methydotēs (= μεθυδώτης) is “giver of wine/intoxication.”

lines.gr: Καδμείοισι δόμοις ὃς ἑλισσόμενος πέρι πάντη,
lines.en: who, coiling all around on every side within the Kadmeian halls,
lines.note: “Kadmeian halls” = Thebes (founded by Kadmos). helissomenos (“coiling”) and peri pantē (“all around on every side”) reinforce the imagery of ivy winding about pillars.

lines.gr: ἔστησε κρατεροῦς βρασμοὺς γαίης ἀποπέμψας·
lines.en: stilled the mighty seethings of the earth, having driven them away;
lines.note: brasmoi (“boilings, seethings”) is a vivid metaphor for earthquake‑tremors; estēse … apopempsas = “stilled … by sending [them] away.”

lines.gr: ἡνίκα πυρφόρος αὐγὴ ἐ κίνησε χθόνα πᾶσαν,
lines.en: when the fire‑bearing radiance set the whole earth in motion,
lines.note: pyrphoros augē (“fire‑bearing radiance”) most naturally alludes to the lightning of Zeus; the scene recalls the Theban mythic setting (Semelē’s conflagration) and ensuing earth‑shaking.

lines.gr: πρηστ ῆρος ῥοίζοις · ὃ δ’ ἀνέδραμε δεσμὸς ἁπάντων.
lines.en: with the whirrings of the whirlwind; and up sprang the bond of all things.
lines.note: The transmitted πρηστ ῆρος is to be read πρηστήρος (“of the whirlwind”); ῥοίζοις = “with whirrings/roarings.” “The bond of all things” (desmos hapantōn) likely denotes ivy, which “sprang up” (anédrame, a verb often used of plant growth) and binds/steadies; some read it as a cosmic “bond,” but the ivy imagery fits the context.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, βακχευτά, γεγηθυίαις πραπίδεσσιν.
lines.en: Come, blessed one, Bacchic leader, with rejoicing mind.
lines.note: bakcheutā (“Bacchic leader/reveler”) addresses Dionysus as instigator of Bacchic rites. prapides, literally the midriff, denotes the seat of thought/feeling; hence “mind/heart.”

lines.gr: Κλῦθι, πάτερ, Κρόνου υἱέ Σαβάζιε, κύδιμε δαῖμον,
lines.en: Hear, father, Sabazios, son of Kronos, illustrious daimon,
lines.note: Calling Sabazios “son of Kronos” aligns him with Zeus; daimon here means a divine power, not a malevolent “demon.”

lines.gr: ὃς Βάκχον Διόνυσον ἐ ρίβρομον, εἰραφιώτην
lines.en: who Bakchos Dionysos, loud-roaring, the Sewn-in,
lines.note: eribromos = “loud-roaring”; Eiraphiotēs (“Sewn‑in”) is an epithet of Dionysos referring to his being sewn into Zeus’s thigh. The spacing in the source (ἐ ρίβρομον) reflects a typographical issue; read ἐρίβρομον.

lines.gr: μηρῷ ἐ γκατέραψας, ὅπως τετελεσμένος ἔλθοι
lines.en: didst sew into your thigh, so that, perfected, he might come
lines.note: μηρῷ ἐγκατέραψας is a compound of rhaptō (“stitch”) with preverbs, “sew/fasten in(to)”; it alludes to the myth of Dionysos’s gestation in Zeus’s thigh. τετελεσμένος can mean “brought to completion,” with possible wordplay on teletai (“mysteries”).

lines.gr: Τμῶλον ἐς ἠγάθεον, παρὰ θ’ Ἵ ππαν καλλιπάρῃον.
lines.en: to holy Tmolos, and beside Hippa of the lovely cheeks.
lines.note: Τμῶλος is the Lydian mountain; ἠγάθεον = “holy/sacred.” Ἵππαν (“Hippa”) is likely the Lydian/Phrygian goddess Hipta/Hippa, associated with Sabazios and Dionysos; the identification and form are debated in the tradition.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, Φρυγίης μεδέων, βασιλεύτατε πάντων,
lines.en: But, blessed one, lord of Phrygia, most kingly of all,

lines.gr: εὐμενέων ἐπαρωγὸς ἐπέλθοις μυστιπόλοισιν.
lines.en: with good will come as a helper to the mystic celebrants.
lines.note: εὐμενέων is a genitive of manner, “with good will.” μυστιπόλοι are “mystery‑servers/celebrants,” those who conduct or participate in the rites; ἐπαρωγός = “helper/ally.”

lines.gr: Ἵππαν κικλήσκω Βάκχου τροφόν, εὐάδα κούρην,
lines.en: I invoke Hipta, nurse of Bakchos, Euiad maiden,
lines.note: Ἵππαν likely reflects the goddess Hipta (often printed Ἵπτα; acc. Ἵπταν), a Phrygian/Lydian nurse of Dionysus. “Euiad” (εὐάδα) = Bacchic, ‘crying euoi’.

lines.gr: μυστι πόλο ν τελετ ῇσιν ἀγαλλομένην Σάβου ἁγνο ῦ,
lines.en: mystic-serving, exulting in the rites of holy Sabos,
lines.note: μυστιπόλον = ‘minister/attendant of mysteries’; τελεταῖσιν = ‘rites/initiations’. Σάβου (gen.) is probably Sabos = Sabazios, the Anatolian god associated with Dionysiac cult.

lines.gr: νυκτερίοισι τε χοροῖσιν ἐριβρεμέταο Ἰάκχου.
lines.en: and in the nocturnal choruses of loud‑roaring Iakkhos.
lines.note: ἐριβρεμέταο = ‘very‑roaring, thunder‑voiced.’ Ἰάκχος (Iakkhos) is both the cult‑cry and a deity linked with Eleusinian/Dionysiac processions.

lines.gr: κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, χθονίη μήτηρ, βασίλεια,
lines.en: Hear me praying, chthonian Mother, sovereign Queen,
lines.note: “Chthonian Mother” may point to Rhea/Kybele or Gaia; the title βασίλεια (‘Queen’) suits an Anatolian Great Mother.

lines.gr: εἴτε σύ γ’ ἐν Φρυγίῃ κατέχεις Ἴδης ὄρος ἁγνὸν,
lines.en: whether you hold in Phrygia the holy mount of Ida,
lines.note: Refers to the Phrygian Ida; the line situates the goddess in Anatolian sacred mountains.

lines.gr: ἢ Τμ ῶλος τέρπει σε, καλὸν Λυδο ῖσι θόασμα·
lines.en: or Tmolos delights you, a fair tumult to the Lydians;
lines.note: θόασμα = ‘rushing noise, din, tumult,’ perhaps of streams (Tmolos/Pactolus) or of orgiastic music; hence ‘fair tumult’ for Lydians.

lines.gr: ἔρχεο πρὸς τελετὰς ἱερῷ γηθο ῦσα προσώπῳ.
lines.en: come to the rites, rejoicing with sacred countenance.
lines.note: ἱερῷ προσώπῳ (‘with holy face’) is a cultic idiom for a gracious epiphany; ἔρχεο is an imperative ‘come’.

lines.gr: Κλῦθι, μάκαρ, Διὸς υ ੈ’, ἐπιλήνιε Ǻάκχε, διμήτωρ,
lines.en: Hear, blessed one, son of Zeus, Iacchos of the wine‑press, twice‑mothered,
lines.note: ἐπιλήνιε = ‘of/at the wine‑press’ (Lenaean epithet). διμήτωρ = ‘twice‑mothered,’ alluding to Dionysus’ birth from Semelē and from Zeus’ thigh.

lines.gr: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον, πολυώνυμε, λύσιε δαῖμον.
lines.en: much‑remembered seed, much‑named, liberating daimon.
lines.note: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον ‘much‑remembered seed’ evokes the ever‑remembered generative power; λύσιε ‘Liberator’ (Lysios) is a Dionysiac epithet for releasing cares/bonds.

lines.gr: κρυψίγονον μακάρων ੂερὸν θάλος, εὔȧε Ǻάκχε,
lines.en: secretly‑born, holy shoot of the Blessed, Euie Iacchos,
lines.note: κρυψίγονον ‘secretly born’ (the hidden gestation in Zeus’ thigh). θάλος ‘shoot/sprout’ of vegetation. εὔιε is the Bacchic cry (Euoi). ‘Blessed’ = the gods.

lines.gr: εὐτραφές, εὔκαρπος , πολυγηθέα καρπὸν ἀέȟων,
lines.en: well‑nourished, fruitful, fostering the much‑delighting fruit,

lines.gr: ῥηȟίχθων, ληναῖε, μεγασθενές, αἰολόμορφε·
lines.en: door‑breaking, Lenaean, mighty in strength, changeful in form;
lines.note: The transmitted epithet is uncertain; many print ῥηξίθυρε ‘breaker of doors’ (cf. Bacchic assaults in Eur. Bacch.). Hence ‘door‑breaking.’ αἰολόμορφε ‘of changeful form’ marks Dionysus’ polymorphy.

lines.gr: παυσίπονον θνητοῖσι φανε ὶς ਙκος, ੂερὸν ਙνθος,
lines.en: manifest remedy that ends pain for mortals, holy blossom,
lines.note: ἄκος ‘remedy/cure’—wine as a visible, pain‑ending balm; ἄνθος ‘blossom,’ likely of the vine.

lines.gr: χάρμα βροτοῖς φιλάλυπον, ἐφάπτορ , καλλιέθειρε,
lines.en: a joy to mortals, lover of freedom from grief, bringer‑on, fair‑tressed,
lines.note: φιλάλυπον ‘fond of freedom from grief,’ i.e., relieving sorrow. ἐπάκτωρ ‘bringer‑on’ (of desire or Bacchic fervor). καλλιέθειρε ‘fair‑tressed.’

lines.gr: λύσιε, θυρσομανές, βρόμι’, ε ὔȧε, π઼σιν ἐ૥φρων,
lines.en: Liberator, thyrsus‑mad, Bromios, Euie, kindly‑minded to all,
lines.note: θυρσομανές ‘mad for the thyrsus.’ Βρόμιος ‘Roarer.’ Reading ‘πᾶσιν ἐπήφρων’ (‘kindly‑minded to all’); some editors have ἐπήρωος ‘helper to all.’

lines.gr: οੈς ἐθέλεις θνητ૵ν ἠδ’ ἀθανάτων σἐπιφαύσκειν·
lines.en: upon whom you choose to shine forth among mortals and immortals;
lines.note: ἐπιφαύσκειν ‘to shine forth’ is technical for divine epiphany and selective revelation.

lines.gr: νῦν σε καλ ૵ μύστૉ σι μολε ῖν ਲδύν, φερέκαρπον.
lines.en: now I call you to come sweetly to the mystai, fruit‑bearing.
lines.note: μύσται ‘initiates,’ pointing to the Eleusinian Iacchos. φερέκαρπος ‘fruit‑bearing,’ of fertility/viticulture.

lines.gr: Νύμφαι, θυγατέρες μεγαλήτορος Ὠκεανοῖο,
lines.en: Nymphs, daughters of great‑hearted Oceanos,
lines.note: μεγαλήτωρ “great‑hearted”; Oceanos is the mythic progenitor of rivers and Nymphs.

lines.gr: ὑγροπόροις γαίης ὑπὸ κεύθεσιν οἰκί’ ἔχουσαι,
lines.en: holding your dwellings beneath the earth’s hollows along watery ways,
lines.note: ὑγροπόροις “with watery passages/ways” evokes subterranean aquifers; ὑπὸ κεύθεσιν “under the hidden hollows.”

lines.gr: κρυψίδ ομοι, Βάκχοιο τροφοί, χθόνιαι, πολυγηθεῖς,
lines.en: secret‑stepping, nurses of Bakchos, chthonian, much‑rejoicing,
lines.note: The epithet is textually uncertain: often κρύφιοι (“hidden”) or κρυψίδρομοι (“secret‑stepping”); I render the sense “secret‑stepping.” “Nurses of Bakchos” reflects Dionysiac nurture myths.

lines.gr: καρποτρόφοι, λειμωνιάδες, σκολιοδρόμοι, ἁγναί,
lines.en: fruit‑fostering, meadow‑maidens, of winding courses, holy,
lines.note: σκολιοδρόμοι “of crooked/winding courses,” suited to meandering stream‑beds; λειμωνιάδες “meadow‑maidens.”

lines.gr: ἀντρο χαρε ῖς, σπήλυγξι κεχαρμέναι, ἠερόφοιτοι.
lines.en: cave‑delighting, rejoicing in grottoes, air‑wandering,
lines.note: ἀντροχαρεῖς “cave‑delighting”; σπήλυγξι “in grottoes”; ἠερόφοιτοι “air‑wandering,” suggesting misty, liminal movement.

lines.gr: πηγα ῖαι, δρομάδες, δροσοείμονες, ἴχνεσι κοῦφαι ·
lines.en: of springs, fleet, dew‑clad, light in your footprints,
lines.note: δροσοείμονες “dew‑clad” (elsewhere a variant δροσοέμβροτοι, “rain‑drenched”); ἴχνεσι κοῦφαι “light in footfall/footprints.”

lines.gr: φαινόμεναι, ἀφανεῖς, α ὐλωνιάδες, πολυανθεῖς·
lines.en: manifest, unseen, vale‑maidens, abounding in flowers,
lines.note: αὐλωνιάδες “Auloniads,” nymphs of dells/vales; the pairing “appearing, unseen” marks their elusive epiphany.

lines.gr: σὺν Πανὶ σκιρτ ῶσαι ἀν’ ο ὔρεα, εὐάστειραι,
lines.en: skipping with Pan over the mountains, crying euai,
lines.note: εὐαστῇραι/εὐάστειραι “crying euai,” the Bacchic shout; σκιρτῶσαι “skipping, frisking.”

lines.gr: πετρόρυτοι, λιγυραί, κρουνίτιδες ὑλονόμοι τε·
lines.en: rock‑gushing, clear‑voiced, fountain‑maidens and wood‑ranging,
lines.note: πετρόρυτοι “gushing from rock”; κρουνίτιδες (also κρήνιτιδες) “fountain‑nymphs”; ὑλονόμοι “wood‑ranging.”

lines.gr: παρθένοι εὐώδεις, λευχείμονες, εὔπνοοι αὔραις,
lines.en: fragrant maidens, white‑clad, fanned by kindly breezes,
lines.note: λευχείμονες “white‑clad”; εὔπνοοι αὔραις “well‑breathed/fanned by kindly breezes” (instrumental dative).

lines.gr: αἰπολικαί, νόμιαι, θηρσὶν φίλαι, ἀγλαόκαρποι,
lines.en: goatherding, pastoral, dear to wild beasts, splendid‑fruited,
lines.note: αἰπολικαί “goatherding”; νόμιαι from νόμιος “pastoral”; θηρσὶν φίλαι “dear to beasts.”

lines.gr: δρυμοχαρεῖς, ἁπαλαί, πολυθρέμμονες, αὐξίτροφοί τε·
lines.en: thicket‑loving, tender, abundant in nurture, growth‑fostering,
lines.note: πολυθρέμμονες “abundant in nurture”; αὐξίτροφοι “growth‑fostering.”

lines.gr: κοῦραι ἁμαδρυάδες, φιλοπαίγμονες, ὑγροκέλευθοι,
lines.en: maidens Hamadryads, fond of play, of watery ways,
lines.note: Ἁμαδρυάδες are tree‑nymphs bound to single trees; ὑγροκέλευθοι “of watery ways/paths.”

lines.gr: Νύσιαι, οἰστρομανεῖς, παιωνίδες, εἰαροτερπεῖς,
lines.en: Nysian, maddened by the gadfly, healing maidens, delighting in spring,
lines.note: Νύσιαι “of Nysa,” the Dionysiac mountain; οἰστρομανεῖς “driven mad by the gadfly” (Bacchic mania); παιωνίδες “healing maidens” (from Paiōn/Paieon).

lines.gr: σὺν Βάκχῳ Δηοῖ τε χάριν θνητοῖσι φέρουσαι·
lines.en: bringing favor to mortals together with Bakchos and Deo,
lines.note: Deo is Demeter; “bringing favor” (χάριν) marks their beneficence with Bakchos and Demeter.

lines.gr: ἔλθετ' ἐπ’ εὐφήμοις ἱεροῖς κεχαρηότι θυμῷ,
lines.en: come to the auspicious rites with gladdened heart,
lines.note: ἐπ’ εὐφήμοις ἱεροῖς “at auspicious/silenced rites,” a ritual formula; κεχαρηότι θυμῷ “with gladdened heart.”

lines.gr: νᾶμα χέουσαι ὑγεινὸν ἀεξιτρόφοισιν ἐν ὥραις.
lines.en: pouring a healthful stream in the seasons that foster increase.
lines.note: νᾶμα “stream, flow”; ἀεξιτρόφοισιν ὥραις “in the seasons that foster increase,” i.e., the growth‑bringing times of year.

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω σε, μάκαρ, πολυώνυμε, μαινόλα, Βακχεῦ,
lines.en: I call upon you, blessed one, of many names, raving-frenzied, Bakcheus,
lines.note: poluōnymos highlights Dionysus’ many aspects; mainolas “raving” conveys Bacchic frenzy.

lines.gr: ταυρόκερως, ληναῖε, πυρίσπορε, Νύσιε, λυσεῦ,
lines.en: bull-horned, of the wine-press, fire-sowing, Nysios, Releaser,
lines.note: Nysios refers to Mt. Nysa, his mythical rearing-place; Lēnaios “of the wine-press”; pyrísporos “fire-sowing” evokes torch-lit rites or lightning.

lines.gr: μηροτρεφής, λικνῖτα, πυρίπνοε, καὶ τελετάρχα·
lines.en: thigh-nurtured, cradle-borne, fire-breathing, and lord of initiations;
lines.note: mērotrephēs “thigh-nurtured” (from Zeus’ thigh); liknītās is “of the winnowing-fan,” the infant’s ritual cradle; pyrípnoos “fire-breathing” metaphorically of inspired fervor; teletárchēs “master of initiations.”

lines.gr: νυκτέρι’, Εὐβουλεῦ, μιτρηφόρε, θυρσοτινάκτα·
lines.en: nocturnal one, Eubouleus, mitra-wearing, thyrsus-shaker;
lines.note: Eubouleus is a chthonic epithet/name (“Good Counsellor”); mitrophóros is “mitra-wearing,” an Eastern-style headband; thyrsotinaktas “one who shakes the thyrsus.”

lines.gr: ὄργιον ἄῤῥητον , τριφυές, κρύφιον Διὸς ἔρνος ·
lines.en: of the ineffable orgia, triple-natured, hidden shoot of Zeus;
lines.note: orgíon árrhēton “ineffable rite” evokes mystery secrecy; triphyḗs is “triple-natured” or “thrice-born”; krýphion Dios hérnos “hidden scion of Zeus.”

lines.gr: πρωτόγον’, ἠ ρικεπα ῖε, θεῶν πάτερ ἠδὲ καὶ υἱέ·
lines.en: primordial one, Erikepaios, father and also son of the gods;
lines.note: Prōtógonos and Ērikepaîos are Orphic names of the primordial god applied to Dionysus; “father and also son of the gods” marks his cyclical, generative identity.

lines.gr: ὠμάδιε, σκηπτοῦχε, χοροιμανές, ἠγέτα κώμων ·
lines.en: raw-feaster, scepter-bearer, mad for the choruses, leader of revel-bands;
lines.note: ōmádios “raw-feaster” (sacrificial raw flesh in ecstatic myth/rite); skēptoûkhos “scepter-bearing”; choroimanḗs “mad for the dances”; hēgeta kōmōn “leader of revels.”

lines.gr: βακχεύων ἁγίας τριετηρίδας ἀμφὶ γαληνάς ·
lines.en: celebrating the holy trieteric festivals amid calms;
lines.note: The trieterides are biennial/third-year Dionysiac festivals; galênai “calms” may refer to serene seasons or metaphorical tranquility of the rites.

lines.gr: ῥηξίχθων, πυριφεγγές, ἐπάπτορ , κο ῦρε διμήτωρ,
lines.en: earth-rending, fire-bright, Epaptor, two-mothered youth,
lines.note: rhēxíchthōn “earth-rending”; pyriphenḗs “fire-bright”; Epáptor is uncertain—often “begetter/assailant” (of women), hence a procreative epithet; koûre dimḗtōr “two-mothered youth” (Semele and Zeus’ thigh).

lines.gr: οὐρεσιφο ῖτα, κερώς, νεβριδοστόλος, ἀμφιέτηρε,
lines.en: mountain-rover, horned one, fawn-skin-clad, of the biennial rite,
lines.note: ouresiphōítas “mountain-rover”; kerōs “horned”; nebridóstolos “clad in fawn-skin (nebris)”; amphietēros “of the biennial rite.”

lines.gr: Παι ὰν θυρσεγχής, ὑποκόλπιε, βοτρυόκοσμε,
lines.en: Paean, thyrsus-grasping, under-bosomed, cluster-adorned,
lines.note: Paean is a healer title; thyrsegkhḗs “thyrsus-grasping”; hypokólpios “under-bosomed,” i.e., carried close to the breast/in the garment’s fold; botryókosmos “garlanded with grape-clusters.”

lines.gr: Βάσσαρε, κισσοχαρής, πολυπάρθενε, καὶ διάκοσμε,
lines.en: Bassareus, ivy-delighting, attended by many maidens, and bestower of order,
lines.note: Bassareus (from bassara, a fox- or fawn-skin garment); kissokharḗs “ivy-delighting”; poluparthenos “attended by many maidens” (Maenads); diákosme is uncertain—‘orderer/adorner’ of the world/rites.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, μύστῃ σι βρύων κεχαρημένος αἰεί.
lines.en: come, blessed one, ever rejoicing, abounding for your initiates.
lines.note: bryōn “abounding, teeming”; mystēs “initiate”; kecharēménos “rejoicing/exultant,” fitting the ritual invocation.

lines.gr: Ἀμφιετῆ καλέω Βάκχον, χθόνιον Διόνυσον,
lines.en: I call Bakkhos Amphietes, chthonian Dionysos,
lines.note: Amphietes is left transliterated; the epithet likely means “wrapped/clad (on all sides),” often taken of Dionysos as richly or ivy‑clad.

lines.gr: ἐγρόμενον κούραις ἅμα νύμφαις εὐπλοκάμοισιν·
lines.en: awakened together with the maid Nymphs of lovely tresses;

lines.gr: ὃς παρὰ Περσεφόνης ἱερο ῖσι δόμοισιν ἰαύων
lines.en: who, abiding beside Persephone’s holy halls,
lines.note: ἰαύων = “abiding, sleeping,” underscoring Dionysos’ chthonian aspect beside Persephone.

lines.gr: κοιμίζει τριετῆρα χρόνον Βακχήϊον ἁγνόν.
lines.en: lulls to rest for a three-year span the holy Bacchic rite;
lines.note: Βακχήϊον ἁγνόν is a substantivized neuter, here “the holy Bacchic rite/revel”; the “three‑year span” alludes to the trieteric cycle of Dionysiac festivals.

lines.gr: αὐτὸς δ’ ἡνίκα τὸν τριετῆ πάλι κῶμον ἐγείρ ῃ,
lines.en: and when he himself rouses again the triennial revel,
lines.note: τριετῆ κῶμον = “triennial revel,” i.e., the trieteris of Dionysiac cult.

lines.gr: εἰς ὕμνον τρέπεται σὺν ἐϋζώνοισι τιθήναις,
lines.en: he turns to hymn with his well‑girdled nurses,
lines.note: “Turns to hymn” (εἰς ὕμνον τρέπεται) marks a ritual shift; “well‑girdled nurses” (τιθαῖναι) are the Nymphs who nurtured the god.

lines.gr: εὐνάζων κινῶν τε χορο ὺς ἐνὶ κυκλάσιν ὥραις.
lines.en: bedding down and setting dances in motion among the circling Horai.
lines.note: εὐνάζων is difficult: lit. “bedding/putting to bed”; here taken as “settling/bedding down” before “setting dances in motion.” “Among the circling Horai” may mean amid the cyclical seasons or literally in company with the goddess Horai.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, χλοόκαρπε, κερασφόρε, κάρπιμε Βάκχε,
lines.en: But come, blessed one, green‑fruited, horn‑bearing, fruitful Bakkhos,
lines.note: Epithets: χλοόκαρπε = “green‑fruited/verdant‑fruited”; κερασφόρε = “horn‑bearing” (bull‑horned Dionysos); κάρπιμε = “fruitful.”

lines.gr: βα ῖν’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν γανόωντι προσώπῳ,
lines.en: step forth to the all‑divine rite with gleaming countenance,
lines.note: πάνθειον τελετήν = “all‑divine rite”; γανόωντι προσώπῳ = “with gleaming/brightened face,” suggesting ritual purity.

lines.gr: εὐϊέροις καρπο ῖσι τελεσσιγόνοισι βρυάζων.
lines.en: brimming with holy, rite‑born fruits.
lines.note: τελεσσιγόνοισι = “born of rites/initiations”; βρυάζων = “brimming, swelling,” conveying abundance of sacred fruits.

hymns.title: Σιληνοῦ, σ ατύρου, Βακχ ῶν

lines.gr: Κλῦθί μευ, ὦ πολύσεμνε τροφεῦ, Βάκχοιο τιθηνέ,
lines.en: Hear me, O most-august fosterer, nurse of Bakchos,
lines.note: ‘Fosterer’ and ‘nurse’ (trophē/ti-thēnē) mark Silenos as Bacchos’ attendant and tutor; Bakchos is transliterated as a divine name.

lines.gr: Σιλην ῶν ὄχ’ ἄριστε, τετιμένε πᾶσι θεοῖσιν
lines.en: best by far of the Silenoi, honored by all the gods
lines.note: Read Σιληνῶν (“of the Silenoi”); Silenoi are Dionysiac companions. τετιμένε is “honored (by),” taking both gods and mortals as agents in the next line.

lines.gr: καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἐπὶ τριετηρίσιν ὥραις,
lines.en: and by mortal men at the trieteric seasons,
lines.note: ‘Trieteric seasons’ (trieterides) are the triennial Dionysiac festivals.

lines.gr: ἁγνοτελής, γεραρός, θιάσου νομίου τελετάρχα·
lines.en: pure in rite, venerable, rite-leader of the pastoral thiasos;
lines.note: ἁγνοτελής = “pure in rites/performing pure rites.” νομίου could mean “pastoral” (from nomē, fitting the rustic thiasos) or “of custom/law” (from nomos); “pastoral” suits the Dionysiac-satyr context. τελετάρχης = “leader of initiations.”

lines.gr: εὐαστής, φιλάγρυπνε σὺν εὐζώνοισι τιθήναις,
lines.en: Eua-shouter, lover of wakefulness, with the well-girdled nurses,
lines.note: εὐαστής = one who cries euai (the Bacchic shout). φιλάγρυπνος = “fond of wakefulness,” i.e., night-vigils. The “well-girdled nurses” are the Nymph-nurses of Dionysus.

lines.gr: Ναΐσι καὶ Βάκχαις ἡγούμενε κισσοφόροισιν·
lines.en: leader of the Naiads and the ivy-bearing Bakchai;
lines.note: Naiads are water nymphs; the Bakchai (“Bacchants”) are the ivy-bearing female devotees of Dionysus.

lines.gr: δεῦρ’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν Σατύροις ἅμα πᾶσιν
lines.en: come hither to the all-divine rite together with all the Satyrs
lines.note: πάνθειος = “all-divine,” marking the rite as of universal divine scope; δεῦρο is a standard epiphanic summons (“come hither”).

lines.gr: θηροτύποις, εὔασμα διδοὺς Βακχείου ἄνακτος,
lines.en: beast-shaped, granting the euas-cry of lord Bakchios,
lines.note: θηροτύποις = “beast-shaped,” a conventional epithet of Satyrs. εὔασμα = the cry euai; here “granting the euas-cry of lord Bakchios.”

lines.gr: σὺν Βάκχαις Λήναια τελεσφόρα σεμνὰ προπέμπων,
lines.en: together with the Bakchai, leading forth the holy Lenaiac celebrations that bring the rites to fulfillment,
lines.note: Λήναια are Dionysiac winter festivals; τελεσφόρα = “bringing rites to fulfillment/consummating.”

lines.gr: ὄργια νυκτιφαῆ τελετα ῖς ἁγίαις ἀναφαίνων,
lines.en: revealing the night-shining orgia in holy initiations,
lines.note: ὄργια are the secret rites of Dionysus (not “orgies” in the modern sense). τελεταί = initiatory rites; νυκτιφαής (“night-shining”) evokes nocturnal revels and torchlight.

lines.gr: εὐάζων, φιλόθυρσε, γαληνιόων θιάσοισιν.
lines.en: crying euai, thyrsus-loving, bringing calm to the thiasoi.
lines.note: φιλόθυρσος = “thyrsus-loving” (the thyrsus is Dionysus’ ivy-twined staff). γαληνιόων = “soothing, bringing calm,” i.e., pacifying the ecstatic bands (thiasoi).

hymns.title_english: To Seilenos, the Satyros, and the Bacchoi

lines.gr: Οὐρανίη , πολύυμνε, φιλομμειδὴς Ἀφροδίτη,
lines.en: Ouraniē, much-hymned, smile-loving Aphroditē,
lines.note: Οὐρανίη ‘heavenly/sky-born’; philommeidēs ‘smile-loving’ is a traditional epithet of Aphroditē.

lines.gr: ποντογενής, γενέτειρα θεά, φιλοπάννυχε, σεμνή,
lines.en: sea-born, begetress goddess, lover of all-night rites, august,
lines.note: philopannychos ‘fond of all-night rites/revels’; geneteira ‘begetress’.

lines.gr: νυκτερίη, ζεύκτειρα, δολοπλόκε μῆτερ ἀνάγκης·
lines.en: nocturnal, yoker, weaver of wiles, mother of Constraint,
lines.note: zēukteira ‘yoker, joiner’; doloploke ‘weaver of wiles’; mētēr anankēs may mean ‘mother of Necessity’ (personified Anankē) or ‘source of compulsion’.

lines.gr: πάντα γὰρ ἐκ σέθεν ἐστίν, ὑπεζεύξω δέ τε κόσμον·
lines.en: for all things are from you, and you yoke the cosmos beneath your sway;
lines.note: hypezēuxō is formally aorist 2nd sg., often understood with gnomic/present force: ‘you yoke’ (bring under your yoke) the kosmos.

lines.gr: καὶ κρατέεις τρισσῶν μοιρ ῶν, γενν ᾷς δὲ τὰ πάντα,
lines.en: you hold power over the three Moirai, and you beget all things,
lines.note: Moirai = the three Fates; gennāis ‘you beget’ stresses cosmic generativity.

lines.gr: ὅσσα τ’ ἐν οὐρανῳ ἐστι καὶ ἐν γαί ῃ πολυκάρπῳ,
lines.en: whatever is in heaven and in the much-fruited earth,
lines.note: polykárpos ‘much-fruited/abundant in fruit’.

lines.gr: ἐν πόντου τε βυθ ῷ· σεμνὴ Βάκχοιο πάρεδρε,
lines.en: and in the depth of the sea; august seatmate of Bakchos,
lines.note: páredros ‘seatmate/attendant’; here ‘consort/partner’ of Bakchos (Dionysos), reflecting Orphic syncretism.

lines.gr: τερπομένη θαλί ῃσι, γαμοστόλε, μ ῆτερ ἐρώτων·
lines.en: delighting in banquets, arranger of marriage, mother of the Erotes;
lines.note: thalíai ‘banquets/festive feasts’; gamostolé ‘marriage-arranger’; Erotes = winged Loves.

lines.gr: πειθο ῖ λεκτροχαρής, κρυφίη, χαριδῶτι ἄνασσα,
lines.en: with Peithō you are bed-delighting, secret one, queen endowed with Graces,
lines.note: Peithō personified Persuasion; lektra-charēs ‘bed-delighting’; charidōti ‘grace-endowed’ evokes the Charites (Graces).

lines.gr: φαινομένη τ’, ἀφανής τ’, ἐ ρατοπλόκαμ’, εὐπατέρεια,
lines.en: both manifest and unseen, lovely-tressed, well-fathered,
lines.note: ‘Manifest and unseen’ balances epiphany and hidden presence; eratoplokamos ‘lovely-locked’; eupatereia ‘well-sired’ (father variously given as Ouranos/Zeus in different traditions).

lines.gr: νυμφιδίη, σύνδαιτε, θεῶν σκηπτο ῦχε, λύκαινα·
lines.en: bridal goddess, feast-companion, scepter-bearing among the gods, she-wolf;
lines.note: nymphidíē ‘of brides/bridal’; syndáite ‘feast-companion’; theōn skēptouchos ‘scepter-holder among the gods’; lykaina ‘she-wolf’ may hint at fierce/rapacious desire or protective fierceness.

lines.gr: γεννοδότειρα, φίλανδρε, ποθεινοτάτη, βιοδ ῶτι·
lines.en: giver of birth, man-loving, most longed-for, giver of life;
lines.note: gennodoteira ‘giver of birth’; potheinotatē superlative ‘most longed-for’; biodōti ‘giver of life/livelihood’.

lines.gr: ἐνζεύξασα βροτο ὺς ἀχαλινώτοισιν ἀνάγκαις,
lines.en: yoking mortals with unbridled compulsions,
lines.note: enzéuxasa ‘having yoked’; achalinōtois anankais ‘unbridled compulsions’ (oxymoronic, expressing irresistible erotic constraint).

lines.gr: καὶ θηρ ῶν πολ ὺ φῦλον, ἐ ρωμανέων ὑπὸ φίλτρων
lines.en: and the great tribe of beasts, under love-maddening charms,—
lines.note: erōmaneōn philtrōn ‘love-maddening charms/philters’; philtra are magical love-charms.

lines.gr: ἔρχεο, Κυπρογενὲς θε ῖον γένος, εἴτ’ ἐν’ Ὀλύμπ ῳ
lines.en: come, Kyprogenes, of divine lineage, whether on Olympos
lines.note: Kyprogenes ‘born of/at Cyprus’; theion genos ‘of divine stock/kind’.

lines.gr: ἐσσί, θεὰ βασίλεια, καλῷ γήθουσα προσώπῳ,
lines.en: you abide, queen goddess, rejoicing in your fair face,
lines.note: No special difficulty; the verse highlights epiphanic beauty (‘fair face’).

lines.gr: εἴτε καὶ εὐλιβάνου Συρίης ἕδος ἀμφιπολεύεις,
lines.en: or you attend the seat of incense-rich Syria,
lines.note: eulibanos ‘rich in incense’: Syria evokes Near Eastern cults (Astarte/Ishtar affinities).

lines.gr: εἴτε σύ γ’ ἐν πεδίοισι σὺν ἅρμασι χρυσεοτεύκτοις
lines.en: or in the plains, with chariots fashioned of gold,
lines.note: chryseo-teuktos ‘golden-wrought’; pedía ‘plains’.

lines.gr: Αἰγύπτου κατέχεις ἱερῆς γονιμώδεα λουτρά,
lines.en: you possess the fertile baths of holy Egypt,
lines.note: gonimōdea loútra ‘fertile baths’: likely alluding to the Nile’s life-giving waters/ritual pools; katecheis ‘you possess/hold’.

lines.gr: ἢ καὶ κυανέοισιν ὄχοις ἐπὶ πόντιον οἶδμα
lines.en: or on dark-blue vehicles upon the sea’s swell
lines.note: ochos ‘vehicle/chariot’; kyaneos ‘dark-blue’ fits marine imagery.

lines.gr: ἐρχομένη χαίρεις νεπόδων κυκλί ῃσι χορείαις·
lines.en: as you come you delight in the circling dances of the Nereids;
lines.note: nepodōn is textually uncertain; commonly taken as ‘of the Nereids’ (sea-nymphs), and translated accordingly.

lines.gr: ἢ νύμφαις τέρπῃ κυανώπισιν ἐν χθον ὶ Δίᾳ,
lines.en: or you take pleasure with dark-eyed nymphs on Zeus’s earth,
lines.note: chthoni Diā: either ‘on Zeus’s earth’ (the inhabited world) or the island Dia (near Crete); ambiguity likely intentional.

lines.gr: θυι ὰς ἐπ’ αἰγιαλο ῖς ψαμμώδεσιν ἅλματι κούφ ῳ·
lines.en: with the Thyads on sandy shores, in a light-leaping bound;
lines.note: Thyíai/Thyads = Bacchic women; image of ecstatic leaping on the shore links Dionysian and Aphrodisian rites.

lines.gr: εἴτ’ ἐν Κύπρῳ, ἄνασσα, τροφ ῷ σέο· ἔνθα καλαί σε
lines.en: or in Kypros, O queen, your nurse—there
lines.note: trophos ‘nurse’: Cyprus as Aphroditē’s nurturer.

lines.gr: παρθένοι ἀδμῆται νύμφαι τ’ ἀνὰ πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸ ν
lines.en: fair unwed maidens and brides throughout each year
lines.note: admētai ‘unwed/untamed’ maidens; yearly hymning indicates ongoing cult.

lines.gr: ὑμνο ῦσιν, σέ, μάκαιρα, καὶ ἄμβροτον ἁγνὸν Ἄδωνιν.
lines.en: sing hymns to you, O blessed one, and holy immortal Adōnis.
lines.note: Calling Adōnis ‘ambrotos, hagnos’ (immortal, holy) is cultic hyperbole, despite his mythic mortality.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρα θεά, μάλ’ ἐπήρατον εἶδος ἔχουσα
lines.en: Come, blessed goddess, bearing a most lovely form,
lines.note: No special difficulty.

lines.gr: ψυχ ῇ γάρ σε καλῶ σεμν ῇ
lines.en: for with a solemn soul I summon you
lines.note: Standard Orphic closure: with a ‘reverent/august’ soul (semnē psychē).

lines.gr: ἁγίοισι λόγοισιν.
lines.en: with holy words.
lines.note: Formulaic ending invoking ‘holy words’ (hagioi logoi).

lines.gr: Κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, πολυώνυμε, δαῖμον ἄριστε,
lines.en: Hear me as I pray, O much‑named one, noblest daimon,
lines.note: “daimon” preserves the Greek term for a divine spirit; polyonymos = “much‑named.”

lines.gr: ἁβροκόμη, φιλέρημε, βρύων ὥρῃσι ποθεινα ῖς,
lines.en: soft‑tressed, lover of lonely places, teeming with the longed‑for seasons,
lines.note: φιλέρημε (‘philērēme’) literally “fond of lonely/solitary places” (from ἐρῆμος); βρύων “teeming, swelling,” here of seasonal growth.

lines.gr: Εὐβουλεῦ, πολύμορφε, τροφεῦ πάντων ἀρίδηλε.
lines.en: Eubouleus, many‑shaped, manifest nourisher of all.
lines.note: Eubouleus is a chthonic epithet (often of Hades/Dionysus), signaling syncretism; πολύμορφος = “many‑shaped”; ἀρίδηλος = “manifest, plain to see.”

lines.gr: κούρη καὶ κόρε· πᾶσι καλ ὸν θάλος αἰὲν, Ἄ δωνι,
lines.en: boy and maiden; an ever‑fair blossom for all, Adonis,
lines.note: κούρη καὶ κόρε (“boy and maiden”) marks an androgynous or bi‑gendered aspect; θάλος “blossom” is a set metaphor for youthful beauty. Vocative Ἄδωνι is standard in cult address.

lines.gr: σβεννύμενος λάμπων τε καλαῖς ἐν κυκλάσιν ὥραις·
lines.en: quenched yet radiant within the fair cycles of the Horai;
lines.note: σβεννύμενος/λάμπων (“quenched yet shining”) is a deliberate paradox of extinction and return; Ὧραι (Horai) are the Seasons personified; κυκλάσιν “cycles.”

lines.gr: αὐξιθαλής, δίκερως, πολυήρατε, δακρυότιμε,
lines.en: luxuriantly‑growing, two‑horned, much‑desired, honored with tears,
lines.note: δίκερως “two‑horned” (perhaps lunar/bovine or venatic); δακρυότιμος “honored with tears,” alluding to Adonis‑laments.

lines.gr: ἀγλαόμορφε, κυνηγεσίαις χαίρων, βαθυχα ῖτα·
lines.en: bright in form, rejoicing in the hunt, long‑haired;
lines.note: βαθυχαίτας “deep‑haired” = long‑haired; κυνηγεσίαις χαίρων “rejoicing in the hunt.”

lines.gr: ἱμερόνους, Κύπριδος γλυκερὸν θάλος, ἔρνο ς ἔρωτος·
lines.en: yearning‑souled, sweet blossom of Kypris, shoot of Eros;
lines.note: ἱμερόνους “yearning‑souled, desire‑minded”; Kypris = Aphrodite; ἔρνος ἔρωτος “shoot/sprout of Eros.”

lines.gr: Φερσεφόνης ἐρασιπλοκάμου λέκτροισι λοχευθείς ·
lines.en: born in the beds of lovely‑tressed Persephone;
lines.note: λοχευθείς (from λοχεύω “to bring to birth”): “born in the beds of Persephone,” reflecting an Orphic/chthonic variant of the Adonis myth.

lines.gr: ὃς ποτ ὲ μὲν ναίεις ὑπὸ Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα,
lines.en: you who at one time dwell beneath misty Tartaros,
lines.note: ἀηερόεντα/ἠερόεντα = “misty, murky”; Tartaros is the underworld abyss.

lines.gr: ἠδὲ πάλιν πρ ὸς Ὄλυμπον ἄγεις δέμας ὡριόκαρπον
lines.en: and again you bring your season‑ripe form back toward Olympos;
lines.note: ὡριόκαρπον “season‑ripe”; δέμας “form, body.” The line describes cyclical descent and return.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, μύστῃ σι φέρων καρποὺς ἀπὸ γαίης.
lines.en: come, blessed one, bringing from the earth fruits for the initiates.
lines.note: μύστῃσι dat. pl. “for the initiates (mystai)”; the fruits are both literal and symbolic of fertility/prosperity.

lines.gr: Κωκυτο ῦ ναίων ἀνυπόστροφον οἶμον ἀνάγκης,
lines.en: Dwelling by Kokytos, the unreturning road of Ananke,
lines.note: Κωκυτοῦ ‘of Kokytos’ (the river of lamentation); ἀνυπόστροφον ‘of no turning back’; οἶμον ἀνάγκης ‘the road of Necessity (Ananke)’. The participle ναίων ‘dwelling’ governs the genitive.

lines.gr: ὃς ψυχ ὰς θνητῶν κατάγεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα γαίης,
lines.en: you who lead the souls of mortals down beneath the nether earth,
lines.note: νέρτερα γαίης ‘the nether regions of the earth’ is a conventional periphrasis for the underworld.

lines.gr: Ἑρμῆ , βακχεχόροιο Διωνύσοιο γένεθλον,
lines.en: Hermes, offspring of Bacchic-dancing Dionysos,
lines.note: βακχεχόροιο ‘of Bacchic dance’; γένεθλον ‘offspring/descent’. Calling Hermes the child of Dionysos (and Aphrodite in the next line) is an Orphic variant that has troubled editors; some suspect contamination with hymns to Priapos or Hermaphroditos.

lines.gr: καὶ Παφίης κούρης, ἑλικοβλεφάρου Ἀφροδίτης,
lines.en: and of the Paphian maiden, curl-lashed Aphrodite,
lines.note: Παφίης κούρης ‘the Paphian maiden’ = Aphrodite; ἑλικοβλεφάρου ‘with curling lashes’ is a Homeric-style epithet of feminine beauty.

lines.gr: ὃς παρὰ Περσεφόνης ἱερὸν δόμον ἀμφιπολεύεις,
lines.en: you who attend about Persephone’s sacred house,
lines.note: ἀμφιπολεύεις ‘you attend/minister about’ emphasizes Hermes’ chthonic service at Persephone’s house.

lines.gr: αἰνομόροις ψυχαῖς πομπὸς κατὰ γαῖαν ὑπάρχων·
lines.en: being the escort for the grim-fated souls beneath the earth;
lines.note: αἰνομόροις ‘grim‑fated’; πομπός ‘escort’ evokes Hermes’ title Psychopompos. κατὰ γαῖαν here means ‘beneath/through the earth’.

lines.gr: ἃς κατάγεις, ὁπόταν μοίρης χρόνος εἰσαφίκηται,
lines.en: whom you bring down whenever the time of fate has arrived,
lines.note: μοίρης χρόνος ‘the appointed time of fate’; εἰσαφίκηται ‘has arrived’ is an epic compound.

lines.gr: εὐϊέρῳ ῥάβδῳ θέλγων ὑπνοδώτιδι πάντα,
lines.en: charming all with your well-hallowed, sleep-bestowing staff,
lines.note: εὐϊέρῳ ‘well-hallowed’; ὑπνοδώτιδι ‘sleep-giving’ modifies ῥάβδῳ ‘staff’. The sleep-charming wand recalls Homeric Hermes (Od. 5.47–54).

lines.gr: καὶ πάλιν ὑπνώοντας ἐγείρεις. σοὶ γὰρ ἔδωκεν
lines.en: and again you rouse those who slumber; for to you
lines.note: No special difficulty; the line completes the thought of 8 and leads to the divine grant in 10.

lines.gr: τιμ ὴν Φερσεφόνεια θεὰ, κατὰ Τάρταρο ν εὐρὺν
lines.en: the goddess Persephone granted honor, down through broad Tartaros,
lines.note: Φερσεφόνεια is a variant form of Persephone; κατὰ Τάρταρον εὐρύν ‘down through broad Tartaros’, with κατά expressing extension into depth.

lines.gr: ψυχαῖς ἀενάοις θνητῶν ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύειν.
lines.en: to lead the way for the ever-flowing souls of mortals.
lines.note: ἀενάοις ‘ever-flowing/perpetual’ of the stream of souls; ἡγεμονεύειν ‘to lead/guide’ reiterates Hermes’ psychopompic role.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πέμποις μύσταις τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἔπ’ ἔργοις.
lines.en: But, blessed one, send the mystai a good end upon their deeds.
lines.note: μύσταις ‘mystai, initiates’ retained in transliteration; τέλος ἐσθλόν ‘a good end/outcome’ carries eschatological force in Orphic prayer.

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω μέγαν ἁγνό ν ἐράσμιον ἡδὺν Ἔρωτα,
lines.en: I call upon great, pure, beloved, sweet Eros,

lines.gr: τοξαλκ ῆ, πτερόεντα, πυρίδρομον, εὔδρομον ὁρμῇ,
lines.en: bow-armed, winged, fire-running, swift in onset,
lines.note: Epithets: toxalkēs = ‘bow-armed’; pyridromos = ‘fire-running’ (i.e., moving with the speed of fire); eúdromos hormē = ‘swift in onset/impulse.’

lines.gr: συμπαίζοντα θεοῖς ἠδὲ θνητο ῖς ἀνθρώποις·
lines.en: playing with the gods and with mortal human beings;
lines.note: ‘Playing’ (sympaizonta) conveys Eros’ sportive yet pervasive activity among gods and humans.

lines.gr: εὐπάλαμον, διφυῆ, πάντων κλη ῗδας ἔχοντα,
lines.en: deft-handed, two-natured, holding the keys of all,
lines.note: eupálamos = ‘good in the hand,’ hence ‘deft-handed’; difyēs = ‘two-natured,’ often of Orphic Eros as androgynous or embodying cosmic dualities; ‘keys’ signify cosmic governance of realms.

lines.gr: αἰθέρος οὐρανίου, πόντου, χθονός, ἠδ’ ὅσα θνητο ῖς
lines.en: of the heavenly aether, the sea, the earth, and whatever to mortals

lines.gr: πνεύματα παντογένεθλα θεὰ βόσκει χλοόκαρπος,
lines.en: all-begotten breathing creatures the grass-fruited goddess nourishes,
lines.note: pneumata pantogenethla literally ‘all-begotten breaths/spirits,’ here ‘breathing creatures’; thea chloókarpos ‘grass-fruited goddess’ is commonly Gaia or Demeter as nourisher.

lines.gr: ἠδ’ ὅσα Τ άρταρος εὐρὺς ἔχει, πόντος θ’ ἁλίδουπος ·
lines.en: and all that wide Tartaros holds, and the loud-roaring sea;

lines.gr: μοῦνος γὰρ τούτων πάντων οἴηκα κρατύνεις.
lines.en: for of all these you alone indeed wield the sway.
lines.note: The transmitted οἴηκα is best taken as οἴη κα(ί) ‘alone indeed’; hence the emphatic ‘you alone indeed’ rule all these. Kratyneis = ‘wield mastery, exercise dominion.’

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, καθαραῖς γνώμαις μύστῃ σι συνέρχου,
lines.en: But, blessed one, with pure intentions come to the initiates,
lines.note: mystēsi = ‘to the initiates’ (mystai); synerchou = ‘come/attend, join with’ in a ritual sense; gnōmais = ‘intentions, thoughts.’

lines.gr: φαύλους δ’ ἐκτοπίους θ’ ὁρμὰ ς ἀπὸ τῶνδ’ ἀπόπεμπε.
lines.en: and drive away from them base and alien impulses.
lines.note: phaulous … ektopious hormas = ‘base and out-of-place (alien) impulses,’ a standard Orphic prayer for moral purification of initiates.

lines.gr: Μοῖραι ἀπειρέσιοι, Νυκτὸς φίλα τέκνα μελαίνης,
lines.en: Boundless Moirai, dear children of black Nyx,
lines.note: ἀπειρέσιοι = “boundless,” a Homeric-form epithet; Nyx is the personified Night.

lines.gr: κλῦτέ μου εὐχομένου, πολυώνυμοι, αἵτ’ ἐπὶ λίμνης
lines.en: hear me praying, you many-named, who by the lake
lines.note: πολυώνυμοι (“many-named”) is a cultic epithet signaling multiple epithets/titles of the goddesses.

lines.gr: οὐρανίας, (ἵνα λευκ ὸν ὕδωρ νυχίας ὑπὸ θερμ ῆς
lines.en: of heaven (where the white water of night, by nocturnal heat,
lines.note: The imagery of the “heavenly lake” and “white water of night” is obscure; many take it as an allusion to the Milky Way. νυχίας ὑπὸ θερμῆς (“by nocturnal heat”) is puzzling and may conceal textual difficulties.

lines.gr: ῥήγνυται ἐν σκιερ ῷ λιπαρο ῦ μυχ ῷ εὐλίθου ἄντρου)
lines.en: bursts forth in the shady recess of a sleek-stoned, well-rocked cave),
lines.note: λιπαρός literally “sleek, shining,” here of the cave; εὐλίθου “well-stoned” (i.e., smoothly rock-lined).

lines.gr: ναίουσαι, πεπότησθε βροτῶν ἐπ’ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν
lines.en: dwelling there, yet you flit over the boundless earth of mortals,
lines.note: πεπότησθε is formally a perfect but often carries present sense (“you fly/flit”) in epic diction.

lines.gr: ἔνθεν ἐπὶ βρότεον δοῦλον γένος ἐλπίδι κοῦφῃ
lines.en: whence toward the mortal, slavish race, with light hope,
lines.note: δοῦλον γένος (“slavish race”) is a traditional Orphic-Anthropogonic topos; ἐλπίδι κοῦφῃ = “with light/fickle hope.”

lines.gr: στείχετε πορφυρέ ῃσι καλ υψάμεναι ὀθόν ῃσι,
lines.en: you go, veiling yourselves in purple linens,
lines.note: ὀθόναι are fine linen veils; πορφυρέαι denotes purple (royal/ritual) coloration.

lines.gr: μορσίμῷ ἐν πεδί ῳ, ὅ θι πάγγεον ἅρμα διώκει
lines.en: in the fated plain, where Glory drives the all-embracing chariot
lines.note: δόξα (nominative) is the subject of διώκει; πάγγεον ἅρμα (“all-embracing chariot”) is uncertain in force—likely a cosmic vehicle of governance.

lines.gr: δόξα, δίκης παρὰ τέρμα καὶ ἐλπίδος ἠδὲ μεριμν ῶν,
lines.en: beside the boundary of Justice and of Hope and of cares,
lines.note: παρὰ τέρμα = “beside the boundary/limit,” marking a liminal cosmic region in which abstract powers are localized.

lines.gr: καὶ νόμου ὠγύγιον παναπείρονος εὐνόμου ἀρχῆς.
lines.en: and the Ogygian ordinance, the origin of boundlessly well-ordered rule.
lines.note: ὠγύγιον = “Ogygian, primeval”; ἀρχή “origin/principle”; the phrase presents primordial Law as source of boundless, well-ordered rule.

lines.gr: Μοῖρα γὰρ ἐν βιότ ῳ καθορ ᾷ μόνον , οὐδέ τις ἄλλος
lines.en: For in life only Moira sees clearly, and no other
lines.note: Μοῖρα in the singular personifies Fate; the exclusivity (“only Moira sees”) sets up the contrast with Zeus in the next lines.

lines.gr: ἀθανάτων, οἳ ἔχουσι κάρη νιφόεντος Ὀλύμπου,
lines.en: of the immortals who hold the peak of snowy Olympos,

lines.gr: καὶ Διὸς ὄμμα τέλειον ἐπεί γ’ ὅσα γίγνεται ἡμῖν,
lines.en: nor even the perfect eye of Zeus; since whatever befalls us,
lines.note: Many editors understand an implicit οὐδὲ (“nor even”) before Διὸς ὄμμα to fit the sense; I translate accordingly.

lines.gr: Μοῖρά τε καὶ Διὸς ο ἶδε νόος δι ὰπαντὸς ἅπαντα.
lines.en: Moira and the mind of Zeus know all things through and through.
lines.note: διὰ παντὸς ἅπαντα = “through and through all things,” i.e., completely, universally.

lines.gr: ἀλλά μοι, ἀέριοι , μαλακόφρονες, ἠπιόθυμοι,
lines.en: But come to me, airy ones, soft-minded, gentle of spirit,
lines.note: ἀέριοι “airy” marks their subtle, aetherial nature; ἠπιόθυμοι “gentle-spirited.”

lines.gr: Ἄτροπε, καὶ Λάχεσι, Κλωθώ, μόλετ’, εὐπατέρειαι,
lines.en: Atrope, and Lachesis, and Klotho, come, nobly-sired,
lines.note: εὐπατέρειαι = “nobly-sired”; though the Moirai are daughters of Nyx in some theogonies, the epithet stresses noble lineage rather than a specific father.

lines.gr: νυκτέριοι, ἀφανεῖς, ἀμετάτροποι, αἰὲν ἀτειρε ῖς,
lines.en: nocturnal, unseen, unchangeable, ever unwearied,
lines.note: ἀμετάτροποι = “unchangeable, not to be turned”; ἀτειρεῖς = “unwearied/unyielding.”

lines.gr: παντοδότειραι, ἀφαιρέτιδες θνητοῖσιν ἀνάγκης,
lines.en: all-giving, removers of Ananke for mortals,
lines.note: ἀφαιρέτιδες θνητοῖσιν ἀνάγκης can mean “removers of Ananke (Necessity) for mortals” or “those who take away (what is due) by Necessity”; I adopt the beneficent nuance suited to prayer.

lines.gr: Μοῖραι, ἀκούσατ’ ἐμῶν ὁσίων λοιβ ῶν τε καὶ εὐχῶν,
lines.en: Moirai, hear my holy libations and prayers,
lines.note: ὁσίων modifies both libations and prayers, marking them as ritually proper/holy offerings.

lines.gr: ἐρχόμεναι μύσταις λαθιπήμονες εὔφρονι βουλ ῇ.
lines.en: coming to the mystai, secretly easing pains with kindly counsel.
lines.note: λαθιπήμονες is semantically ambiguous (“secretly baneful” or “stealthily relieving pain”); in a supplicatory context to the Moirai I take it as “secretly easing pains.”

lines.gr: Κλῦτέ μοι, ὦ Χάριτες μεγαλώνυμοι, ἀγλαότιμοι,
lines.en: Hear me, O Charites, renowned of name, splendidly honored,
lines.note: μεγαλώνυμοι “great‑named, renowned,” and ἀγλαότιμοι “splendidly honored”: paired epithets typical of hymnic style.

lines.gr: θυγατέρες Ζηνός τε καὶ Εὐρυνόμης βαθυκόλπου,
lines.en: daughters of Zeus and deep‑bosomed Eurynome,
lines.note: βαθυκόλπου “deep‑bosomed” is a Homeric epithet of goddesses; Eurynome is the Charites’ mother in some genealogies.

lines.gr: Ἀγλαΐη, Θαλίη τε, καὶ Εὐφροσύνη πολύολβε,
lines.en: Aglaia, and Thalia, and Euphrosyne the much‑blest,
lines.note: πολύολβε “much‑blest” most naturally modifies Euphrosyne alone; divine names are transliterated.

lines.gr: χαρμοσύνης γενέτειραι, ἐράσμιαι, εὔφρονες, ἁγναί,
lines.en: begetters of rejoicing, lovely, kindly‑minded, holy,
lines.note: γενέτειραι literally “begetters”; εὔφρονες can mean “kindly‑minded” as well as “cheerful.”

lines.gr: αἰολόμορφοι, ἀειθαλέες, θνητοῖσι ποθειναί
lines.en: variform, ever‑blooming, longed‑for by mortals—
lines.note: αἰολόμορφοι suggests “shimmering/variform”; ἀειθαλέες “ever‑green, ever‑blooming.”

lines.gr: ὄυτε γὰρ ἠελίου ταχιναὶ φλόγες, οὔτε σελήνης,
lines.en: for neither the swift rays of Helios nor of Selene,
lines.note: φλόγες “flames” is rendered idiomatically as “rays”; Helios and Selene are the deified Sun and Moon.

lines.gr: καὶ σοφίης, ἀρετ ῆς τε, καὶ ἐργασίμου θρασύτητος
lines.en: nor the boast of wisdom and excellence and enterprising boldness,
lines.note: αὔχημ’ (αὔχημα) “boast, proud claim”; ἐργασίμου θρασύτητος is “enterprising/industrious boldness.” Minor spacing in ἀρετῆς is orthographic.

lines.gr: αὔχημ’, ο ὔτε βίου λιπαρῆς περικαλλέος ἥβης
lines.en: nor the resplendent, all‑beautiful bloom of life’s youth,
lines.note: λιπαρῆς “shining, luxuriant”; ἥβη “youth” as the “bloom” of life is conventional epic diction.

lines.gr: ὑμέων χωρὶς ἐγείρει ἐϋφροσύνας βιότοιο.
lines.en: apart from you awakens the good cheer of mortal living.
lines.note: βιότοιο is an epic form “of life”; ἐγείρει “rouses/awakens”; ἐϋφροσύνας “good cheer, merriment.”

lines.gr: εὐκτα ῖαι, κυκλάδες, καλυκώπιδες, ἱμερόεσσαι
lines.en: much‑invoked ones, circle‑dancers, blossom‑eyed, desire‑stirring,
lines.note: εὐκταῖαι “much‑invoked/prayed‑to”; κυκλάδες here means “circle‑dancers,” not the islands; καλυκώπιδες literally “bud‑eyed,” hence “blossom‑eyed.”

lines.gr: ἔλθοιτ’ ὀλβοδότειραι, ἀεὶ μύστ ῃσι προσηνε ῖς.
lines.en: come, givers of prosperity, ever gracious to the mystai.
lines.note: ὀλβοδότειραι “givers of prosperity”; μύστῃσι “to the mystai (initiates)”; προσηνεῖς “gracious, propitious.”

lines.gr: Ὦ Νέμεσι, κλήιζω σε, θεά, βασίλεια μεγίστη,
lines.en: O Nemesis, I invoke you, goddess, greatest queen,
lines.note: κλήιζω (“I invoke/call by name”) marks formal ritual address.

lines.gr: πανδερκής, ἐσορ ῶσα β ίον θνητῶν πολυφύλων·
lines.en: all-seeing, beholding the life of many-tribed mortals;
lines.note: πανδερκής = “all-seeing”; πολυφύλων = “of many tribes/kinds,” characterizing the diversity of mortals.

lines.gr: ἀϊδίη , πολύσεμνε, μόνη χαίρουσα δικαίοις,
lines.en: ageless, much-revered, the only one who takes delight in the just,
lines.note: ἀϊδίη = “ageless/everlasting”; μόνη χαίρουσα δικαίοις underscores Nemesis’ exclusive pleasure in justice.

lines.gr: ἀλλάσσουσα λόγον πολυποίκιλον, ἄστατον αἰεί,
lines.en: adjusting the manifold reckoning, ever inconstant,
lines.note: λόγον πολυποίκιλον “manifold/variegated reckoning/account”; ἀλλάσσουσα “adjusting/altering”; ἄστατον qualifies the ever-unstable ‘reckoning’ of mortal affairs, not caprice in Nemesis.

lines.gr: ἣν πάντες δεδίασι βροτοὶ ζυγ ὸν α ὐχένι θέντες.
lines.en: whom all mortals dread, the yoke set upon the neck.
lines.note: ζυγὸν αὐχένι θέντες is syntactically with βροτοί; sense: mortals dread her, with the yoke set upon their neck. The yoke is a trope for subjection to just retribution.

lines.gr: σοὶ γὰρ ἀεὶ γνώμη πάντων μέλει, οὐδέ σε λήθει
lines.en: For the judgment of all is ever your concern, nor does there escape you
lines.note: γνώμη here “judgment/decision”; μέλει “is a concern to you.”

lines.gr: ψυχ ὴ ὑπερφρονέουσα λόγων ἀδιακρίτῳ ὁρμῇ.
lines.en: a soul that grows overproud, in an undiscriminating rush of words.
lines.note: ὑπερφρονέουσα “overproud/overweening”; λόγων ἀδιακρίτῳ ὁρμῇ = “with an undiscriminating rush/impulse of words,” i.e., reckless speech does not escape Nemesis’ notice.

lines.gr: πάντ' ἐσορ ᾷς, καὶ πάντ' ἐπακούεις, πάντα βραβεύεις·
lines.en: You see all, and you hear all, you adjudge all;
lines.note: βραβεύεις = “act as umpire/adjudge/award,” a technical term of arbitration.

lines.gr: ἐν σοὶ δ’ εἰσὶ δίκαι θνητῶν, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον.
lines.en: and in you are the judgments of mortals, O most exalted daimōn.
lines.note: δαῖμον rendered as transliterated daimōn, denoting a divinity/spirit (not “demon”); πανυπέρτατε = “most exalted/supreme.”

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρ’, ἁ γνή, μύσταις ἐπιτά ῤῥοθος αἰεί·
lines.en: Come, blessed one, pure, ever a helper to the mystai;
lines.note: ἁγνή = “pure/holy”; ἐπιτάρροθος = “helper/succorer”; μύσται (mystai) = “initiates” in cultic context.

lines.gr: δὸς δ’ ἀγαθὴ ν διάνοιαν ἔχειν, παύουσα πανεχθεῖς
lines.en: grant that we may possess good understanding, checking utterly hateful
lines.note: διάνοια = “understanding/disposition of mind”; πανεχθεῖς = “utterly odious” (not necessarily “hateful to all”).

lines.gr: γνώμας, οὐχ ὁσίας, πανυπέρφρονας, ἀλλοπροσάλλας.
lines.en: thoughts—unholy, all-overweening, and changeable.
lines.note: πανυπέρφρονας = “utterly overweening/very arrogant”; ἀλλοπροσάλλας = “changeable/fickle/inconsistent.”

lines.gr: Ὄμμα Δίκης μέλπω πανδερκέος, ἀγλαομόρφου,
lines.en: I hymn the Eye of Dike, all-seeing, of radiant form,
lines.note: Ὄμμα Δίκης personifies the ‘Eye of Dike (Justice)’, highlighting her all-seeing oversight; πανδερκέος = “all-seeing,” ἀγλαομόρφου = “bright/radiant in form.”

lines.gr: ἣ καὶ Ζηνὸς ἄνακτος ἐπὶ θρόνον ἱερὸν ἵζει,
lines.en: who also takes her seat upon the sacred throne of lord Zeus,
lines.note: ἵζει (“takes her seat/sits”) is intransitive; ἄνακτος (“lord”) gives Zeus a regal epithet appropriate to cultic diction.

lines.gr: οὐρανόθεν καθορῶσα βίον θνητῶν πολυφύλων,
lines.en: looking down from heaven upon the life of mortals of many tribes,
lines.note: πολυφύλων = “of many races/tribes,” stressing the universal scope of Justice’s gaze.

lines.gr: τοῖς ἀδίκοις τιμωρὸς ἐπιβρίθουσα δικαίη,
lines.en: a just avenger, pressing heavily upon the unjust,
lines.note: τιμωρός = “avenger”; ἐπιβρίθουσα literally “pressing heavily upon,” conveying punitive weight.

lines.gr: ἐξ ἰσότητος ἀληθεί ῃ συνάγουσ’ ἀνομο ῖα.
lines.en: bringing the unlike together by true equity,
lines.note: Syntax: ἐξ ἰσότητος (“from/with equity, fairness”), ἀληθείῃ (dative of manner, “truly/in truth”); συνάγουσα ἀνόμοια = “bringing unlike things together,” i.e., reconciling disparities into fair balance. The line’s abstract diction is typical of Orphic moral theology.

lines.gr: πάντα γάρ, ὅσσα κακα ῖς γνώμαις θνητοῖσιν ὀχεῖται,
lines.en: for whatever among mortals is carried on by evil counsels,
lines.note: ὀχεῖται (“is borne/advanced, carried on”) used metaphorically of actions/counsels; κακαῖς γνώμαις = “evil/wicked counsels/intentions.”

lines.gr: δύσκριτα, βουλομένοις τὸ πλέον βουλαῖς ἀδίκοισιν,
lines.en: is hard to adjudge, as men by unjust plans desire the larger share,
lines.note: δύσκριτα (neut. pl.) = “hard to distinguish/judge”; βουλομένοις τὸ πλέον is the idiom “desiring the larger share” (pleonexia), with βουλαῖς ἀδίκοισιν as the unjust means.

lines.gr: μούνη ἐπεμβαίνουσα δίκ ῃ ἀδίκοις ἐπὶ ἔργοις,
lines.en: you alone, intervening with Justice against unjust deeds,
lines.note: ἐπεμβαίνουσα δίκῃ = “stepping in with Justice,” dative of instrument; expresses intervention against wrongdoing.

lines.gr: ἐχθρ ὴ τῶν ἀδίκων, ε ὔφρων δὲ σύνεσσι δικαίοις,
lines.en: enemy of the unjust, yet well-disposed to just understandings,
lines.note: σύνεσι(ν) δικαίοις = “to just understandings” (dative), i.e., to those of just discernment; εὔφρων = “well-disposed, gracious.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεά, μόλ’ ἔπι γνώμαις ἐσθλ ῆσι δικαίη,
lines.en: come, goddess, to noble counsels, O Just One,
lines.note: μόλ’ is the apocopated aorist imperative of βλώσκω (“come!”), a standard cultic summons; ἐπὶ γνώμαις ἐσθλαῖσι = “to noble counsels”; δικαίη voc. addresses Dike.

lines.gr: ὡς ἂν ἀεὶ βιοτ ῆς τὸ πεπρωμένον ἦμαρ ἐπέλθ ῃ.
lines.en: so that the fated day of life may ever arrive.
lines.note: βιοτῆς τὸ πεπρωμένον ἦμαρ = “the fated day of life,” a traditional formula for one’s allotted time; ἀεί (“ever”) expresses the wish for the destined outcome to arrive unfailingly.

lines.gr: Ὠ θνητοῖσι δικαιοτάτη, πολύολβε, ποθεινή,
lines.en: O most just to mortals, much-blessed, longed-for,

lines.gr: ἐξ ἰσότητος ἀεὶ θνητο ῖς χαίρουσα δικαίοις,
lines.en: ever rejoicing, from equality, in the just among mortals,
lines.note: ἐξ ἰσότητος (“from/by equality”): ἐκ marks basis or source; θνητοῖς δικαίοις is the dative of those in whom she delights.

lines.gr: πάντιμ’, ὀλβιόμοιρε, Δικαιοσύνη μεγαλαυχής,
lines.en: all-honored, blessed in lot, Dikaiosynē, high-glorying,
lines.note: μεγαλαυχής = “high-/great-glorying”; ὀλβιόμοιρε “blessed in lot.”

lines.gr: ἣ καθαραῖ ς γνώμαισ αἰεὶ τὰ δέοντα βραβεύεις,
lines.en: who with pure judgments ever award what is due,
lines.note: βραβεύειν “to act as arbiter/umpire”; τὰ δέοντα “what is due/fitting.”

lines.gr: ἄθραυστος τὸ συνειδός ἀεὶ θραύεις γἁρ ἅπαντας,
lines.en: unbroken is the conscience always; for you shatter all
lines.note: τὸ συνειδός = “the conscience/inner awareness” (rare poetically). Some punctuate after ἀεί, or read ἄθραυστον; sense: conscience stands firm, yet Dikaiosynē breaks wrongdoers.

lines.gr: ὅσσοι μ ὴ τὸ σὸν ἦλθον ὑπὸ ζυγόν, ἀλλοπρόσαλλοι,
lines.en: who have not come beneath your yoke, fickle and changeful,
lines.note: ἀλλοπρόσαλλοι “changeable, inconstant,” of those not submitting to Justice’s yoke.

lines.gr: πλάστιγξιν βριαρῇσι παρεγκλίναντες ἀπλήστως
lines.en: greedily deflecting the heavy scale-pans,
lines.note: πλάστιγγες “scale-pans”; βριαρός “stout/heavy”; παρεγκλίνειν “to tip aside” (tampering with the scales of justice).

lines.gr: ἀστασίαστε, φίλη πάντων, φιλόκωμ’, ἐ ρατεινή,
lines.en: factionless, dear to all, revel-loving, lovely,
lines.note: ἀστασίαστος “free from faction/civil strife”; φιλόκωμος “revel-loving,” with positive cultic/festal connotations.

lines.gr: εἰρήνῃ χαίρουσα, βίον ζηλοῦσα βέβαιον.
lines.en: delighting in peace, aspiring to a stable life.

lines.gr: αἰεὶ γἁρ τὸ πλέον στυγέεις, ἰσότητι δὲ χαίρεις.
lines.en: for you ever loathe excess, and you rejoice in equality.
lines.note: τὸ πλέον “the excess,” evoking pleonexia (grasping excess) opposed to ἰσότης (equality).

lines.gr: ἐν σοὶ γὰρ σοφίη ἀρετ ῆς τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἱκάνει.
lines.en: for in you wisdom attains the noble end of excellence.
lines.note: τέλος ἀρετῆς “the fulfillment/goal of excellence”; ἱκάνει “attains, reaches.”

lines.gr: κλῦθι, θεά, κακίην θνητῶν θραύουσα δικαίως,
lines.en: Hear, goddess, you who justly shatter the wickedness of mortals,

lines.gr: ὡς ἂν ἰσοῤῥοπί ῃσιν ἀεὶ βίος ἐσθλ ὸς ὁδεύοι
lines.en: so that the good life may always travel with even balance
lines.note: ἰσορροπίῃσι(ν) = dat. pl. “with even balance(s)”; some MSS spell ἰσορροπῇσιν; image of a well-balanced scale/life.

lines.gr: θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἳ ἀρούρης καρπὸν ἔδουσιν,
lines.en: of mortal humans, who eat the fruit of the ploughland,
lines.note: ἀρούρα “ploughland,” Homeric/poetic for arable land.

lines.gr: καὶ ζώων πάντων, ὁπόσ’ ἐν κόλποισι τιθηνεῖ
lines.en: and of all living creatures, as many as in their bosoms are nurtured
lines.note: The English renders the Greek active τιθηνεῖ (“nurtures/fosters”) as passive for smoother syntax; κόλποι “bosoms” of earth and sea.

lines.gr: γα ῖα θεὰ μήτηρ καὶ πόντιος εἰνάλιος Ζεύς.
lines.en: by Gaia, goddess-mother, and Zeus of the sea, sea-dwelling.
lines.note: Πόντιος εἰνάλιος Ζεύς = “Zeus of the sea, sea-dwelling,” i.e., Poseidon; Orphic diction can apply the name Zeus to the divine in multiple domains.

lines.gr: Ἀθανάτων καλέω καὶ θνητῶν ἁγνὸν ἄνακτα,
lines.en: I call the pure lord of immortals and mortals,
lines.note: ἁγνός (“pure”) is a ritual epithet; ἄναξ (“lord”) marks high divine status in hymnic diction.

lines.gr: οὐράνιον Νόμον, ἀστροθέτην, σφραγῖδα δικαίαν
lines.en: the heavenly Nomos, the star-setter, the just seal
lines.note: Nomos is treated as a theonym. ἀστροθέτης (“star-setter”) evokes cosmic ordering; σφραγίς (“seal”) suggests a guarantee or authoritative stamp.

lines.gr: πόντου τ’ εἰναλίου καὶ γῆς, φύσεως τὸ βέβαιον
lines.en: of the briny sea and of earth, the surety of Nature,
lines.note: εἰναλίος = “of/within the sea”; φύσεως τὸ βέβαιον = “the firm/sure guarantee of Nature.”

lines.gr: ἀκλινὲς ἀστασίαστον ἀεὶ τηροῦντα νόμοισιν,
lines.en: guarding, by laws, forever the unbending, factionless order,
lines.note: The participle τηροῦντα (“guarding”) governs φύσεως τὸ βέβαιον from the previous line; νόμοισιν is instrumental (“by means of laws”). ἀστασίαστος = “free from stasis (civil strife),” hence “without upheaval.”

lines.gr: οἷσιν ἄνωθε φέρων μέγαν οὐρανὸν αὐτὸς ὁδεύει,
lines.en: by which, bearing aloft the great heaven, he himself goes his course,
lines.note: οἷσιν refers back to νόμοισιν (“by which [laws]”); ἄνωθε (“from above/aloft”); ὁδεύει (“goes, proceeds”) poetically of cosmic course.

lines.gr: καὶ φθόνον οὐ δίκαιον ῥοίζου τρόπον αὐτὸς ἐλαύνει·
lines.en: and he himself drives off unjust Envy with a whirring rush;
lines.note: ῥοίζου τρόπον = “in the manner of a whir/roar (rush of wind).” ἐλαύνει here “drives off/expels.”

lines.gr: ὃς καὶ θνητοῖσιν βιοτῆς τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἐγείρει.
lines.en: who also for mortals awakens a noble end of life.
lines.note: τέλος of life can be “end” or “fulfillment/consummation”; ἐγείρει (“raises/awakens”) is a bold hymnic collocation.

lines.gr: αὐτὸς γὰρ μοῦνος ζῶων οἴηκα κρατύνει,
lines.en: for he alone holds the helm of living beings,
lines.note: The transmitted οἴηκα is likely for οἴακα (“helm, tiller”); many editors emend accordingly. Sense: Nomos “holds the helm” of all living things.

lines.gr: γνώμαις ὀρθοτάτῃσι συνών, ἀδιάστροφος αἰεί,
lines.en: consorting with the straightest counsels, ever unperverted,
lines.note: γνώμαις ὀρθοτάτῃσι = “the straightest/most upright counsels”; συνών = “consorting/being in company with.” ἀδιάστροφος = “unperverted, uncorrupted.”

lines.gr: ὠγύγιος, πολύπειρος, ἀβλάπτως πᾶσι συνοικῶν
lines.en: Ogygian, much-experienced, dwelling harmlessly with all
lines.note: ὠγύγιος = “Ogygian,” i.e., primeval/very ancient; πολύπειρος = “much-experienced.” συνοικῶν = “dwelling with, living among.”

lines.gr: τοῖς νομίμοις, ἀνόμοις δὲ φέρων κακότητα βαρεῖαν.
lines.en: who are lawful, but bringing heavy wickedness upon the lawless.
lines.note: νομίμοις = “the lawful, those who live by law”; ἀνόμοις = “the lawless.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πάντιμε, φερόλβιε, πᾶσι ποθεινέ,
lines.en: But come, blessed one, all-honored, wealth-bringing, desired by all,
lines.note: ἀλλά marks the transition to prayer. Vocatives: μάκαρ (“blessed”), πάντιμος (“all-honored”), φερόλβιος (“wealth-bringing”), πᾶσι ποθεινός (“desired by all”).

lines.gr: εὐμενὲς ἦτορ ἔχων μνήμην σέο πέμπε, φέριστε.
lines.en: with gracious heart, send the remembrance of yourself, O best.
lines.note: μνήμην σέο = “remembrance of you” (objective genitive), i.e., grant mindful presence/favor; εὐμενές ἦτορ = “gracious heart.”

lines.gr: Ἄρηκτ', ὀμβριμόθυμε, μεγασθενές, ἄλκιμε δαῖμον,
lines.en: Unyielding one, storm‑hearted, great in strength, valiant daimon,
lines.note: Ἄρηκτ’ = vocative ἄρηκτε (“unbreakable, unyielding”).

lines.gr: ὁπλοχαρής, ἀδάμαστε, βροτοκτόνε, τειχεσιπλοτα,
lines.en: arm‑loving, untamed one, slayer of mortals, wall‑roaming besieger,
lines.note: τειχεσιπλοτα: a rare epithet, “prowling about the walls,” hence “besieger” (from teichos ‘wall’ + a wandering/roving notion).

lines.gr: Ἄρες ἄναξ, ὁπλόδουπε, φόνοις πεπαλαγμένος αἰεί,
lines.en: Ares, lord, armour‑thundering, ever bespattered with slaughters,
lines.note: ὁπλόδουπε = “armour‑thundering”; πεπαλαγμένος “bespattered, defiled” (with slaughters).

lines.gr: αἵματι τ' ἀνδροφόνῳ χαίρων, πολεμόκλονε, φρικτέ,
lines.en: rejoicing in man‑slaying blood, war‑stirring, dread one,
lines.note: πολεμόκλονε “war‑stirring/shaking”; φρικτέ “dread one.”

lines.gr: ὅς ποθέ εις ξίφεσίν τε καὶ ἔγχεσι δοῦριν ἄμουσον ·
lines.en: who long for swords and for spears, the unmusical spear;
lines.note: The text is difficult: many read ποθεῖς/ποθέεις (“you long for”); ξίφεσίν … ἔγχεσι are weapons (swords, spears). δοῦριν ἄμουσον = “the unmusical spear,” i.e., alien to the Muses and the arts of peace.

lines.gr: στῆσον ἔριν λυσσῶσαν, ἄνες πόνον ἀλγεσίθυμον·
lines.en: still raging strife; unloose the heart‑aching toil;
lines.note: ἀλγεσίθυμον = “grief‑minded, pain‑at‑heart.”

lines.gr: εἰς δὲ πόθον νεῦσον Κύπριδος, κώμους τε Βυαίου,
lines.en: and incline toward the desire of Kypris and the revels of Lyaios,
lines.note: Βυαίου is likely a corruption for Λυαίου (“Lyaios,” epithet of Dionysus, ‘the Loosener’); hence “revels of Lyaios.”

lines.gr: ἀλλάξας ἀλκήν ὅπλων εἰς ἔργα τὰ Δηοῦς,
lines.en: having exchanged the might of arms for the works of Deo,
lines.note: Δηοῦς = “Deo,” an epic name for Demeter.

lines.gr: εἰρήνην ποθέων κουροτρόφον, ὀλβιοδῶτιν.
lines.en: desiring Peace, nurse of youths, giver of prosperity.
lines.note: εἰρήνη here is personified (the goddess Eirene), hence capitalized; κουροτρόφος “nurse of youths,” ὀλβιοδῶτις “giver of prosperity.”

lines.gr: Ἥφαιστ’ ὀμβριμόθυμε, μεγασθενές, ἀκάματον πῦρ,
lines.en: Hephaistos, impetuous of heart, mighty-strong, unwearied fire,
lines.note: ὀμβριμόθυμε = “of stormy/impetuous spirit.” ἀκάματον πῦρ appositionally identifies Hephaistos with tireless fire.

lines.gr: λαμπόμενε φλογέαις αὐγαῖς, φαεσίμβροτε δαῖμον,
lines.en: shining with flaming rays, light-bringing-to-mortals, daimon,
lines.note: φαεσίμβροτε = “light-bringing to mortals.” δαῖμον here is a neutral term for a divine power.

lines.gr: φωσφόρε, καρτερόχειρ, αἰώνιε, τεχνοδίαιτε,
lines.en: light-bearer, strong-handed, eternal, craft-subsisting,
lines.note: τεχνοδίαιτε literally “living by/through craft”; hence “craft-subsisting.”

lines.gr: ἐργαστήρ, κόσμοιο μέρος, στοιχεῖον ἀμεμφές,
lines.en: craftsman, a portion of the cosmos, unblemished element,
lines.note: ἐργαστήρ = “artisan/craftsman.” στοιχεῖον ἀμεμφές = “faultless/basic element,” presenting Fire as one of the stoicheia.

lines.gr: παμφάγε, πανδαμάτωρ, πανυπέρτατε, παντοδίαιτε,
lines.en: all-devouring, all-subduer, supreme over all, dwelling everywhere,
lines.note: παντοδίαιτε can mean “dwelling everywhere” or “feeding on all”; in context of fire, the former is adopted alongside “all-devouring.”

lines.gr: αἰθήρ, ἥλιος, ἄστρα, σελήνη, φῶς ἀμίαντον·
lines.en: Aither, Sun, Stars, Moon, undefiled Light;
lines.note: A litany equating Hephaistos with cosmic fires; “Light undefiled” emphasizes purity/immaculacy.

lines.gr: ταῦτα γὰρ Ἡφαίστοιο μέλη θνητοῖσι προφαίνει.
lines.en: for these appear to mortals as the members of Hephaistos.
lines.note: μέλη (“members/limbs”) metaphorically of cosmic parts manifesting the god to mortals.

lines.gr: πάντα δὲ οἶκον ἔχεις, π ᾶσαν πόλιν, ἔθνεα πάντα·
lines.en: and you possess every house, every city, all peoples;
lines.note: ἔχεις = “you occupy/hold,” expressing fire’s pervasion of houses, cities, and peoples.

lines.gr: σώματά τε θνητῶν ο ἰκεῖς, πολύολβε, κραταιέ·
lines.en: and you dwell in the bodies of mortals, much-blest, mighty one;
lines.note: πολύολβε = “much-blest/very prosperous.” οἰκεῖς “you dwell,” of the vital fire within bodies.

lines.gr: κλῦθι, μάκαρ, κλῄζω σε πρ ὸς εὐϊέρους ἐπιλοιβάς,
lines.en: hear, blessed one; I acclaim you with holy libations,
lines.note: ἐπιλοιβάς are concluding/ritual libations; εὐϊέρους = “well-hallowed/holy.” κλῄζω = “proclaim/celebrate, invoke.”

lines.gr: αἰεὶ ὅπως χαίρουσιν ἐπ’ ἔργοις ἥμερος ἔλθ ῃς.
lines.en: that you may ever come mild to the works wherein we rejoice.
lines.note: ἥμερος = “mild, tame.” The subject of χαίρουσιν is understood (we/mortals): a prayer for a gentle presence in our works.

lines.gr: παῦσον λυσσῶσαν μανίην πυρ ὸς ἀκαμάτοιο,
lines.en: Restrain the raging frenzy of the unwearied fire,
lines.note: λυσσῶσαν μανίην = “raging frenzy,” the destructive aspect of fire; ἀκάματος echoes line 1.

lines.gr: καῦσιν ἔχων φύσεως ἐν σώμασιν ἡμετέροισιν.
lines.en: since you hold Nature’s burning within our bodies.
lines.note: καῦσις φύσεως = “natural heat,” the innate warmth in ancient physiology; the prayer asks the god to moderate it.

lines.gr: Ἰητὴρ πάντων Ἀσκληπιέ, δέσποτα Παιάν,
lines.en: Healer of all, Asklepios, lord Paian,
lines.note: Paian is a healing epithet (originally of Apollo) used here for Asklepios; “despota” marks hymnic address.

lines.gr: θέλγων ἀνθρώπων πολυαλγέα πήματα νούσων,
lines.en: charming away the much-aching woes of the diseases of men,
lines.note: thelgōn is ‘charming/soothing’ in a beneficent sense; polyalgea pēmata are ‘much-aching banes/sufferings.’

lines.gr: ἠπιόδωρε, κραταιέ, μόλοις κατάγων ὑγίειαν,
lines.en: gentle in your gifts, mighty, bringing health to those in toils,
lines.note: ēpiodōre means ‘gentle in gifts’; molois (dat. pl.) = ‘toils, hardships’; katagō ‘bring down’ can have a cultic nuance (‘draw down’ healing).

lines.gr: καὶ παύων νούσους χαλεπ ὰς θανάτοιο τε κῆρας.
lines.en: and stopping grievous diseases and the dooms of death.
lines.note: Keras are personified ‘dooms’ of death; hence ‘dooms of death.’ The source spacing “χαλεπ ὰς” is to be read χαλεπὰς.

lines.gr: αὐξιθαλής κόρε, ἀπαλεξίκακ’, ὀλβιόμοιρε,
lines.en: ever-thriving youth, averting-evil, of blessed lot,
lines.note: auxithalēs = ‘ever-thriving, luxuriantly growing’; kore here is vocative of kouros ‘youth’; apalexikakos = ‘averter of evil’; olbiomoiros = ‘of blessed lot.’

lines.gr: Φοίβου Ἀπόλλωνος κρατερὸν θάλος ἀγλαότιμον,
lines.en: sturdy scion of Phoibos Apollon, splendidly honored,
lines.note: thalos = ‘shoot, offspring,’ hence ‘scion’; Asklepios is the offspring of Phoibos Apollon; aglaotimos = ‘splendidly honored.’

lines.gr: ἐχθρ ὲ νόσων, Ὑγίειαν ἔχων σύλ λεκτρον ἀμεμφ ῆ,
lines.en: foe to diseases, possessing Hygieia as blameless bedfellow,
lines.note: Read ἐχθρέ, νόσων; Ὑγίειαν ἔχων σύλλεκτρον ἀμέμφη = ‘having Hygieia as blameless bedfellow/consort’; σύλλεκτρον ‘bedfellow’ underscores Hygieia’s close association with Asklepios.

lines.gr: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σωτήρ, βιοτῆς τέλος ἐσθλὸν ὀπάζων.
lines.en: come, blessed one, Soter, bestowing a good end to life.
lines.note: telos biotēs esthlon = ‘a good end of life,’ i.e., a blessed death; Soter is a hymnic epithet ‘Savior.’

lines.gr: Ἱμερόεσσ’, ἐ ρατή, πολυθάλμιε, παμβασίλεια,
lines.en: Desire-sweet, lovely, much-flourishing, all-sovereign Queen,
lines.note: Ἱμερόεσσα = “desire-sweet, lovely”; πολύ-θάλμιε is from θάλλω (“to bloom, thrive”): “much-/richly flourishing.” Παμβασίλεια = “all-sovereign (queen).”

lines.gr: κλῦθι, μάκαιρ’ Ὑγίεια, φερόλβιε, μῆτερ ἁπάντων.
lines.en: hear, blessed Hygieia, wealth-bringing, Mother of all.
lines.note: φερόλβιος = “bringing ὄλβος,” i.e., prosperity/blessed wealth. “Mother of all” is a cultic hyperbole for Health’s universal beneficence.

lines.gr: ἐκ σέο γὰρ νο ῦσοι μὲν ἀποφθινύθουσι βροτοῖσιν,
lines.en: For from you diseases waste away among mortals,
lines.note: ἀποφθινύθω = “waste away, perish” (intrans.); νοῦσοι = “diseases.”

lines.gr: πᾶς δὲ δόμος θάλλει πολυγηθὴς ε ἵνεκα σεῖο,
lines.en: and every house blooms, much-rejoicing, because of you,
lines.note: θάλλει = “to bloom, flourish” (metaphor of prosperity). πολυγηθής = “much-rejoicing.”

lines.gr: καὶ τέχναι βρίθουσι. ποθε ῖ δέ σε κόσμος, ἄνασσα,
lines.en: and the crafts are laden; the cosmos longs for you, Lady,
lines.note: βρίθουσι literally “are heavy,” here “are weighty/abundant, thrive.” κόσμος taken as “cosmos, ordered world,” not “adornment.” ἄνασσα = “Lady.”

lines.gr: μοῦνος δὲ στυγέει σ’ Ἀΐ δης ψυχοφθόρος αἰεί·
lines.en: but only Aides, the soul-destroyer, ever hates you;
lines.note: Ἀΐδης here transliterated “Aides” per instruction; ψυχοφθόρος = “soul-destroying,” a traditional epic epithet.

lines.gr: ἀϊθαλής , εὐκταιοτάτη, θνητῶν ἀνάπαυμα.
lines.en: ever-green, most-prayed-for, the repose of mortals.
lines.note: The transmitted ἀϊθαλής (“sooty”) is likely a corruption; most read ἀειθαλής (“ever-green/ever-thriving”), which suits Hygieia’s life-giving aspect. εὐκταιοτάτη = “most prayed-for”; ἀνάπαυμα = “repose, relief.”

lines.gr: σοῦ γὰρ ἄτερ πάντ' ἐστὶ ν ἀνωφελ ῆ ἀνθρώποισιν.
lines.en: For without you everything is unprofitable for human beings.
lines.note: ἀνωφελής = “useless, unprofitable,” stressing Health’s necessity for all human endeavors.

lines.gr: οὔτε γὰρ ὀλβοδότης Πλο ῦτος γλυκερὸς θαλί ῃσιν,
lines.en: For not even Ploutos, the wealth-giver, is sweet at feasts,
lines.note: ὀλβοδότης = “giver of ὄλβος (blessed wealth).” θάλιαι/θαλία = “banquets, festivity.” “Ploutos” transliterates the theonym.

lines.gr: οὔτε γέρων πολύμοχθος ἄτερ σέο γίγνεται ἀνήρ.
lines.en: nor does a man become an old man, much-toiling, apart from you.
lines.note: πολύμοχθος = “much-toiling, much-enduring.” γέρων … ἀνήρ = “a man become old”; the sense is that without Health no one reaches old age.

lines.gr: πάντων γὰρ κρατέεις μούνη, καὶ πᾶσιν ἀνάσσεις.
lines.en: For you alone hold sway over all, and you rule all.
lines.note: μοῦνη is emphatic “you alone.” κρατέω “to hold sway (over),” ἀνάσσω “to rule,” marking Hygieia’s supremacy.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεά, μόλε μυστιπόλοις ἐπιτά ῤῥοθος αἰεὶ,
lines.en: But come, goddess, ever a helper to the mystic attendants,
lines.note: μυστιπόλοις = “mystic attendants/servants,” i.e., officiants in rites; ἐπιτάρροθος = “helper, ally.” μόλε = aorist imperative “come.”

lines.gr: ῥυομένη νούσων χαλεπῶν κακόποτμον ἀνίην.
lines.en: rescuing from grievous diseases the ill-fated distress.
lines.note: ῥυομένη (middle) = “rescuing, delivering.” κακόποτμος ἀνίη = “ill-fated distress/trouble,” a conventional collocation for grievous suffering.

lines.gr: Κλῦτε, θεαὶ πάντιμοι, ἐ ρίβρομοι, εὐάστειραι,
lines.en: Hear, goddesses most-honored, loud-roaring, star-bright,
lines.note: εὐάστειραι literally “well-starred” or “star-bright,” an epithet suited to nocturnal deities; ἐρίβρομοι “loud-roaring.”

lines.gr: Τισιφόνη τε καὶ Ἀλληκτώ, καὶ δῖα Μέγαιρα ·
lines.en: Tisiphonē and Alēktō, and divine Megaira;
lines.note: The usual Greek forms are Τισιφόνη (Tisiphonē), Ἀληκτώ (Alēktō), and Μέγαιρα (Megaira). Some manuscripts show Ἀλληκτώ; the single lambda is standard.

lines.gr: νυκτέριαι, μ ύχιαι, ὑπὸ κεύθεσιν οἰκί’ ἔχουσαι
lines.en: nightly, of the inner depths, keeping house beneath hidden places,
lines.note: νυκτέριαι “nightly/pertaining to night”; μύχιαι “of the innermost (depths).” The idiom οἰκί’ ἔχουσαι = “keeping house, dwelling.” κεύθεα “hidden places, recesses.”

lines.gr: ἄντρῳ ἐν ἠερόεντι, παρὰ Στυγὸς ἱερὸν ὕδωρ·
lines.en: in a misty cavern, beside the holy water of Styx;
lines.note: ἠερόεντι “misty, murky.” Styx is the personified underworld river; here “beside the holy water of Styx.”

lines.gr: οὐχ ὁσίαις βουλ ῇσι βροτ ῶν πεποτημέναι αἰεὶ
lines.en: ever smitten by mortals’ unholy counsels,
