lines.note: The transmitted πεποτημέναι is likely corrupt for πεπληγμέναι (“smitten, struck”), which fits the sense “moved to wrath by” mortals’ impious plans. I translate with that widely accepted correction.

lines.gr: λυσσήρεις, ἀγέρωχοι, ἐπευάζουσαι ἀνάγκαις,
lines.en: raging, overbearing, crying sanction upon constraints,
lines.note: ἐπευάζουσαι is a cultic verb “to cry over, to give acclamation/ sanction.” ἀνάγκαις is plural “constraints/necessities” (not necessarily the goddess Anankē). Hence “crying sanction upon constraints.”

lines.gr: θηρόπεπλοι, τιμωροί, ἐ ρισθενέες, βαρυαλγεῖς,
lines.en: beast-clad, avengers, very mighty, heavy with pains,
lines.note: θηρόπεπλοι “beast-clad, wearing the skins of beasts”; τιμωροί “avengers”; βαρυαλγεῖς “heavy with pains, sorely-grieving.”

lines.gr: Ἀΐδεω χθόνιαι φοβεραὶ κόραι αἰολόμορφοι,
lines.en: chthonic daughters of Aidēs, dreadful, of shifting form,
lines.note: Ἀΐδης (Aidēs) as the underworld god; χθόνιαι “chthonic”; αἰολόμορφοι “of variegated/shifting form.” κόραι “maidens” is traditional for the Erinyes despite their dreadful aspect.

lines.gr: ἠέριαι, ἀφανεῖς, ὠ κύδρομοι ὥστε νόημα.
lines.en: airy, unseen, swift-running like thought.
lines.note: ὠκύδρομοι ὥστε νόημα “swift-running like thought,” a simile for unerring, instantaneous pursuit; ἠέριαι “airy, mist-like”; ἀφανεῖς “unseen.”

lines.gr: αἵτ’ αἰεὶ
lines.en: who ever

lines.gr: θνητῶν πάντων ἐπ’ ἀπείρονα φῦλα
lines.en: over the boundless tribes of all mortals
lines.note: ἀπείρονα “boundless, without limit,” of the multitude of mortals.

lines.gr: ὄμμα Δίκης ἐφορᾶτε, δικασπόλοι αἰὲν ἐοῦσαι.
lines.en: watch as the eye of Dikē, ever being ministers of judgment.
lines.note: ὄμμα Δίκης can be taken as “the eye of Dikē (Justice)”—the Erinyes function as Justice’s vigilant eye; δικασπόλοι “ministers/agents of judgment.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεαὶ Μοῖραι, ὀφιοπλόκαμοι, πολύμορφοι,
lines.en: But, goddesses, Moirai, snake-locked, many-formed,
lines.note: The hymn syncretizes the Erinyes with the Moirai. ὀφιοπλόκαμοι “snake-locked” is a traditional epithet of the Furies; πολύμορφοι “many-formed.”

lines.gr: πρηΰνοον μετάθεσθε βίου μαλακόφρονα δόξαν.
lines.en: turn the tenor of life to a gentle-minded disposition.
lines.note: μετάθεσθε is a prayerful imperative “turn/alter.” πρηΰνοον (“gentle, soothing-minded”) and μαλακόφρονα (“soft-minded, mild”) express the desired mitigation of harsh fate; the line asks the goddesses to turn life’s disposition to gentleness.

lines.gr: Κλῦτέ μευ , Εὐμενίδες μεγαλώνυμοι, εὔφρονι βουλ ῇ,
lines.en: Hear me, Eumenides of great name, with kindly counsel.
lines.note: “Κλῦτέ μευ” uses the archaic genitive pronoun (meu) in the sense “hear me”; Εὐμενίδες (“Kindly Ones”) is a euphemistic title for the Erinyes; εὔφρονι βουλῇ = “with kindly/propitious counsel.”

lines.gr: ἁγνα ὶ θυγατέρες μεγάλοιο Διὸς χθονίοιο,
lines.en: Holy daughters of great Zeus Chthonios,
lines.note: “Zeus Chthonios” in Orphic diction often identifies the underworld Zeus (i.e., Hades).

lines.gr: Φερσεφόνης τ’, ἐ ρατῆς κούρης καλλιπλοκάμοιο,
lines.en: and of Phersephonê, the lovely maiden of fair-braided hair,
lines.note: Φερσεφόνη (here gen. Φερσεφόνης) is the Orphic form of Persephonê; καλλιπλοκάμοιο = “of fair-braided [hair],” a traditional epic epithet.

lines.gr: αἳ πάντων καθορᾶτε βίον θνητῶν ἀσεβούντων,
lines.en: who behold the life of all mortals when they act impiously,
lines.note: ἀσεβούντων (“acting impiously”) is a participle qualifying θνητῶν (“mortals”), emphasizing their surveillance of human impiety.

lines.gr: τῶν ἀδίκων τιμωροί, ἐφεστηκυ ῖαι ἀνάγκῃ,
lines.en: avengers of the unjust, standing over them with Necessity,
lines.note: ἐφεστηκυῖαι ἀνάγκῃ can mean “attending with Anankê (Necessity, personified)” or “enforcing by compulsion”; τιμωροί = “avengers.”

lines.gr: κυανόχρωτοι ἄνασσαι, ἀπαστράπτουσαι ἀπ’ ὄσσων
lines.en: dark-hued queens, flashing from your eyes
lines.note: κυανόχρωτοι = “blue-black/dark-hued,” perhaps of complexion or robes; ἀπαστράπτουσαι ἀπ’ ὄσσων = “flashing from [your] eyes.”

lines.gr: δειν ὴν ἀνταυγ ῆ φάεος σαρκοφθόρον αἴγλην
lines.en: a dread reflection of light, a flesh-consuming radiance,
lines.note: ἀνταυγή φάεος = “reflection of light”; the case is debated in the tradition, but sense is a dread glare; σαρκοφθόρος = “flesh-wasting/consuming,” suggesting wasting terror or disease.

lines.gr: ἀΐδιοι , φοβερ ῶπες, ἀπόστροφοι, αὐτοκράτειραι,
lines.en: everlasting, fearsome of aspect, averting, all-sovereign,
lines.note: ἀπόστροφοι may mean “averting (evil)” in an apotropaic sense or “turned-away/averse”; αὐτοκράτειραι = “sovereign in their own right.”

lines.gr: λυσιμελε ῖς οἴστρῳ, βλοσ υροί , νύχιαι, πολύποτμοι,
lines.en: with limb-loosening frenzy, grim, taloned, of manifold doom,
lines.note: οἶστρος = “goad, frenzy”; λυσιμελής = “limb-loosening”; νύχιαι = “clawed, taloned”; πολύποτμοι = “of manifold doom/fate.”

lines.gr: νυκτέριαι κοῦραι, ὀφιοπλόκαμοι, φοβερῶπες,
lines.en: nocturnal maidens, with snaky tresses, fearsome of gaze,
lines.note: νυκτέριαι = “nocturnal”; ὀφιοπλόκαμοι = “with snaky locks,” a standard Fury epithet; φοβερῶπες = “fearsome-faced.”

lines.gr: ὑμέας κικλήσκω γνώμαις ὁσίῃσι πελάζειν.
lines.en: I call upon you to draw near with holy intentions.
lines.note: γνώμαις ὁσίῃσι is a dative of manner, “with holy intentions/purposes,” a propitiatory appeal.

lines.gr: Μηλινόην καλέω, νύμφην χθονίην , κροκόπεπλον,
lines.en: I call upon Melinoe, chthonic nymph, saffron-robed,

lines.gr: ἣν παρὰ Κωκυτο ῦ προχοα ῖς ἐλοχεύσατο σεμνὴ
lines.en: whom august Persephone bore by the outflows of Kokytos,
lines.note: ἐλοχεύσατο is middle ‘bore’; Kokytos is the underworld river; προχοαί = ‘outflows’.

lines.gr: Φερσεφόνη, λέκτροις ἱεροῖς Ζηνὸς Κρονίοιο·
lines.en: in the holy bed of Zeus Kronios;
lines.note: λέκτρα ‘bed’ denotes sexual union; Zeus bears the epithet ‘Kronios’.

lines.gr: ἧι ψευσθε ῖς Πλούτων’ ἐμίγη δολίαις ἀπάτ ῃσιν,
lines.en: with whom, in the false guise as Plouton, he mingled by wily deceits,
lines.note: ψευσθείς is formally ‘having been deceived,’ but commonly taken as ‘falsely (as) Plouton’; the implied subject is Zeus (from line 3), who couples with Persephone in Plouton’s guise; δολίαις ἀπάταις underscores the disguise.

lines.gr: θυμῷ Φερσεφόνης δὲ δισώματον ἔσπασε χροιήν,
lines.en: and, in her anger, Persephone split her complexion into a two-bodied hue,
lines.note: δισώματον χροιήν (‘two-bodied complexion’) is obscure; likely marks Melinoe’s dual aspect (light/dark), anticipating line 8; ἔσπασε ‘wrenched/drew forth’ suggests a punitive, wrath-driven bestowal by Persephone.

lines.gr: ᾓ θνητο ὺς μαίνει φαντάσμασιν ἠερίοισιν,
lines.en: whereby she maddens mortals with airy phantasms,
lines.note: φαντάσμασιν ἠερίοισιν ‘airy phantasms’ = insubstantial apparitions producing mania.

lines.gr: ἀλλοκότοις ἰδέαις μορφῆς τύπον ἐκπροφανοῦσα·
lines.en: revealing the stamp of form in strange appearances;
lines.note: μορφῆς τύπον ‘imprint/stamp of form’; ἀλλόκοτος ‘strange, uncanny’.

lines.gr: ἄλλοτε μὲν προφανής, ποτὲ δὲ σκοτόεσσα, νυχαυγής,
lines.en: now manifest, now dark, night-gleaming,
lines.note: νυχαυγής ‘night-gleaming’; προφανής/σκοτόεσσα mark alternating visibility.

lines.gr: ἀνταίαις ἐφόδοισι κατὰ ζοφοειδέα νύκτα.
lines.en: with hostile assaults throughout the darkling night.
lines.note: ἀνταίαι ἐφόδοι ‘hostile onsets/assaults’; ζοφοειδής ‘gloom-like, murky’.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεά, λίτομαί σε, καταχθονίων βασίλεια,
lines.en: But, goddess, I beseech you, queen of those below,
lines.note: καταχθονίων βασίλεια ‘queen of those below’: an honorific underworld title applied to the addressed goddess.

lines.gr: ψυχ ῆς ἐκπέμπειν οἶστρον ἐπὶ τέρματα γαίης,
lines.en: to dispatch the soul’s gadfly to the borders of the earth,
lines.note: οἶστρος ‘gadfly’ metaphorically ‘frenzy/torment’; ἐκπέμπειν ἐπὶ τέρματα γαίης = ‘send away to the ends of the earth’.

lines.gr: εὐμενὲς εὐΐερον μύσταις φαίνουσα πρόσωπον.
lines.en: showing a gracious and holy face to the mystai.
lines.note: εὐμενές ‘gracious, propitious’; εὐΐερον (euhieron) is a rare compound ‘well-holy’; μύσται ‘initiates’ (Orphic cult context).

lines.gr: Δεῦρο, Τύχη, καλέω σ’, ἀγαθὴ ν κράντειραν ἐπ’ εὐχαῖς,
lines.en: Come, Tyche, I summon you, good fulfiller of prayers,
lines.note: “κράντειραν ἐπ’ εὐχαῖς” = ‘fulfiller with respect to prayers’; κράντειρα is epic from κραίνω ‘accomplish, fulfill,’ a standard prayer-formula.

lines.gr: μειλιχίην, ἐνοδῖτιν, ἐπ’ εὐόλβοις κτεάτεσσιν,
lines.en: gentle, of the roads, presiding over well-blest possessions,
lines.note: ἐνοδῖτιν = ‘of/along the roads’ (cf. Enodia); “ἐπ’ εὐόλβοις κτεάτεσσιν” literally ‘over well-blest possessions,’ i.e., presiding over prosperity in goods.

lines.gr: Ἄρτεμιν ἡγεμόνην, μεγαλώνυμον, Εὐβουλ ῆος
lines.en: Artemis the Guide, of great renown, of Eubouleus,
lines.note: Syntax runs on to line 4: “Εὐβουλῆος … αἵματος ἐκγεγαῶσαν.” Eubouleus (Good-Counsel) is a cult-name, often of Plouton or Dionysos in Orphic contexts; “ἡγεμόνην” is an epithet ‘the Guide/Leader,’ here applied in an identification of Tyche with Artemis Hegemone.

lines.gr: αἵματος ἐκγεγα ῶσαν, ἀπρόσμαχον εὖχος ἔχουσαν,
lines.en: born from his blood, possessing unassailable glory,
lines.note: “αἵματος ἐκγεγαῶσαν” = ‘sprung from the blood’; “ἀπρόσμαχον εὖχος” is ‘unassailable renown/glory,’ a martial-tinged epithet of inviolability.

lines.gr: τυμβιδίην, πολύπλαγκτον, ἀοίδιμον ἀνθρώποισιν.
lines.en: tomb-haunting, much-wandering, renowned among mortals.
lines.note: τυμβιδίην is rare: ‘tumulary, of the tombs’ (from τύμβος), hence ‘tomb-haunting’; πολύπλαγκτος = ‘much-wandering’; ἀοίδιμος = ‘famed in song.’

lines.gr: ἐν σοὶ γὰρ βίοτος θνητῶν παμποίκιλός ἐστιν·
lines.en: For in you the life of mortals is all-variegated;
lines.note: παμποίκιλος ‘all-variegated, manifold,’ stressing Tyche’s protean influence on human life.

lines.gr: οἷς μὲν γὰρ τεύχεις κτεάνων πλῆθος πολύολβον,
lines.en: for to some you fashion a much-blessed abundance of possessions,
lines.note: τεύχεις = ‘you make/bring about’; πολύολβος = ‘much-blest, very prosperous.’

lines.gr: οἷς δὲ κακὴ ν πενίην, θυμῷ χόλον ὁρμαίνουσα.
lines.en: but to others wretched poverty, brooding anger in your heart.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεά, λίτομαί σε μολεῖν βίωι εὐμενέουσαν,
lines.en: But, goddess, I beseech you to come propitious to my life,
lines.note: λίτομαι with infinitive μολεῖν: ‘I beseech you to come’; εὐμενής ‘propitious, gracious’ as predicative participle agreeing with the addressed goddess; βίῳ is a dativus commodi (‘to/for my life’).

lines.gr: ὄλβοισιν πλήθουσαν ἐπ’ εὐόλβοις κτεάτεσσιν.
lines.en: brimming with prosperities upon well-blest possessions.
lines.note: “ὄλβοισιν πλήθουσαν” = ‘brimming with prosperities’; the repeated phrase “ἐπ’ εὐόλβοις κτεάτεσσιν” links back to line 2, emphasizing prosperity in possessions.

lines.gr: Δαίμονα κικλήσκω, μέγαν εὐηγήτορα, φρικτόν,
lines.en: I call upon the Daimōn, great good‑guide, dread,
lines.note: “Daimōn” denotes a divine power, not a “demon.” “Good‑guide” renders euēgētōr; “dread” = phriktos, a standard cultic epithet.

lines.gr: μειλίχιον Δία, παγγενέτην, βιοδώτορα θνητῶν,
lines.en: mild Zeus, all‑begetter, life‑giver of mortals,
lines.note: “Mild” renders meilichios, a well‑known cult epithet of Zeus (Zeus Meilichios). “All‑begetter” (paggenetēs) and “life‑giver” (biodōtor) are Orphic-style cosmogenic titles.

lines.gr: Ζῆνα μέγαν, πολύπλαγκτον, ἀλάστορα, παμβασιλῆα·
lines.en: great Zeus, far‑wandering, implacable, all‑king;
lines.note: “Far‑wandering” (poluplanktos) characterizes a power that ranges widely or drives others to wander; “implacable” renders alastōr (“unforgetting avenger”); “all‑king” = panbasileus.

lines.gr: πλουτοδότην, ὁπόταν γε βρυάζων οἶκον ἐσέλθ ῃ,
lines.en: wealth‑giver, whenever, overflowing, he enters a house,
lines.note: The participle bryazōn (“overflowing, brimming”) is used adverbially of the god’s manner of entering; some have suspected bryōn. The sense is of lavish, swelling abundance.

lines.gr: ἔμπαλι δὲ τρύχοντα βίον θνητῶν πολυμόχθων
lines.en: and in turn a wasting life for much‑toiling mortals,
lines.note: “In turn” (empali) marks reversal; “a wasting life” translates trychonta bion (“a life that wears away”), picking up an implied antithesis to “wealth‑giver.”

lines.gr: ἐν σοὶ γὰρ λύπης τε χαρᾶς κλῇδες ὀχοῦνται.
lines.en: for in you the keys of sorrow and of joy are borne.
lines.note: “The keys of sorrow and joy are borne in you” expresses control over human fortunes; klēides are symbolic of decisive power.

lines.gr: τοιγάρ τοι, μάκαρ, ἁγνέ, πολύστονα κήδε’ ἐλάσσας,
lines.en: therefore, O blessed, holy one, having driven away cares full of groaning,
lines.note: The aorist participle (“having driven away”) is prayer‑style, leading into the following petition.

lines.gr: ὅσσα βιοφθορίην πέμπει κατὰ γαῖαν ἅπασαν,
lines.en: those that send life‑destroying ruin over the whole earth,
lines.note: Neuter plural hossa takes a singular verb (pémpei), standard in Greek; bio‑phthoriē (“life‑destroying [ruin]”) is abstract and collective.

lines.gr: ἔνδοξον βιοτῆς γλυκερ ὸν τέλος ἐσθλὸν ὀπάζοις.
lines.en: may you bestow a glorious, sweet, noble end of life.
lines.note: “Bestow” renders opazois; “noble” for esthlon preserves elevated register alongside “glorious” and “sweet.”

lines.gr: Λευκοθέην καλέω Καδμηΐδα, δαίμονα σεμνήν,
lines.en: I call upon Leukothea, the Kadmeian, august daimôn,
lines.note: “Kadmeian” marks Leukothea as Ino, daughter of Kadmos; “daimôn” retains the Greek term for a divine power lower than an Olympian.

lines.gr: εὐδύνατον, θρέπτειραν ἐϋστεφάνου Διονύσου.
lines.en: potent, nurse of well-crowned Dionysos.
lines.note: εὐδύνατος is taken as “potent, able to help” in hymnic usage; θρέπτειρα (“nurse, foster‑mother”) alludes to Ino’s care for Dionysos in myth.

lines.gr: κλῦθι, θεά πόντοιο βαθυστέρνοιο μέδουσα,
lines.en: Hear me, goddess who rules the deep‑bosomed sea,
lines.note: βαθυστέρνοιο (“deep‑bosomed”) is a conventional epic epithet for the sea; μέδουσα = “she who rules/guards.”

lines.gr: κύμασι τερπομένη, θνητῶν σώτειρα μεγίστη.
lines.en: delighting in the waves, greatest savior of mortals.
lines.note: No special difficulty; σωτεῖρα (fem.) rendered as “savior.”

lines.gr: ἐν σοὶ γὰρ νηῶν πελαγοδρόμος ἄστατος ὁρμή,
lines.en: For in you is the sea‑running, inconstant impulse of ships,
lines.note: πελαγοδρόμος ὁρμή = “sea‑running impulse/drive”; ἄστατος “inconstant, unstable,” capturing the changeable venture of seafaring under her control.

lines.gr: μούνη δὲ θνητῶν οἰκτρὸν μόρον εἰν ἁλὶ λύεις,
lines.en: and you alone loosen mortals’ pitiable doom in the sea,
lines.note: λύειν (“loosen, undo”) conveys averting/relieving doom (μόρος) in shipwreck; hence “you alone undo the pitiable fate … in the sea.”

lines.gr: οἷς ἂν ἐφορμαίνουσα φίλη σωτήριος ἔλθοις.
lines.en: for whomsoever, roused to act, gracious one, you come as savior.
lines.note: ἐφορμαίνουσα = “being stirred/roused to set upon,” here “stirred to act”; φίλη is rendered “gracious one” in prayerful address.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, θεὰ δέσποινα, μόλοις ἐπαρωγὸς ἐοῦσα
lines.en: But come, goddess, lady, as a helper,
lines.note: δέσποινα is a title “lady/mistress,” not the separate Arcadian goddess Despoina; ἐπαρωγός = “helper, ally.”

lines.gr: νηυσὶν ἐπ’ εὐσέλμοις σωτήριος εὔφρονι βουλῇ,
lines.en: as savior with kindly counsel for well‑benched ships,
lines.note: εὐσέλμοις (“well‑benched”) is technical for oared ships; εὔφρονι βουλῇ = “with kindly/propitious counsel, intent.”

lines.gr: μύσταις ἐν πόντῳ ναυσίδρομον οὖρον ἄγουσα.
lines.en: bringing to the mystai on the sea a ship‑driving fair wind.
lines.note: ναυσίδρομον οὖρον is the stock phrase for a favorable wind that speeds ships; μύσται (“initiates”) reflects the Orphic cultic audience.

lines.gr: Σύντροφε βακχεχόροιο Διωνύσου πολυγηθοῦς,
lines.en: Companion of the Bacchic chorus of much‑rejoicing Dionysos,
lines.note: βακχεχόροιο = “of the Bacchic chorus/dance,” marking association with Dionysiac ritual; πολυγηθής “much‑rejoicing” is an epithet of Dionysos.

lines.gr: ὃς ναίεις πόντοιο βυθοὺς βαθυκύμονας ἁγνούς,
lines.en: who dwell in the holy, deep‑billowed depths of the sea,
lines.note: βαθυκύμονας “deep‑waved, deep‑billowed”; ἁγνούς “holy/pure” modifies the sea‑depths; ναίεις is 2nd sg. “you dwell.”

lines.gr: κικλήσκω σέ, Παλα ῖμον, ἐπ’ εὐϊέροις τελετ ῇσιν
lines.en: I summon you, Palaimon, at well‑hallowed initiations,
lines.note: τελεταί are initiatory rites (Orphic context). Orthography in the prompt shows artefacts: read Παλαῖμον; ἐπ’ εὐϊέροις τελεταῖσιν (“at well‑hallowed rites”). κικλήσκω is a formal ritual “I summon/call upon.”

lines.gr: ἐλθεῖνεὐμενέοντα, νέῳ γήθοντα προσώπῳ,
lines.en: to come propitious, rejoicing with a youthful countenance,
lines.note: εὐμενέοντα = “well‑disposed, propitious”; νέῳ … προσώπῳ evokes Palaimon’s youthful aspect (the deified child of Ino/Leukothea).

lines.gr: καὶ σώζειν μύστας κατά τε χθόνα καὶ κατὰ πόντον.
lines.en: and to save the initiates both over land and over the sea.
lines.note: μύστας = “initiates” (technical religious term); κατά with acc. (“over/throughout”) expresses protection both on land and sea.

lines.gr: ποντοπλάνοις γὰρ ἀεὶ ναυσὶ ν χειμ ῶνος ἐναργ ὴς
lines.en: for to sea‑wandering ships, whenever the storm shows itself clearly,
lines.note: ποντοπλάνοις ναυσίν “to sea‑wandering ships.” Read ναυσίν; χειμῶνος ἐναργὴς φαινομένου is a genitive absolute, “as the storm becomes manifest.” ἀεί “ever/always” underscores habitual aid.

lines.gr: φαινομένου σωτὴρ μοῦνος θνητο ῖς ἀναφαίνῃ,
lines.en: you reveal yourself the sole savior to mortals,
lines.note: Wordplay: φαινομένου (“appearing”) with ἀναφαίνῃ (“you reveal yourself”). σωτὴρ μοῦνος = “sole savior,” highlighting exclusivity of help.

lines.gr: ῥυόμενος μῆνιν χαλεπ ὴν κατὰ πόντιον οἶδμα.
lines.en: warding off the grievous wrath upon the sea‑swell.
lines.note: μῆνις (“wrath”) used of the stormy sea’s fury; ῥυόμενος with acc. here = “warding off/averting” rather than “rescuing [someone] from.” Read πόντιον οἶδμα = “sea‑swell.”

lines.gr: Μνημοσύνης καὶ Ζηνὸς ἐριγδούποιο θύγατρες,
lines.en: Daughters of Mnemosyne and loud‑thundering Zeus,
lines.note: ἐριγδούπος is a traditional epithet of Zeus meaning “loud‑thundering.”

lines.gr: Μοῦσαι Πιερίδες μεγαλώνυμοι, ἀγλαόφημοι,
lines.en: Mousai Pierides, great‑named, of radiant fame,
lines.note: Pierides = “those of Pieria,” i.e., Muses from Pieria; ἀγλαόφημοι “of shining/illustrious fame.”

lines.gr: θνητοῖς, οἷς κε παρῆτε, ποθεινόταται, πολύμορφοι,
lines.en: to mortals, whenever you are present, most longed‑for, many‑formed,
lines.note: κε with the optative (οἷς κε παρῆτε) conveys “whenever/if ever you are present”; πολύμορφοι = “many‑formed,” i.e., manifold in manifestations/arts.

lines.gr: πάσης παιδείης ἀρετὴν γεννῶσαι ἄμεμπτον·
lines.en: bringing to birth the blameless excellence of all education,
lines.note: παιδείη (paideia) is “education/culture”; ἀρετή here “excellence.”

lines.gr: θρέπτειραι ψυχῆς, διανοίας ὀρθοδότειραι,
lines.en: nourishers of the soul, bestowers of right counsel for thought,
lines.note: ὀρθοδότειραι is a rare compound, “bestowers of right/straight counsel”; διανοία = “thinking/understanding.”

lines.gr: καὶ νόου εὐδυνάτοιο καθηγήτειραι ἄνασσαι,
lines.en: and queens, guides of potent mind,
lines.note: καθηγήτειραι “female guides/leaders”; νόου εὐδυνάτοιο = “of potent/capable mind.”

lines.gr: αἳ τελετὰς θνητοῖς ἀνεδείξατε μυστιπολεύτους,
lines.en: who revealed to mortals rites attended by mystic processions,
lines.note: τελετάς are initiatory rites; μυστιπολεύτους is a rare compound, “served/performed by mystic processions (of initiates).”

lines.gr: Κλειώ τ’, Εὐτέρπη τε, Θάλειά τε, Μελπομένη τε,
lines.en: Kleio, and Euterpe, and Thaleia, and Melpomene,

lines.gr: Τερψιχόρη τ’, Ἐρατώ τε, Πολύμνιά τ’, Οὐρανίη τε,
lines.en: Terpsichore, and Erato, and Polymnia, and Ouraniê,
lines.note: Ouraniê is a transliteration of Οὐρανίη (often Latinized as Urania).

lines.gr: Καλλιόπῃ σὺν μητρὶ, μάλ’ εὐδύνάτοι θεαὶ ἁγναί.
lines.en: together with mother Kalliopê, most mighty holy goddesses.
lines.note: Καλλιόπῃ σὺν μητρὶ is commonly taken as “together with mother Kalliopê,” likely referring to Orpheus’ mother; note the tension with line 1, where Mnemosyne is the Muses’ mother—some have proposed emendations, but the transmitted text is defended as self‑referential.

lines.gr: ἀλλὰ μόλοιτε, θεαί, μύσταις, πολυποίκιλοι, ἁγναί,
lines.en: But come, goddesses, to the mystai, many‑patterned, holy,
lines.note: μύσταις = “initiates”; πολυποίκιλοι “many‑patterned/varied,” often of manifold skills or arts.

lines.gr: εὔκλειαν ζῆλόν τ’ ἐρατὸν πολύυμνον ἄγουσαι.
lines.en: bringing fair fame and lovely, much‑hymned zeal.
lines.note: ζῆλος here is positive “zeal/emulation,” not jealousy; πολύυμνον “much‑hymned/oft‑praised.”

lines.gr: Μνημοσύνην καλέω, Ζηνὸς σύλλεκτρον, ἄνασσαν,
lines.en: I call upon Mnemosyne, bedfellow of Zeus, queen,
lines.note: σύλλεκτρον = “bedfellow/bedmate,” an intimate epithet; Ζηνός is the genitive of Zeus; ἄνασσαν = “queen.”

lines.gr: ἣ Μούσας τέκνωσ’ ἱεράς, ὁσίας, λιγυφώνους,
lines.en: who bore the Mousai, sacred, holy, clear-voiced,
lines.note: “Mousai” is kept as a theonym; ἱεράς, ὁσίας form a hendiadys “sacred, holy”; λιγυφώνους = “clear-/piercing‑voiced.”

lines.gr: ἐκτὸς ἔχουσα κάκης μνήμην βλαψίφρονος αἰεί,
lines.en: ever keeping outside the memory of baneful evil,
lines.note: ἐκτὸς ἔχουσα = “keeping outside/at bay”; βλαψίφρονος (baneful‑minded) qualifies κακῆς; rendering as “baneful evil” captures the force.

lines.gr: πάντα νόον συνέχουσα βροτῶν ψυχ ῇσι σύνοικον,
lines.en: holding together the mind of all, co‑dweller with the souls of mortals,
lines.note: πάντα νόον συνέχουσα = “holding together/sustaining all mind”; σύνοικον with ψυχῇσι (“with the souls”) is predicate “co‑dweller.”

lines.gr: εὐδύνατον κρατερὸν θνητῶ ν α ὔξουσα λογισμόν,
lines.en: augmenting in mortals a discernment that is capable and strong,
lines.note: εὐδύνατον = “effective/capable,” κρατερόν = “strong/steadfast,” both with λογισμόν (“discernment, reasoning”); αὔξουσα = “augmenting.” The spacing in the prompt reflects θνητῶν αὔξουσα.

lines.gr: ἡδυτάτη, φιλάγρυπνος, ὑπομνήσκουσά τε πάντα,
lines.en: sweetest one, lover of wakefulness, reminding of all things
lines.note: φιλάγρυπνος = “fond of wakefulness” (opp. to sleep/forgetfulness); ὑπομνήσκουσα = “reminding, calling to mind.”

lines.gr: ὧν ἂν ἕκαστος ἀεὶ στέρνοις γνώμην κατάθηται·
lines.en: that each one ever lays down as judgment in his breast;
lines.note: γνώμη = “judgment/resolve”; στέρνοις = “in the breast,” the seat of thought and decision.

lines.gr: οὔτι παρεκβαίνουσ’, ἐπεγείρουσα φρένα πᾶσιν.
lines.en: not straying from them, awakening the mind in all.
lines.note: οὔτι παρεκβαίνουσα = “not deviating/straying (from those judgments)”; φρένα = “mind/wits.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαιρα θεά, μύσταις μνήμην ἐπέγειρε
lines.en: But, blessed goddess, rouse in the mystai the memory
lines.note: μύσταις = “initiates” in mystery cult context; μάκαιρα θεά = “blessed goddess,” a standard cultic address; ἐπέγειρε = “rouse, stir up.”

lines.gr: εὐϊέρου τελετ ῆς, λήθην δ’ ἀπὸ τῶνδ’ ἀπόπεμπε.
lines.en: of the holy rite, and from them drive away forgetfulness.
lines.note: εὐϊέρου (euïerou) = “well‑hallowed/holy”; τελετή = “(initiatory) rite”; ἀπόπεμπε = “send away/banish”; τῶνδ’ refers to the mystai mentioned.

lines.gr: Κλῦθι, θεά θνητο ῖς φαεσίμβροτον ἦμαρ ἄγουσα,
lines.en: Hear, goddess, who bringest to mortals the light-bringing day,
lines.note: φαεσίμβροτον = “shining for mortals”; rendered idiomatically as “light-bringing.”

lines.gr: Ἠὼς λαμπροφαής, ἐρυθαινομένη κατὰ κόσ μον,
lines.en: Eos, bright-beaming, reddening the ordered world in due array,
lines.note: λαμπροφαής “bright-beaming”; ἐρυθαινομένη “reddening”; κατὰ κόσμον “in due order/array,” with possible cosmological nuance (“ordered world”).

lines.gr: ἀγγελίεια θεο ῦ μεγάλου Τιτ ῆνος ἀγαυο ῦ,
lines.en: tidings-bearing herald of the great god, the noble Titan,
lines.note: ἀγγελίεια = “tidings-bearing, heralding.” “the great god, the noble Titan” most likely refers to Helios (poetically styled a Titan) or his Titan sire Hyperion; translation leaves “Titan” unqualified.

lines.gr: ἣ νυκτὸς ζοφ όεντα κελαινόχρωτα πορείην
lines.en: who the murky, black-hued course of Night
lines.note: πορείην (for πορείαν/πορεῖαν) = “course, path”; ζοφοέντα and κελαινόχρωτα emphasize Night’s gloom and dark hue; capitalization of Night reflects personification (Nyx).

lines.gr: ἀντολίαις ταῖς σα ῖς πέμπεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα γαίης
lines.en: by your risings you send beneath the nether earth,
lines.note: ἀντολίαις = “risings” (of dawn/sun); νέρτερα γαίης = “the nether earth.”

lines.gr: ἔργων ἡγήτειρα, βίου πρόπολε θνητοῖσιν
lines.en: leader of works, life’s attendant for mortals,
lines.note: πρόπολος = “attendant, acolyte” (often cultic); paired with ἡγήτειρα “leader,” giving Eos both guiding and ministering roles for human activity (ἔργα).

lines.gr: ᾗ χαίρει θνητῶν μερόπων γένος οὐδέ τίς ἐστιν,
lines.en: at whose appearing the race of mortal men rejoices, and there is no one
lines.note: μερόπων = “articulate-speaking” (formulaic epithet of humans); ᾗ refers to Eos’s appearance/arrival (“at whose appearing”).

lines.gr: ὃς φεύγει τ ὴν σὴ ν ὄψιν καθυπέρτερον οὖσαν,
lines.en: who shuns your face, since it is overmastering,
lines.note: καθυπέρτερον = “quite superior, overmastering, irresistible,” qualifying ὄψιν (“face, presence”); hence “since it is overmastering.”

lines.gr: ἡνίκα τὸν γλυκὺ ν ὕπνον ἀπὸ βλεφάρων ἀποσείσ ῃς,
lines.en: whenever you shake sweet sleep from their eyelids,
lines.note: Subject is Eos; the understood object of “eyelids” is mortals’ (supplied as “their”).

lines.gr: πᾶς δὲ βροτὸς γήθει, π ᾶν ἑρπετὸν, ἄ λλά τε φῦ λα
lines.en: and every mortal rejoices, every creeping thing, and the other tribes
lines.note: ἑρπετόν = “creeping thing”; the line catalogs all living kinds responding to dawn.

lines.gr: τετραπόδων, πτηνῶν τε, καὶ εἰναλίων πολυεθνῶν
lines.en: of quadrupeds and of birds, and of the many-kind sea-dwellers,
lines.note: εἰναλίων πολυεθνῶν = “sea-dwelling of many kinds/tribes”; rendered as “many-kind sea-dwellers” to convey polyethnic diversity applied to marine life.

lines.gr: πάντα γὰρ ἐργάσιμον βίοτον θνητοῖσι πορίζεις.
lines.en: for you provide to mortals a life fit for work in all things.
lines.note: ἐργάσιμον βίοτον = “a life fit for work/productive livelihood.”

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαιρ’, ἁγνή, μύσταις ἱερ ὸν φάος α ὔξοις.
lines.en: But do you, blessed, pure one, increase the holy light for the mystai.
lines.note: αὔξοις is optative of wish (“may you increase”); μύσταις is transliterated “mystai,” denoting initiates; “holy light” suits the ritual register.

lines.gr: Οὐρανόπαιδ’ ἁ γν ὴν καλέω, Θέμιν εὐπατέρειαν,
lines.en: I call the holy child of Ouranos, Themis well‑fathered,
lines.note: The transmitted spacing ἁ γν ὴν = ἁγνήν (“holy”). Οὐρανόπαις = “child of Ouranos”; εὐπατέρειαν = “well‑fathered, of noble sire.”

lines.gr: Γαίης τὸ βλάστημα νέον, καλυκώπιδα κούρην,
lines.en: the young shoot of Gaia, the fair‑eyed maiden,
lines.note: καλυκώπιδα (lit. “bud‑eyed”) is a traditional epithet meaning “fair‑eyed.” βλάστημα νέον (“young shoot”) uses arboreal imagery for birth/offspring.

lines.gr: ἣ πρώτη κατέδειξε βροτοῖς μαντήιον ἁγνὸν
lines.en: who first revealed to mortals the holy oracle

lines.gr: Δελφικῷ ἐν κευθμῶνι, θεμιστεύουσα θεοῖσιν,
lines.en: in the Delphic recess, dispensing ordinances for the gods,
lines.note: θεμιστεύουσα = “dispensing themistes (divinely sanctioned ordinances/oracular judgments).” κευθμών = “hidden recess,” of the Delphic chasm.

lines.gr: Πυθίῳ ἐν δαπέδῳ, ὅ τε Πυθοῖ ἐμβασίλευεν·
lines.en: upon the Pythian ground, where he held kingship at Pytho;
lines.note: ὅ τε is often printed ὅτε (“where/when”); the implied subject of ἐμβασίλευεν is Phoibos (Apollo). “Pythian ground” refers to the Delphic precinct at Pytho.

lines.gr: ἣ καὶ Φοῖβον ἄνακτα θεμιστοσύνας ἐδίδαξεν.
lines.en: who also taught lord Phoibos the ways of themistes.
lines.note: θεμιστοσύνας is a rare abstract: “the practice/art of themistes”; hence the slightly technical rendering.

lines.gr: πάντιμ’, ἀγλαόμορφε, σεβάσμιε, νυκτιπόλευτε·
lines.en: All‑honoured, radiant in form, august, night‑roaming,

lines.gr: πρώτη γὰρ τελετὰς ἁγίας θνητοῖς ἀνέφηνας,
lines.en: for you first made known to mortals the holy rites,
lines.note: τελεταί = initiation rites/mysteries.

lines.gr: βακχιακὰς ἀνὰ νύκτας ἐπευάζουσα ἄνακτα ·
lines.en: lifting the Bacchic cry through the nights, invoking the lord;
lines.note: ἐπευάζουσα refers to the Bacchic cry (euai/euoi); the “lord” is Dionysos.

lines.gr: ἐκ σέο γὰρ τιμαὶ μακάρων μυστήριά θ’ ἁ γνά.
lines.en: for from you are the honors of the Blessed and the holy mysteries.
lines.note: μακάρων may denote the Blessed Gods or the blessed (initiates/the dead); the ambiguity is deliberate.

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαιρ’, ἔλθοις κεχαρημένη εὔφρονι βουλ ῇ
lines.en: But come, O blessed one, rejoicing, with kindly counsel,
lines.note: κεχαρημένη εὔφρονι βουλῇ is a conventional hymnic appeal for a deity’s gracious, kindly intent.

lines.gr: εὐϊέρους ἐπὶ μυστιπόλους τελετὰς σέο, κούρη.
lines.en: to your well‑hallowed, mystic‑ministered rites, maiden.
lines.note: εὐϊέρους (“well‑hallowed,” diaeresis marking hiatus); μυστιπόλους (“ministered/served by mystai,” i.e., initiates).

lines.gr: Χειμερίοις αὔρῃσι δον ῶν βαθ ὺν ἠέρα κόσμου,
lines.en: Shaking with wintry breezes the deep air of the cosmos,
lines.note: δονῶν = “shaking”; ἠήρ is the lower, misty “air” (contrasted with αἰθήρ in line 5). The odd spacing in the source (δον ῶν, βαθ ὺν) reflects typographical issues; the reading is δονῶν, βαθὺν.

lines.gr: κρυμοπαγὴς Βορέα, χιονώδεος ἔλθ’ ἀπὸ Θρ ῄκης·
lines.en: frost-fast Boreas, snowy one, come from Thrace;
lines.note: κρυμοπαγής = “frost-fast, frost-bound”; χιονώδεος = “snowy.” Boreas is traditionally linked with Thrace. The spacing Θρ ῄκης is a typographical artifact; read Θρῄκης.

lines.gr: λῦέ τε παννέφελον στάσιν ἠέρος ὑγροκελεύθου,
lines.en: and loosen the all-clouded stagnation of the moist-path’d air,
lines.note: παννέφελον στάσιν = “all-clouded stagnation,” i.e., a becalmed, overcast state. ὑγροκελεύθου (lit. “of moist paths”) is an Orphic compound applied to ἠήρ; I render it literally as “moist‑path’d” to suggest moisture-laden courses in the air.

lines.gr: ἰκμάσι ῥ ιπίζων νοτεραῖς ὀμβρηγενὲς ὕδωρ,
lines.en: fanning with damp exhalations the rain-born water,
lines.note: ῥιπίζων = “fanning.” ἰκμάς = “moisture, dew/exudation”; νοτερός = “wet, damp” (cf. Notos, the wet south wind). ὀμβρηγενές = “rain-born.” The sense is dispersing rainfall by gusts.

lines.gr: αἴθρια πάντα τιθείς, θαλερόμματον αἰθέρα τεύχων
lines.en: making all fair-weather, fashioning the aether bright-eyed,
lines.note: αἴθρια = “clear skies, fair weather.” θαλερόμματον (lit. “with a flourishing/abundant eye”) is a poetic epithet of the aether, here rendered “bright‑eyed” to convey luminosity.

lines.gr: ἀκτίσιν λάμπουσαν ἐπὶ χθον ὸς ἠελίο ιο.
lines.en: shining with the rays of Helios upon the earth.
lines.note: ἀκτίσιν … ἠελίοιο = “with the rays of Helios,” modifying “aether”; ἐπὶ χθονός = “upon the earth.” The spacing χθον ὸς ἠελίο ιο is typographical; read χθονὸς ἠελίοιο.

lines.gr: Αὖραι ποντογενεῖς Ζεφυριτίδες, ἠεροφο ῖτοι,
lines.en: Aurai, sea-born, Zephyritides, roving the air,
lines.note: The reading ἠεροφοῖτοι (“roving the air”) underlies the translation; “Zephyritides” marks them as maidens of Zephyros. Αὖραι are breeze-nymphs; ποντογενεῖς (“sea-born”) evokes sea-breezes.

lines.gr: ἡδύπνοοι ψιθυραί, θανάτου ἀνάπαυσιν ἔχουσαι,
lines.en: sweet-breathing whisperers, who bring respite from death,
lines.note: ψιθυραί (“whispering”) is a common epithet of soft winds; θανάτου ἀνάπαυσιν ἔχουσαι can mean “possessing/providing respite from death,” i.e., life-giving relief—hence “bring respite from death.”

lines.gr: εἰαριναί, λειμωνιάδες, πεποθημέναι ὅρμοις,
lines.en: vernal, meadow-dwelling, longed-for in harbors,
lines.note: λειμωνιάδες (“of the meadows”) casts the Aurai like nymphs; πεποθημέναι ὅρμοις means “longed-for in harbors,” i.e., desired by sailors.

lines.gr: σύρουσαι νηυσὶ ν τρυφερὸν πόρον, ἠ έρα κο ῦφον,
lines.en: drawing for ships a gentle passage, a light air,
lines.note: σύρουσαι (“drawing, towing along”) is used of currents/winds carrying ships; τρυφερὸν πόρον is a “gentle passage”; ἠέρα κοῦφον is “light air.” (The text shows spacing glitches: read νηυσίν, ἠέρα κοῦφον.)

lines.gr: ἔλθοιτ’ εὐμενέουσαι, ἐπιπνείουσαι ἀμεμφε ῖς,
lines.en: come in goodwill, breathing upon us blamelessly,
lines.note: ἔλθοιτ’ is an optative of wish typical of hymnic invocations (“come”); ἐπιπνείουσαι means “breathing/blowing upon,” and ἀμεμφεῖς “blamelessly” (adverbial).

lines.gr: ἠέριαι, ἀφανεῖς, κουφόπτεροι, ἠερόμορφοι.
lines.en: airy ones, unseen, light-winged, air-formed.
lines.note: A string of epithets stressing insubstantiality: ἠέριαι (“of the air”), ἀφανεῖς (“unseen”), κουφόπτεροι (“light-winged”), ἠερόμορφοι (“air-formed”).

lines.gr: Λαιψηρὸν πήδημα δι’ ἠ έρος ὑγροπόρευτον,
lines.en: A nimble bound through the mist, coursing along wet paths,
lines.note: The transmitted ἠ έρος is to be read ἠέρος (“mist, lower air”). ὑγροπόρευτον (“moist‑travelling”) is rare and poetical. The accusative phrase functions as an appositive epithet typical of hymnic style, describing the deity’s motion (likely a wind).

lines.gr: ὠκείαις πτερύγεσσι δονούμενον ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα,
lines.en: quivering to and fro with swift wings,
lines.note: δονούμενον suggests “shaken, made to tremble,” evoking the vibratory movement of wings; ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα = “hither and thither.”

lines.gr: ἔλθοις σὺν νεφέλαις νοτίαις, ὄμβροιο γενάρχα.
lines.en: may you come with the dewy clouds, begetter of the shower.
lines.note: νοτίαις = “dewy, moist.” γενάρχα (“begetter, origin”) is striking applied to weather; the addressee is likely a rain‑bringing Wind (e.g., Notos).

lines.gr: τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκ Διός ἐστι σέθεν γέρας ἠερόφοιτον,
lines.en: for this air‑roving office is your privilege from Zeus,
lines.note: γέρας ἠερόφοιτον = “air‑roving privilege/office,” with ἠερόφοιτος (“air‑haunting”) qualifying γέρας. ἐκ Διός indicates Zeus as the granter of this function.

lines.gr: ὀμβροτόκους νεφέλας ἐξ ἠέρος εἰς χθόνα πέμπειν.
lines.en: to send rain‑bearing clouds from the mist down to earth.
lines.note: ἐξ ἠέρος (“from the mist/air”). ὀμβροτόκους (“rain‑bearing”) modifies νεφέλας. The infinitive πέμπειν expresses the function tied to the granted γέρας and the prayer.

lines.gr: τοιγάρ τοι λιτόμεσθα, μάκαρ, ἱερο ῖσι χαρέντα
lines.en: therefore we beseech you, blessed one, pleased by holy rites,
lines.note: The spacing ἱερο ῖσι is to be read ἱεροῖσι (“holy rites/offerings”). χαρέντα (aorist participle) = “having been gladdened/propitiated.” λιτόμεσθα = “we beseech.”

lines.gr: πέμπειν καρποτρόφους ὄμβρους ἐπὶ μητέρα γαῖαν.
lines.en: to send fruit‑nurturing showers upon Mother Earth.
lines.note: καρποτρόφους = “nourishing crops/fruit” (lit. “fruit‑nurturing”). μητέρα γαῖαν is a traditional formulaic epithet, “Mother Earth.”

lines.gr: Ὠκεαν ὸν καλέω, πατέρ’ ἄ φθιτον, αἰὲν ἐόντα,
lines.en: I call upon Okeanos, the imperishable father, ever-existing,
lines.note: Reading Ὠκεανόν (not “Ὠκεαν ὸν”); πατέρ’ ἄφθιτον = “imperishable father.” The phrase αἰὲν ἐόντα is Homeric “ever-being.”

lines.gr: ἀθανάτων τε θεῶν γένεσιν θνητῶν τ’ ἀνθρώπων,
lines.en: origin of the immortal gods and of mortal men,
lines.note: “γένεσιν” = “origin/birth,” not merely physical begetting but cosmic source.

lines.gr: ὃς π ερικυμαίνει γαίης περιτέρμονα κύκλον·
lines.en: who surges around the earth’s bounding circle;
lines.note: περικυμαίνει “billows/surges around”; γαίης περιτέρμονα κύκλον = the outermost ring that bounds the earth in archaic cosmology.

lines.gr: ἐξ ο ὗπερ πάντες ποταμοὶ καὶ π ᾶσα θάλασσα,
lines.en: from whom indeed all rivers and the whole sea issue,
lines.note: ἐξ οὗπερ = “from whom indeed”; rivers and sea are conceived as issuing from Okeanos.

lines.gr: καὶ χθόνιοι γαίης πηγό ῤῥυτοι ἰ κμάδες ἁγναί.
lines.en: and the pure chthonian moistures of earth that flow from springs.
lines.note: χθόνιοι … ἱκμάδες = “chthonic moistures/saps”; πηγόρρυτοι “spring-flowing” (with double ρρ). “Moistures” avoids the overly physiological sense of “juices.”

lines.gr: κλῦθι, μάκαρ, πολύολβε, θεῶν ἅγνισμα μέγιστον,
lines.en: Hear, blessed and much-blest one, greatest purifier of the gods,
lines.note: κλῦθι = “hear [me]”; πολύολβε “much-blest.” θεῶν ἅγνισμα μέγιστον literally “the greatest hagnisma of the gods,” i.e., the greatest purifier/means of purification—water as ritual purifier.

lines.gr: τέρμα φίλον γαίης, ἀρχὴ πόλου, ὑγροκέλευθε,
lines.en: dear boundary of the earth, origin of the vault, you whose path is liquid,
lines.note: τέρμα φίλον γαίης “dear/beloved boundary of the earth”; ἀρχὴ πόλου “origin/principle of the vault/pole (the heavens).” ὑγροκέλευθε from ὑγρός “wet” + κέλευθος “path” = “whose path is liquid.”

lines.gr: ἔλθοις εὐμενέων μύσταις κεχαρισμένος αἰεί.
lines.en: come, always gracious, with good will to the initiates.
lines.note: εὐμενέων is best taken as a genitive of manner, “with good will”; hence “come … with good will to the initiates.” The closing formula is typical of the Orphic Hymns.

lines.gr: Ἱστίη εὐδυνάτοιο Κρόνου θύγατερ βασίλεια,
lines.en: Hestia, queen, daughter of mighty Kronos,
lines.note: "eudynatoio" literally "of goodly might"; rendered as "mighty". "Basileia" is a vocative epithet, “queen.”

lines.gr: ἣ μέσον ο ἶκον ἔχεις πυρ ὸς ἀενάοιο μεγίστου,
lines.en: who hold the middle of the house, the hearth of the great everlasting fire,
lines.note: "meson oikon" = the central place of the house, i.e., the hearth; "aenaoio" usually of water (“ever-flowing”), here applied to cosmic/eternal fire; I render "everlasting" to suit the context.

lines.gr: τούσδε σὺ ἐν τελετα ῖς ὁσίους μύστας ἀναδείξαις,
lines.en: in the rites do you declare these initiates holy,
lines.note: "anadeixais" is an optative of wish/prayer: “may you declare/reveal”; "teletai" are ritual rites, and "mystai" technical for initiates.

lines.gr: θεῖσ’ αἰειθαλέας, πολυόλβους, εὔφρονας, ἁγνούς ·
lines.en: making them ever-flourishing, much-blest, kindly-minded, pure.
lines.note: "theîs’" = contracted for θεῖσα (“having made”); the participle depends on the prayer: “declare … making them ….” Epithets retain their benedictive force.

lines.gr: οἶκε θεῶν μακάρων, θνητῶν στήριγμα κραταιόν.
lines.en: home of the blessed gods, strong support of mortals,
lines.note: "oike" is an appositional vocative noun (“home/house”), not a verb: Hestia is the home of gods and the firm support of mortals.

lines.gr: ἀϊδίη , πολύμορφε, ποθεινοτάτη, χλοόμορφε,
lines.en: everlasting, multiform, most longed-for, green-formed,
lines.note: The epithets are striking: "polymorphe" (“multiform”) and especially "chloomorphe" (“green-formed”) are unexpected for Hestia; some take them metaphorically (the ever-changing shapes of flame; ‘fresh’/life-giving power), and the line has been suspected of textual corruption by some editors.

lines.gr: μειδιόωσα, μάκαιρα, τάδ’ ἱερὰ δέξο προθύμως,
lines.en: smiling, blessed one, receive these sacred offerings willingly,
lines.note: "dexo prothymos" = “receive willingly/with ready will”; "hiera" are the sacred offerings or rites accompanying the hymn.

lines.gr: ὄλβον ἐπιπνείουσα καὶ ἠπιόχειρ’ ὑγίειαν.
lines.en: breathing forth prosperity and gentle-handed health.
lines.note: "epipneousa" literally “breathing/blowing upon,” a benedictive image; "epiocheir’" = “gentle-handed,” a rare epithet qualifying "hygieian" (health).

lines.gr: Ὕπνε, ἄναξ μακάρων πάντων, θνητῶν τ’ ἀνθρώπων,
lines.en: Hypnos, lord of all the blessed and of mortal humans,
lines.note: “the blessed” (makarōn) denotes the gods; the vocative Ὕπνε identifies the addressee as the deity Hypnos.

lines.gr: καὶ πάντων ζώων, ὁπόσα τρέφει εὐρε ῖα χθών ·
lines.en: and of all living creatures that the broad earth nourishes;
lines.note: “the broad earth” (eureia chthōn) is a traditional epic formula for the inhabited world and all its creatures.

lines.gr: πάντων γὰρ κρατέεις μοῦνος, καὶ π ᾶσι προσέρχῃ,
lines.en: for you alone hold sway over all, and you come to all,
lines.note: μοῦνος is the epic/poetic form of μόνος (“alone”); the line stresses Hypnos’s universal reach and authority.

lines.gr: σώματα δεσμεύων ἐν ἀχαλκεύτοισι πέδ ῃσιν.
lines.en: binding bodies in unfashioned, unforgeable fetters.
lines.note: ἀχαλκεύτοις πέδῃσιν literally “in fetters not wrought by the bronzesmith,” i.e., immaterial, unforgeable bonds—the metaphor for the power of sleep.

lines.gr: λυσιμέριμνε, κόπων ἡδεῖαν ἔχων ἀνάπαυσιν,
lines.en: care‑relieving one, who hold sweet repose from toils,
lines.note: λυσιμέριμνε is an epithet meaning “loosener of cares”; κόποι are physical/mental toils; ἡδεῖα ἀνάπαυσις is “sweet repose.”

lines.gr: καὶ πάσης λύπης ἱερὸν παραμύθιον ἔρδων ·
lines.en: and bringing a sacred consolation for every grief;
lines.note: ἔρδων is a ritual verb (“perform, accomplish”); παραμύθιον is “consolation/relief,” here sacralized by ἱερόν (“holy, sacred”).

lines.gr: καὶ θανάτου μελέτην ἐπάγεις, ψυχ ὰς διασώζων·
lines.en: and you induce a rehearsal of death, safeguarding souls;
lines.note: μελέτη θανάτου is “practice/rehearsal of death,” a phrase with philosophical resonance; διασώζων (“safeguarding”) reflects Orphic soteriological nuance about the soul (psychē).

lines.gr: αὐτοκασίγνητος γὰρ ἔφυς Λήθης Θανάτου τε.
lines.en: for you are by nature full brother of Lethe and of Thanatos.
lines.note: αὐτοκασίγνητος = “own/full brother”; Orphic genealogy associates Hypnos as twin to Thanatos and kin to Lethe (personified Forgetfulness).

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, λίτομαί σε κεκραμένον ἡδὺν ἱκάνειν,
lines.en: But, blessed one, I beseech you to come sweet and well‑tempered,
lines.note: κεκραμένον (“well‑mixed/tempered”) evokes the mixing of wine, here of sleep’s quality—gentle, moderated; ἱκάνειν = “to come, arrive.”

lines.gr: σώζοντ’ εὐμενέως μύστας θείοισιν ἐπ’ ἔργοις.
lines.en: graciously preserving the initiates in their divine rites.
lines.note: μύσται are “initiates”; θεῖα ἔργα (“divine works”) refers to ritual acts; σώζοντ’ is the elided participle (“saving/preserving”), modifying the addressee’s coming.

lines.gr: Κικλήσκω σε, μάκαρ, τανυσίπτερε, οὖλε Ὄνειρε,
lines.en: I summon you, blessed, long-winged—hail, Oneiros,
lines.note: οὖλε is a Homeric greeting (“hail!”); τανυσίπτερε = “long-winged,” a conventional epic epithet. Oneiros is the personified Dream.

lines.gr: ἄγγελε μελλόντων, θνητοῖς χρησμ ῳδὲ μέγιστε.
lines.en: herald of things to come, to mortals the greatest in oracle-song.
lines.note: χρησμῳδός (“oracle-singing”) is transferred to Oneiros: “greatest to mortals in oracle-song.”

lines.gr: ἡσυχί ῃ γὰρ ὕπνου γλυκεροῦ σιγηλ ὸς ἐπελθών
lines.en: for in the quiet of sweet sleep, coming silently,
lines.note: σιγηλός = “silent(ly)”; the participle ἐπελθών modifies “you.”

lines.gr: προσφωνῶν ψυχαῖς θνητῶν, νόον αὐτὸς ἐγείρεις,
lines.en: addressing the souls of mortals, you yourself awaken the mind,
lines.note: προσφωνῶν … ἐγείρεις: Dreams “address” souls and “rouse” the mind paradoxically in sleep.

lines.gr: καὶ γνώμας μακάρων αὐτὸς καθ’ ὕ πνους ὑποπέμπεις,
lines.en: and you yourself in sleep send down the counsels of the Blessed,
lines.note: γνώμας μακάρων = “counsels of the Blessed,” i.e., of the gods; ὑποπέμπεις “send down/secretly dispatch,” here “in sleep.”

lines.gr: σιγ ῶν σιγώσαις ψυχαῖς μέλλοντα προφαίνων,
lines.en: keeping silence, to silent souls revealing what is to come,
lines.note: Paronomasia: σιγῶν … σιγώσαις (“silent … to silent [souls]”); μέλλοντα = “things to come.”

lines.gr: οἷσιν ἐπ’ εὐσεβί ῃσι θεῶν νόος ἐσθλ ὸς ὁδεύει,
lines.en: for those upon whose pieties the good mind of the gods attends,
lines.note: ἐπ’ εὐσεβίῃσι (“by/through pieties”); νόος θεῶν ὁδεύει = “the gods’ good intent goes along/attends.”

lines.gr: ὡς ἂν ἀεὶ τὸ καλ ὸν μ ᾶλλον, γνώμ ῃσι προληφθέν,
lines.en: so that ever the good, foretaken in counsel,
lines.note: προληφθέν (“pre-apprehended/foretaken”) with γνώμαις (“counsels/intentions”) modifies τὸ καλόν (“the good”).

lines.gr: τερπωλαῖς ὑπάγῃ βίον ἀνθρώπων προχαρέντων,
lines.en: may lead the life of men, already gladdened, to delights,
lines.note: προχαρέντων (“already gladdened”) likely proleptic of the beneficiaries; τερπωλαί = “delights, enjoyments.”

lines.gr: τῶν δὲ κακῶ ν ἀνάπαυλαν, ὅπως θε ὸς αὐτὸς ἐνίσπ ῃ,
lines.en: and a respite from evils—how God himself declares—
lines.note: ὅπως … ἐνίσπῃ is parenthetical (“how God himself declares”); the content of “how” is completed in the next line.

lines.gr: εὐχωλαῖς θυσίαις τε χόλον λύσωσιν ἀνάκτων.
lines.en: that by prayers and sacrifices they may loosen the wrath of the Lords.
lines.note: εὐχωλαῖς θυσίαις = “with prayers and sacrifices”; ἀνάκτων (“of the Lords”) is a reverential plural for the gods; λύσωσιν = “they may loosen/appease.”

lines.gr: εὐσεβέσιν γὰρ ἀεὶ τὸ τέλος γλυκερώτερόν ἐστιν·
lines.en: for to the pious the end is ever sweeter;
lines.note: εὐσεβέσιν … τὸ τέλος: proverbial sentiment; “end” = outcome/lot.

lines.gr: τοῖς δὲ κακο ῖς οὔ κεν φαίνοι μέλλουσαν ἀνάγκην
lines.en: but to the wicked the dream-vision would not show the coming necessity,
lines.note: οὔ κεν φαίνοι (potential optative) = “would not show”; μέλλουσαν ἀνάγκην = “the necessity that is coming.”

lines.gr: ὄψις ὀνειρήεσσα, κακῶν ἐξάγγελος ἔργων,
lines.en: the dream-sight, announcer of evil deeds,
lines.note: ὄψις ὀνειρήεσσα = “dream-vision”; ἐξάγγελος = “announcer/herald” of deeds (here, evil).

lines.gr: ὄφρα κεν ε ὕρωνται λύσιν ἄλγεος ἐρχομένοιο.
lines.en: so that they might find release from the pain that is coming.
lines.note: ὄφρα κεν + optative expresses purpose/contingency: “so that they might find”; ἐρχομένοιο qualifies ἄλγεος (“coming pain”).

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, λίτομαί σε θεῶν μηνύματα φράζειν,
lines.en: But, blessed one, I beseech you to declare the messages of the gods,
lines.note: μηνύματα = “messages/revelations” (of the gods) to be conveyed by Oneiros.

lines.gr: ὡς ἂν ἀεὶ γνώμαις ὀρθα ῖς κατὰ πάντα πελάζ ῃς,
lines.en: so that you may ever draw near in all things with right counsels,
lines.note: πελάζῃς = “draw near, be at hand (to us)” with γνώμαις ὀρθαῖς (“right counsels/interpretations”).

lines.gr: μηδὲν’ ἐπ’ ἀλλοκότοισι κακῶν σημεῖα προφαίνων.
lines.en: revealing no evil signs in connection with strange portents.
lines.note: ἀλλοκότοις = “strange, anomalous, unnatural”; ἐπ’ ἀλλοκότοισι indicates the basis or occasion of the signs. The line prays for no dire omens drawn from bizarre portents.

lines.gr: Κλῦθί μευ, ὃς πάντων θνητῶν οἴηκα κρατύνεις,
lines.en: Hear me, you who hold the tiller of all mortals,
lines.note: οἴηκα is the epic accusative of οἶαξ “tiller”; a nautical metaphor for steering the lot of mortals.

lines.gr: πᾶσι διδοὺς χρόνον ἁγνόν, ὅσων πόῤῥωθεν ὑπάρχεις.
lines.en: granting to all a hallowed span of time, from whom you remain far away.
lines.note: χρόνον ἁγνόν “hallowed/pure time” likely means the allotted span untroubled by Death’s presence; ὅσων πόρρωθεν ὑπάρχεις “you are far away from them,” i.e., until their time arrives.

lines.gr: σὸς γὰρ ὕπνος ψυχὴν θραύει καὶ σώματος ὁλκόν,
lines.en: for your sleep shatters the soul and the body’s cable,
lines.note: σώματος ὁλκόν is difficult: ὅλκος can mean a “tow-rope/cable” (keeping the nautical image), or a “furrow/track”; here taken as “the body’s tether,” i.e., the bond linking soul and body; σὸς ὕπνος = Death’s “sleep.”

lines.gr: ἡνίκ’ ἂν ἐκλύῃς φύσεως κεκρατημένα δεσμὰ,
lines.en: whenever you loosen the bonds of nature that are held fast,
lines.note: κεκρατημένα “held fast/compacted”; the “bonds of nature” are the ties of body and soul which Death slackens.

lines.gr: τὸν μακρὸν ζῳοῖσι φέρων αἰώνιον ὕπνον,
lines.en: bringing to living beings the long, everlasting sleep,

lines.gr: κοινὸς μὲν πάντων, ἄδικος δ' ἐνίοισιν ὑπάρχων,
lines.en: common to all, yet unjust to some,
lines.note: Paradox of Death as universal yet “unjust” to some (premature death).

lines.gr: ἐν ταχυτῆτι βίου παύων νεοήλικας ἀκμάς.
lines.en: halting, in life’s swift course, the fresh heights of youth.
lines.note: νεοήλικας ἀκμάς literally “new-of-age peaks,” i.e., the fresh bloom/prime of youth; ἐν ταχυτῆτι βίου “in life’s swiftness.”

lines.gr: ἐν σοὶ γὰρ μούνῳ πάντων τὸ κριθὲν τελεοῦται ·
lines.en: For in you alone all that has been decided is brought to completion;
lines.note: τὸ κριθέν “what has been decided/decreed” (by Fate); τελεοῦται “brought to its telos (completion).”

lines.gr: οὔτε γὰρ εὐχῇσιν πείθῃ μόνος οὔτε λιταῖσιν.
lines.en: for you alone are persuaded neither by prayers nor by supplications.
lines.note: μόνος emphasizes “you alone are not swayed” by either εὐχαί (prayers) or λιταί (supplications).

lines.gr: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, μακροῖσι χρόνοις ζωῆς σε πελάζειν
lines.en: But, Blessed One, I ask to draw near to you only after long spans of life,
lines.note: πελάζειν “to approach” = to come near Death only after a long life; μάκαρ is a standard hymnic epithet even for chthonic powers.

lines.gr: αἰτοῦμαι, θυσίῃσι καὶ εὐχωλαῖς λιτανεύων,
lines.en: entreating with sacrifices and vowed prayers,
lines.note: εὐχωλαί are “vowed prayers”; λιτανεύων “beseeching, performing supplication.”

lines.gr: ὡς ἂν ἔοι γέρας ἐσθλὸν ἐν ἀνθρώποισι τὸ γῆρας.
lines.en: so that old age may be a noble privilege among humankind.
lines.note: γέρας “honor-gift, privilege”; wishing that γῆρας (old age) be a goodly boon rather than an early death.

lines.gr: Ἆρες ὑπερμενέτα, βρισάρματε, χρυσεοπήληξ,
lines.en: Ares, over-mighty, strong in the chariot, golden-helmed,
lines.note: ὑπερμενέτα “over-mighty”; βρισάρματε “mighty in/with the chariot”; χρυσεοπήληξ “golden-helmed.”

lines.gr: ὀβριμόθυμε, φέρασπι, πολισσόε, χαλκοκορυστά,
lines.en: fierce-hearted, shield-bearing, city-saving, bronze-cuirassed,
lines.note: πολισσόε (from πολισσόος) means “city-saving/preserving” (cf. σῶος); χαλκοκορυστά “bronze-cuirassed/bronze-armed.”

lines.gr: καρτερόχειρ, ἀμόγητε, δορισθενές, ἕρκος Ὀλύμπου,
lines.en: strong-handed, unwearied, strong with the spear, bulwark of Olympos,
lines.note: ἕρκος Ὀλύμπου “bulwark of Olympos” adapts the Homeric formula ἕρκος Ἀχαιῶν.

lines.gr: Νίκης εὐπολέμοιο πάτερ, συνάρωγε Θέμιστος,
lines.en: father of warlike Nike, co-helper of Themis,
lines.note: Νίκης εὐπολέμοιο = “warlike Nike” (εὐπολέμος “good in war” used as epithet); συνάρωγε Θέμιστος “co-helper/ally of Themis (Right/Justice).”

lines.gr: ἀντιβίοισι τύραννε, δικαιοτάτων ἀγὲ φωτῶν,
lines.en: sovereign in force-on-force encounters, leader of the most righteous men,
lines.note: ἀντιβίοισι “in force-on-force/hand-to-hand encounters.” The phrase δικαιοτάτων ἀγὲ φωτῶν is textually awkward; commonly taken as “leader of the most just men” (understanding ἀγέ < ἀγήτωρ by ellipsis), though some take ἄγε as the exclamatory particle “come!”; sense: Ares as champion of the just.

lines.gr: ἠνορέης σκηπτοῦχε, πυραυγέα κύκλον ἑλίσσ ων
lines.en: scepter-bearer of valor, wheeling the fire-bright circle
lines.note: ἠνορέης σκηπτοῦχε “scepter-bearer of manly valor.” πυραυγέα κύκλον “fire-bright circle” refers to the celestial/planetary orb.

lines.gr: αἰθέρος ἑπταπόροις ἐνὶ τείρεσιν, ἔνθα σε πῶλοι
lines.en: of aither among the seven-tracked stars, where your steeds
lines.note: αἰθέρος ἑπταπόροις ἐνὶ τείρεσιν: “among the seven-tracked stars,” i.e., the seven planetary paths; τείρεα = stars/constellations.

lines.gr: ζαφλεγέες τριτάτης ὑπὲρ ἄντυγος αἰὲν ἔχουσιν·
lines.en: fiery, ever hold you above the third chariot-rim;
lines.note: τριτάτης ὑπὲρ ἄντυγος “above the third rim/orbit”: in the Chaldean order (Saturn–Jupiter–Mars–Sun–Venus–Mercury–Moon), Ares/Mars occupies the third sphere from the outermost; ἄντυξ “rim” metaphorically for an orbit.

lines.gr: κλῦθι, βροτῶν ἐπίκουρε, δοτὴρ εὐθαρσέος ἥβης,
lines.en: hear, helper of mortals, giver of stout-hearted youth,
lines.note: εὐθαρσέος ἥβης “bold/stout-hearted youth”; ἥβη denotes youthful vigor.

lines.gr: πρηῢ κατάστιλψον σέλας ὑψόθεν ἐς βιότητα
lines.en: gently shed down a radiance from on high upon our life
lines.note: κατάστιλψον (from κατα-στιλπ-) “cause to gleam down/send down shining”; πρηΰ “gently, mildly.”

lines.gr: ἡμετέρην, καὶ κάρτος ἀρήϊον, ὥς κε δυναίμην
lines.en: and warlike strength, so that I may be able

lines.gr: σεύεσθαι κακότητα πικρὴν ἀπ ̓ ἐμοῖο καρήνου,
lines.en: to drive bitter evil away from my own head,
lines.note: σεύεσθαι (mid.) “to drive/chase away”; καρήνου is epic for “head.”

lines.gr: καὶ ψυχῆς ἀπατηλὸν ὑπογνάμψαι φρεσὶν ὁρμήν,
lines.en: and to bend the soul’s deceitful impulse beneath my wits,
lines.note: ὑπογνάμψαι “to bend down/subdue”; φρένες = “wits/understanding.”

lines.gr: θυμοῦ τ' αὖ μένος ὀξὺ κατισχέμεν, ὅς μ ̓ ἐρέθῃσιν
lines.en: and to restrain as well the sharp might of the spirit that goads me
lines.note: θυμός and μένος both denote inner impulse/spirit; κατισχέμεν “to restrain, hold back”; ἐρέθῃσιν “provokes, stirs up.”

lines.gr: φυλόπιδος κρυερῆς ἐπιβαινέμεν. ἀλλὰ σὺ θάρσος
lines.en: to mount the chill din of battle; but you,
lines.note: φυλόπις “the din/clash of battle”; κρυερός “chilling, cold,” a standard martial epithet.

lines.gr: δός, μάκαρ, εἰρήνης τε μένειν ἐν ἀπήμοσι θεσμοῖς,
lines.en: grant, blessed one, to remain within the unharmed ordinances of peace,
lines.note: ἀπήμοσι θεσμοῖς “harmless/unharmed ordinances,” i.e., the safe, beneficent laws/conditions of peace.

lines.gr: δυσμενέων προφυγόντα μόθον, κῆράς τε βιαίας.
lines.en: having escaped the toil of enemies and violent fates.
lines.note: κῆρες “death-spirits/fates of death,” hence “violent fates” ≈ violent deaths; μόθος “toil/strife (of combat).

appendix.title: Ὀρφικὸς Ὕμνος εἰς Δία (Κοσμογονικός)
appendix.description: Zeus cosmogonic hymn - separate ancient text

lines.gr: Ζεὺς πρῶτος γένετο, Ζεὺς ὕστατος ἀργικέραυνος·
lines.en: Zeus came to be first; Zeus, the bright-thundered, last.
lines.note: ‘ἀργικέραυνος’ is the Homeric epithet “bright-/flashing-thundered.” ‘γένετο’ suggests cosmogenic becoming rather than simple birth.

lines.gr: Ζεὺς κεφαλή, Ζεὺς μέσσα· Διὸς δ’ ἐκ πάντα τέτυκται.
lines.en: Zeus is the head, Zeus the middle; from Zeus have all things been fashioned.
lines.note: ‘μέσσα’ = “middle/center.” ‘τέτυκται’ (perf. of τεύχω) implies the cosmos as something “fashioned/made” from Zeus.

lines.gr: Ζεὺς ἄρσην γένετο, Ζεὺς ἄμβροτος ἔπλετο νύμφη·
lines.en: Zeus became male; Zeus became the immortal nymph-bride.
lines.note: The line asserts Zeus’s androgyny. ‘νύμφη’ can mean “bride/young woman,” here “immortal nymph-bride.”

lines.gr: Ζεὺς πυθμὴν γαίης τε καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος·
lines.en: Zeus the foundation of Earth and of starry Heaven.
lines.note: ‘πυθμήν’ = “base/foundation.” Earth and starry heaven are structural elements of Zeus’s cosmic body.

lines.gr: Ζεὺς βασιλεύς, Ζεὺς αὐτὸς ἁπάντων ἀρχιγένεθλος· 5
lines.en: Zeus is king; Zeus himself the first-begetter of all.
lines.note: ‘ἀρχιγένεθλος’ is rare: “first-begetter,” “primogenitor,” i.e., the originating source of all births.

lines.gr: ἓν κράτος, εἷς δαίμων γένετο, μέγας ἀρχὸς ἁπάντων,
lines.en: One power, one daimon came to be, the great ruler of all.
lines.note: ‘δαίμων’ here = “divine power” or “numinous being,” not “demon.” The line stresses monism: one power/daimon as universal ruler.

lines.gr: ἓν δὲ δέμας βασίλειον, ἐν ὧι τάδε πάντα κυκλεῖται,
lines.en: And one royal body, in which all these are encompassed,
lines.note: ‘κυκλεῖται’ = “are encircled/are cycled/encompassed,” hinting at a cosmology in which elements revolve within Zeus’s single royal body.

lines.gr: πῦρ καὶ ὕδωρ καὶ γαῖα καὶ αἰθήρ, νύξ τε καὶ ἦμαρ,
lines.en: fire and water and earth and Aither, and Night and Day,

lines.gr: καὶ Μῆτις, πρῶτος γενέτωρ καὶ Ἔρως πολυτερπής·
lines.en: and Metis, the first begetter, and Eros much-delighting;
lines.note: ‘Μῆτις’ personifies “counsel/cunning.” ‘πρῶτος γενέτωρ’ (“first begetter”) is theologically charged; some take it to allude to Protogonos/Phanes, but here it is predicated in the list within Zeus; ‘Ἔρως πολυτερπής’ = “Eros much-delighting.”

lines.gr: πάντα γὰρ ἐν Ζηνὸς μεγάλωι τάδε σώματι κεῖται· 10
lines.en: for in the great body of Zeus all these things lie.

lines.gr: τοῦ δ ή τοι κεφαλὴ μὲν ἰδεῖν καὶ καλὰ πρόσωπα
lines.en: His head, indeed, to behold, and his beautiful faces—
lines.note: ‘πρόσωπα’ (plural “faces”) and the mapping of body parts to cosmic regions mark a hieratic, symbolic anatomy.

lines.gr: οὐρανὸς αἰγλήεις, ὃν χρύσεαι ἀμφὶς ἔθειραι
lines.en: the radiant sky, around which golden tresses
lines.note: Golden “tresses” (χρύσεαι ἔθειραι) of the sky are the rays/effulgence of the stars.

lines.gr: ἄστρων μαρμαρέων περικαλλέες ἠερέθονται,
lines.en: of the gleaming stars, most beautiful, stir and quiver,

lines.gr: ταύρεα δ’ ἀμφοτέρωθε δύο χρύσεια κέρατα,
lines.en: and on both sides two bull-like golden horns,
lines.note: The “bull-like horns” are often taken as the extremities of the horizon or celestial arcs; bovine imagery is traditional for luminaries.

lines.gr: ἀντολίη τε δύσις τε, θεῶν ὁδοὶ οὐρανιώνων, 15
lines.en: the East and the West, the roads of the heaven-dwelling gods,
lines.note: ‘ἀντολίη/δύσις’ = “east/rising” and “west/setting,” the paths of the sky-dwelling gods; continues the cosmographic mapping.

lines.gr: ὄμματα δ’ ἠέλιός τε καὶ ἀντιόωσα σελήνη·
lines.en: and the eyes are Helios and the counter-facing Selene;
lines.note: ‘ἀντιόωσα’ = “facing/counter-facing,” of Selene vis-à-vis Helios (opposition, phases).

lines.gr: νοῦς δέ ἀψευδὴς βασιλήϊος ἄφθιτος αἰθήρ,
lines.en: and the unerring royal mind is imperishable Aither,
lines.note: The identity of Zeus’s ‘mind’ with imperishable Aither reflects Orphic physics: aether as the pure, intelligent medium.

lines.gr: ὧι δή πάντα κλύει καὶ φράζεται· οὐδέ τίς ἐστιν
lines.en: with which indeed he hears all things and takes thought;

lines.gr: αὐδὴ οὔδ' ἐνοπὴ οὐδὲ κτύπος οὐδὲ μὲν ὄσσα,
lines.en: nor is there any voice nor shout nor crash nor rumor
lines.note: A rhetorical crescendo of sound terms (‘αὐδή/ἐνοπή/κτύπος/ὄσσα’) to deny anything can elude Zeus’s hearing.

lines.gr: ἣ λήθει Διὸς οὖας ὑπερμενέος Κρονίωνος. 20
lines.en: that escapes the ears of Zeus, the over-mighty Kronion.
lines.note: ‘Κρονίων’ = “son of Kronos” (Kronion). ‘ὑπερμενής’ = “over-mighty, exceedingly strong.”

lines.gr: ὧδε μὲν ἀθανάτην κεφαλὴν ἔχει ἠδὲ νόημα·
lines.en: Thus he has an immortal head and understanding;
lines.note: ‘νόημα’ = “understanding/intention/mind,” here paired with the immortal head in the cosmic anatomy.

lines.gr: σῶμα δέ οἱ περιφεγγές, ἀπείριτον, ἀστυφέλικτον,
lines.en: but his body is all-bright, boundless, city-smashing,
lines.note: ‘ἀστυφέλικτον’ literally “city-smashing,” an unusual epithet for a “body”; likely transferred from martial contexts to signify irresistible force; often noted as a difficulty.

lines.gr: ἄτρομον, ὀβριμόγυιον, ὑπερμενές ὧδε τέτυκται·
lines.en: fearless, strong-limbed, over-mighty—thus it is fashioned;
lines.note: ‘ὀβριμόγυιος’ = “strong-/mighty-limbed”; a cluster of epic strength epithets describes Zeus’s cosmic body.

lines.gr: ὦμοι μὲν καὶ στέρνα καὶ εὐρέα νῶτα θεοῖο
lines.en: the shoulders and chest and the broad back of the god

lines.gr: ἀὴρ εὐρυβίης, πτέρυγες δέ οἱ ἐξεφύοντο, 25
lines.en: are the Air of wide might, and wings sprang forth for him,
lines.note: ‘πτέρυγες’ (“wings”) are symbolic of the airy medium enabling Zeus’s omnipresence.

lines.gr: τῆις ἐπὶ πάντα ποτᾶθ’, ἱερὴ δέ οἱ ἔπλετο νηδύς
lines.en: with which he flies everywhere; and sacred became his womb,
lines.note: ‘νηδύς’ can mean “belly/womb”; the male god’s “womb” becoming Gaia underscores panentheistic containment.

lines.gr: γαῖά τε παμμήτωρ ὀρέων τ’ αἰπεινὰ κάρηνα·
lines.en: Gaia the all-mother and the lofty peaks of mountains;
lines.note: ‘παμμήτωρ’ = “all-mother,” a fixed epithet of Gaia.

lines.gr: μέσση δὲ ζώνη βαρυηχέος οἶδμα θαλάσσης
lines.en: and the middle belt is the deep-sounding swell of sea and main,
lines.note: ‘ζώνη’ (“belt/girdle”) for the encircling ocean; ‘βαρυήχεος’ = “deep-/heavy-sounding.”

lines.gr: καὶ πόντου· πυμάτη δὲ βάσις, χθονὸς ἔνδοθι ῥίζαι,
lines.en: and the lowest base, the roots within the earth,
lines.note: ‘πυμάτη’ = “furthest/lowest”; ‘ῥίζαι’ (“roots”) imagines the earth’s extremities as root-like supports.

lines.gr: Τάρταρά τ’ εὐρώεντα καὶ ἔσχατα πείρατα γαίης. 30
lines.en: and dank Tartaros and the furthest bounds of Gaia.
lines.note: ‘εὔρώεις’ = “dank/mouldy,” conventional for Tartaros; ‘ἔσχατα πείρατα’ = “furthest limits/edges.”

lines.gr: πάντα δ’ ἀποκρύψας αὖθις φάος ἐς πολυγηθὲς
lines.en: And having hidden all things, again into the much-gladdening light
lines.note: ‘πολυγηθές’ = “much-gladdening”; ‘ἀποκρύψας’ suggests Zeus’s re-absorption of all things within himself.

lines.gr: μέλλεν ἀπό κραδίης προφέρειν πάλι, θέσκελα ῥέζων.
lines.en: he was about to bring them forth anew from his heart, working wonders.
lines.note: Orphic theology: Zeus “was about to” re-emit all things from his heart; ‘θέσκελα ῥέζων’ = “working wonders,” the re-creation after cosmic ingathering.
